body:
[Line 429](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/4dcee2b14945a80276f1b30abd99088ed7009d9f/src/mavsdk/core/mavlink_command_sender.cpp#L440) of mavlink_commands.cpp,  is a check to see if particular parameter on the command long has been set using the contextural conversion of std::optional. If it has not been set, the the value is initialised to certain values depending on whether the auto pilot is ardupilot or not. 

It does appear that this check always returns true, regardless if the param has been set. This maybe due to the initialisation of the values in CommandLong to NAN. This will result in ardupilot autopilots throwing a SIGFPE and closing the connection. This may be the cause of some of the problems in #728 and elsewhere particularly when SITL is used. 

I'm not sure of the correct solution but perhaps not initialising those parameters is probably an option?

answer_comments.body:
Oh, I think this one is wrong actually:
https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/4dcee2b14945a80276f1b30abd99088ed7009d9f/src/mavsdk/core/system_impl.cpp#L515

It should be ~zero initialized~ default constructed.

Interesting, so for passthrough it's different... Well, given it's "raw passthrough" it's just up to the user. I would say it's best if you zero-initialize the struct before setting the rest of the values. Does that make sense?

I finally had a closer look at this. I can see where you're coming from. However, given it's a passthrough API, I would say that it's just up to the user to set all values to something that the flight stack can cope with. So, for PX4 that means filling the reserved values with NAN, and for ArduPilot it might have to be 0 in some (older AP versions?) cases as NAN will cause a fault. I'm reluctant to make this more complex than it is, unless you have a suggestion how this could easily be improved?

Closing, re-open if you still think this needs to be addressed and change.

comments.body: Aha, thanks for the note. Is this for all commands that are sent or just one specific one?

The Ardupilot failure comes from CommandLong. They try to convert it to a CommandInt for logging purposes and it is this that causes the fault. I comment out the conversion and I don't have problems. I also don't have commands logged though. 

Some of the values I have seen, particularly for param6 were uninitialised values e.g. 2.452.. e+38. In my code, I'm not initialising those values in the mavsdk::MavlinkPassthrough::CommandLong that I am using. 
This also faults during the systemImpl [sending of a command long](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/4dcee2b14945a80276f1b30abd99088ed7009d9f/src/mavsdk/core/system_impl.cpp#L512) for autopilot capabilities.

I would have expected the check on Line429 to initialise those values to the correct ones, but it doesn't appear to work.
 The Values for command types are not std::optional in the MavlinkPassthrough[ definitions](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/4dcee2b14945a80276f1b30abd99088ed7009d9f/src/mavsdk/plugins/mavlink_passthrough/include/plugins/mavlink_passthrough/mavlink_passthrough.h#L87) of CommandLong or CommandInt. In this case as params are not initialised as a std::optional its probably part of the reason the check in mavlink_commands.cpp fails.

Actually, maybe this is only an issue with the mavlink passthrough command long. I went back undid my changes to ardupilot and initialised those parameters. I haven't seen it fault on the std::optional CommandLong used in systemImpl, I think I got that wrong. 
So I'd say this is limited to mavlink_passthrough CommandLong, as they are not initialised as std::optional. This makes more sense.

Oh, I think this one is wrong actually:
https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/4dcee2b14945a80276f1b30abd99088ed7009d9f/src/mavsdk/core/system_impl.cpp#L515

It should be ~zero initialized~ default constructed.

what about the[ initialiser](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/4dcee2b14945a80276f1b30abd99088ed7009d9f/src/mavsdk/plugins/mavlink_passthrough/include/plugins/mavlink_passthrough/mavlink_passthrough.h#L87) for mavlink_passthrough::Command

Interesting, so for passthrough it's different... Well, given it's "raw passthrough" it's just up to the user. I would say it's best if you zero-initialize the struct before setting the rest of the values. Does that make sense?

Well they're not raw types to start with, ie. we are not interfacing with mavlink passthrough using mavlink_msg_command_long_t.
Its a new type defined in mavlink_passthrough, so I don't think the "raw passthrough" applies. It also, as far as I can tell, goes through the same code path and calls maybe_reserved() on its way out. I think a solution would be to typedef the mavlink_passthrough::CommandLong  definition to the one in [Mavlink Command Sender ](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/4dcee2b14945a80276f1b30abd99088ed7009d9f/src/mavsdk/core/mavlink_command_sender.h#L57).

Its up to you, but it would solve this issue for future, assuming that the command in mavlink passthrough uses the code path through the mavlink command sender.
If it doesn't use the same code path, then it is probably not worth worrying about.
You're right, let me have a closer look later.

I finally had a closer look at this. I can see where you're coming from. However, given it's a passthrough API, I would say that it's just up to the user to set all values to something that the flight stack can cope with. So, for PX4 that means filling the reserved values with NAN, and for ArduPilot it might have to be 0 in some (older AP versions?) cases as NAN will cause a fault. I'm reluctant to make this more complex than it is, unless you have a suggestion how this could easily be improved?

Closing, re-open if you still think this needs to be addressed and change.

title: Testing an 'Unsupported component' with sitl?
author: reedev
body:
First of all: I am learning about the discovery of components and I see that SystemImpl::add_new_component() is constantly called. Obviously, components are dynamically checked at runtime. Is that a right assumption?

Since I have an 'Unsupported component' from my setup Herelink/Pixhawk4/PX4 I would like to check if that is the reason why component discovery does not work as with sitl. Is there any way to do this in sitl?

answer_comments.body: @reedev this might help your debugging: https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/pull/1557

title: MAVSDK remote control hangs
author: MIKE9708
body:
Hi, i was trying to to use the MAVSDK python library to communicate with a drone in a  simulation ( the simulation is based on the PX4 repository using gazebo has a simulation tool ) hosted on a different machine. When i run the simulation and try :

``
drone = System()
await drone.connect(system_address="udp://ip_addr_of_target_machine:14540")
``

the script remains hanged, while on the simulation logs im able to see:

`INFO [mavlink] partner IP: ip_addr_of_MAVSDK_machine
`

Now looking on the [PX4 documentation](https://docs.px4.io/v1.12/en/simulation/) i read that there are a series of option in order to achieve what i want to do , i tried  **Enable UDP Broadcasting** , **Enable Streaming to Specific Address**,and   **Use MAVLink Router**, without being able to get any result.

Can anyone help me understand  if i am doing something wrong or the PX4 docu solution should be modified?
Thanks

title: MavlinkDirect does not receive some messages via serial
author: matt-at-spsa
body:
I think I have found a bug in MavlinkDirect. The following MAVLink messages are (almost never) received when sent via a serial port, and subscribed to by MavlinkDirect:

```
HEARTBEAT 
SYS_STATUS
POWER_STATUS
MEMINFO
NAV_CONTROLLER_OUTPUT
MISSION_CURRENT
GPS_RAW_INT
```
There may be others, but these are the missing messages I've found so far in my testing.

Tested with MAVSDK version 3.15, installed from `libmavsdk-dev_3.15.0_debian12_arm64.deb`

### Test Code

I have two different C++ scripts/files that I am using for this testing:

* [mavlink_message_listener.cpp](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/26691963/mavlink_message_listener.cpp) - uses `mavsdk.intercept_incoming_messages_async` to print out **every** MAVLink message on the device. This seems to work accurately as far as I can verify with QGroundControl/MissionPlanner. So I do trust this script, and it is actually heavily based on one of the mavsdk examples IIRC.
* [mavsdk_message_matrix.cpp](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/26691988/mavsdk_message_matrix.cpp) - Iterates through a hard-coded list of MAVLink messages from both `serial:///dev/ttyUSB0:115200` and `udpin://192.168.1.6:14550` using BOTH **MavlinkDirect** and **MavlinkPassthrough**, then compiles a table of the results, populating it based on whether each message was received from that source. Full disclosure, this is a ChatGPT-generated script that is based off more basic scripts manually written by me, where I looked at each message one at a time. The result from this script matches what I have seen with my own, non-AI-generated scripts. I just wrote this script for convenience and to help you replicate my findings quickly.

### Expected Result:

I expect to see that every message is received (i.e. the message callback is called) for each message tested, regardless of whether it was subscribed to by MavlinkDirect OR MavlinkPassthrough, and regardless of the port used.

I have used mavlink_message_listener.cpp to verify that each message IS being sent to each UDP/serial port. 

### Actual Result:
This is the last part of the terminal output from mavsdk_message_matrix.cpp. It shows that there are seven message types that are NOT received by MavlinkDirect, but only when sent via serial. 

```

answer_comments.body:
## Root Cause

After tracing through the code, the bug is in `LibmavReceiver` (the parser that feeds MavlinkDirect): it **only handles MAVLink v2** (`0xFD` magic byte). MAVLink v1 messages (`0xFE`) are silently skipped.

### How MavlinkDirect receives messages

When data arrives on a serial connection, MAVSDK runs two independent parsers on the same raw byte stream ([`serial_connection.cpp`](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/main/cpp/src/mavsdk/core/serial_connection.cpp#L322-L335)):

1. **Standard C library parser** (`MavlinkReceiver`) — feeds MavlinkPassthrough, `intercept_incoming_messages_async`, plugins, etc. Handles both MAVLink v1 and v2.
2. **libmav `BufferParser`** (`LibmavReceiver`) — feeds MavlinkDirect. **Only handles MAVLink v2.**

In [`BufferParser::parseMessage`](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/main/cpp/src/mavsdk/core/serial_connection.cpp), the scan literally is:

```cpp
while (start_pos < buffer_size && buffer[start_pos] != 0xFD) {
    start_pos++;  // skips 0xFE (MAVLink v1 start byte) without parsing it
}
```

Any v1 message bytes are consumed/skipped, and `nullopt` is returned — so MavlinkDirect never sees them.

### Why it works over UDP but not serial

When connecting via UDP through a GCS relay (QGC / Mission Planner), the GCS has typically negotiated MAVLink v2 with the autopilot, so all forwarded messages arrive as v2. Over a direct serial connection, ArduPilot sends many common messages as MAVLink v1 by default (HEARTBEAT, SYS_STATUS, GPS_RAW_INT, etc.). Those are exactly the ones missing.

The "sometimes works after power-on" behaviour is also consistent: if MAVSDK starts sending v2 heartbeats quickly enough, ArduPilot may switch those streams to v2 before the subscription is set up, making them visible for that session. After a power cycle, ArduPilot boots into v1 again.

The dialect question (MEMINFO in ardupilotmega.xml) is a red herring — the ardupilotmega XML *is* loaded, but that doesn't matter because the message is sent as v1 and the BufferParser never reaches the definition lookup.

### Fix

The cleanest fix is to bridge messages parsed by the standard C library into the libmav handler chain. Since the C library already handles v1+v2, every successfully parsed `mavlink_message_t` can be converted to a `Mavsdk::MavlinkMessage` (via the libmav MessageSet for field names and JSON serialization) and dispatched to `receive_libmav_message`. The independent libmav raw-stream parser could then be kept as a fallback only for custom messages loaded via `MavlinkDirect::load_custom_xml` that the C library doesn't know.

Alternatively, `BufferParser` could be extended to support MAVLink v1 (`0xFE`), but that requires converting the v1 wire format, and the C library approach is simpler and avoids duplication.
I hope my AI buddy is correct :). Thanks for the detailed issue.
In the meantime, you might be able to force Mavlink 2 to avoid the issue?
Feel free to try https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/releases/tag/v3.17.1.

fix: bump libmavlike to add MAVLink v1 support in BufferParser

comments.body:
My first though is whether this could have something to do with the MAVLink dialect? I see that you're looking for `MEMINFO` but that's only part of [ardupilotmega.xml](https://github.com/ArduPilot/mavlink/blob/master/message_definitions/v1.0/ardupilotmega.xml#L1409), which actually should be included...

I will have to do some debugging, thanks for the issue anyway.

## Root Cause

After tracing through the code, the bug is in `LibmavReceiver` (the parser that feeds MavlinkDirect): it **only handles MAVLink v2** (`0xFD` magic byte). MAVLink v1 messages (`0xFE`) are silently skipped.

### How MavlinkDirect receives messages

When data arrives on a serial connection, MAVSDK runs two independent parsers on the same raw byte stream ([`serial_connection.cpp`](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/main/cpp/src/mavsdk/core/serial_connection.cpp#L322-L335)):

1. **Standard C library parser** (`MavlinkReceiver`) — feeds MavlinkPassthrough, `intercept_incoming_messages_async`, plugins, etc. Handles both MAVLink v1 and v2.
2. **libmav `BufferParser`** (`LibmavReceiver`) — feeds MavlinkDirect. **Only handles MAVLink v2.**

In [`BufferParser::parseMessage`](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/main/cpp/src/mavsdk/core/serial_connection.cpp), the scan literally is:

```cpp
while (start_pos < buffer_size && buffer[start_pos] != 0xFD) {
    start_pos++;  // skips 0xFE (MAVLink v1 start byte) without parsing it
}
```

Any v1 message bytes are consumed/skipped, and `nullopt` is returned — so MavlinkDirect never sees them.

### Why it works over UDP but not serial

When connecting via UDP through a GCS relay (QGC / Mission Planner), the GCS has typically negotiated MAVLink v2 with the autopilot, so all forwarded messages arrive as v2. Over a direct serial connection, ArduPilot sends many common messages as MAVLink v1 by default (HEARTBEAT, SYS_STATUS, GPS_RAW_INT, etc.). Those are exactly the ones missing.

The "sometimes works after power-on" behaviour is also consistent: if MAVSDK starts sending v2 heartbeats quickly enough, ArduPilot may switch those streams to v2 before the subscription is set up, making them visible for that session. After a power cycle, ArduPilot boots into v1 again.

The dialect question (MEMINFO in ardupilotmega.xml) is a red herring — the ardupilotmega XML *is* loaded, but that doesn't matter because the message is sent as v1 and the BufferParser never reaches the definition lookup.

### Fix

The cleanest fix is to bridge messages parsed by the standard C library into the libmav handler chain. Since the C library already handles v1+v2, every successfully parsed `mavlink_message_t` can be converted to a `Mavsdk::MavlinkMessage` (via the libmav MessageSet for field names and JSON serialization) and dispatched to `receive_libmav_message`. The independent libmav raw-stream parser could then be kept as a fallback only for custom messages loaded via `MavlinkDirect::load_custom_xml` that the C library doesn't know.

Alternatively, `BufferParser` could be extended to support MAVLink v1 (`0xFE`), but that requires converting the v1 wire format, and the C library approach is simpler and avoids duplication.

Wow, that was really really fast! I'm very glad I posted the issue here - I don't think I have all knowledge of QGC and MAVSDK required to identify this issue quickly (if at all, frankly). 

Thanks a lot for the quick fix @bansiesta!!
I hope my AI buddy is correct :). Thanks for the detailed issue.
In the meantime, you might be able to force Mavlink 2 to avoid the issue?

No problem!

I've just rolled back the core functionality I need to use `MavlinkPassthrough` for now. When I update to the next MAVSDK release I'll switch back to `MavlinkDirect` as I see `MavlinkPassthrough` is being depreciated.
Feel free to try https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/releases/tag/v3.17.1.

title: mavsdk_server crashes when a geofence is uploaded
author: JonasVautherin
body:
`mavsdk_server` gets a segmentation fault when uploading a geofence over gRPC.

Steps to reproduce:

1. Build `mavsdk_server` from #870.
2. Checkout MAVSDK-Python into the [python geofence PR](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK-Python/pull/114)
3. Run jmavsim and the `mavsdk_server` built in 1 above.
4. Run `examples/geofence.py` in MAVSDK-Python fetched in 2 above.
5. The geofence is uploaded successfully, but `mavsdk_server` crashes.

@coderkalyan: Would you mind having a look at this? :blush:.

answer_comments.body:
@coderkalyan I've been debugging that, and my observation is that the callback given to `send_geofence_async(...)` is called twice: once with result `Success`, and another time with result `Timeout` (which doesn't make sense to me if it succeeded before).

`mavsdk_server` crashes on the second call (with `Timeout`), because it expects the callback to be called exactly once.

Would you mind investigating why the timeout is called after a `Success` result is sent?

More specifically, the mission plugin unregisters the timeout on [`receive_command_result`](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/develop/src/plugins/mission/mission_impl.cpp#L1299-L1300), and maybe this mechanism is missing in the geofence plugin :thinking:.

It could be that it is something stupid in the geofence plugin with all the callbacks and locks happening there. I'm planning to refactor the mission and geofence plugin to clean these up, hopefully next week.
@coderkalyan good question. I would have to look into it and try it out.

title: Help: Multiple Connections via MavSdk_Server
author: endofpen
body:
Hi, 
i am trying to write a program in kotlin using the MavSdk Java Impl.

I want to archieve the following scenario.

Multiple drones (2 are fine to test the szenario) should connect to my program. Therefore i want to start seperate mavsdk_servers (current version 3.X.X) to connect to the drones 1 to 1.  Afterwards i connect in my kotlin program which uses java 11 (so i have to use Mavsdk Java client in version ~1.X.X) to the mavsdk servers to control the drones and to get telemetry data from them.

Is that a good approach or did i missunderstood something.

I am also struggling with the right setup to simulate this szenario. 
I am using px4 sitl on my wsl ubuntu instance. Is there a cleaner way to start 2 drones with diffrent ports and ips, so they can connect to the mavsdk_servers ? 

Sorry for that maybe easy question, but i am very new to this topic.

Greetings

answer_comments.body:
> i want to start seperate mavsdk_servers

Yes, that's how I've done it in the past!

I had multiple drones on the network, and I wrote a small proxy that was receiving MAVLink from them and then redirecting each stream to a separate port (based on the IP of the drone). My different instances of mavsdk_server were listening on those different ports, and voila!

> Starting the mavsdk_server like this:
> .\mavsdk_server_win_x86.exe udpout://172.20.116.189:14580 -p 50041

Oh actually you could do that too: have each mavsdk_server instance filter for the IP of the drone it wants. But I think you want `udpin`, then? Not sure (I haven't used `udpin` and `udpout` in a while, I may have them inverted 🤔)

> should i use the same versions ?

You should use the corresponding versions. Latest versions match, so mavsdk-java 3.10.1 corresponds to mavsdk_server 3.10.1. In the past it was not like this, so you'd have to check which version of mavsdk_server was pulled by the mavsdk-java you're using.

title: Discrepancy between Documentation and Example
author: RizzwareEngineer
body:
I have the following basic `CMakeLists.txt` for my C++ code that makes use of the Telemetry API.

<details>
  <summary>CMakeLists.txt</summary>

```cpp

cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 3.15)
project(telemetry-stream)

# Set the C++ standard
set(CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD 17)
set(CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD_REQUIRED ON)

# Enable strict handling of warnings
add_definitions("-Wall -Wextra -Werror")

# Find MAVSDK package
find_package(MAVSDK REQUIRED)

# Add executable target with source files
add_executable(telemetry-stream main.cpp)

# Link MAVSDK library
target_link_libraries(telemetry-stream
  MAVSDK::mavsdk
)
```

</details>

<details>
  <summary>Output</summary>

```
-- Configuring done (0.1s) CMake Error at CMakeLists.txt:18 (target_link_libraries): Target "telemetry-stream" links to:
MAVSDK::mavsdk_telemetry
but the target was not found. Possible reasons include:

* There is a typo in the target name.
* A find_package call is missing for an IMPORTED target.
* An ALIAS target is missing.
-- Generating done (0.0s)
CMake Generate step failed. Build files cannot be regenerated correctly.
```

</details>


According to [this documentation](https://mavsdk.mavlink.io/main/en/cpp/guide/telemetry.html), `MAVSDK::mavsdk_telemetry` is needed within the `target_link_libraries` call.

However, this [following example's](https://mavsdk.mavlink.io/main/en/cpp/examples/takeoff_and_land.html) source code which makes use of Telemetry does **_NOT_** include `MAVSDK::mavsdk_telemetry` within the `target_link_libraries` call.

If I delete `MAVSDK::mavsdk_telemetry`, I am able to build and execute. 

However, I wanted to ask: why there is a discrepancy between the documentation and the example, and which I should follow?

answer_comments.body:
With recent versions of MAVSDK, you only need `MAVSDK::mavsdk`. It appears that the documentation is outdated here.

Would you be willing to open a PR and correct the documentation? That would be highly appreciated :upside_down_face:.

It's here:
https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK-docs/blob/main/en/cpp/guide/telemetry.md?plain=1#L54-L65

We have this (unrelated but similar) `BUILD_STATIC_MAVSDK_SERVER` flag where we define `-static-libstdc++`. It appears in 3 CMakeLists.txt, including `src/mavsdk_server/test/CMakeLists.txt`.

Maybe you could try hardcoding your flags around that flag (not in the `if BUILD_STATIC_MAVSDK_SERVER` obviously, because by default this is not enabled, but put it close to it) and see if that helps?

Thanks for the suggestion, but I didn't really want to modify the internal CMake files of MAVSDK for CI/CD reasons. 
To still make it work, I ended up only building the `mavsdk` target and copying the library and headers manually. It now successfully links against my Unreal Engine project.

If anyone else has a similar use-case, this is the script I'm using to replace the `install` target:
https://gist.github.com/LarsLeferenz/11b05b8ff8e1255e9b6c29d21d044bfe

I can't guarantee that all plugins will link, as I only need `telemetry` for now.

> Thanks for the suggestion, but I didn't really want to modify the internal CMake files of MAVSDK for CI/CD reasons.

I was mostly asking in an informative way: would be nice to know what it takes to make it work.

Ran into the same issue when integrating MAVSDK with unreal on ubuntu 22.

For me, on Unreal 5.5, this worked for me:

1. Add these flags on top of CMakeLists.txt (obviously change the path of these to be the path of your unreal engine c++ stuff, right now the paths are set to mine)

```
set(CMAKE_C_COMPILER "/home/john/repos/Linux_Unreal_Engine_5.5.0/Engine/Extras/ThirdPartyNotUE/SDKs/HostLinux/Linux_x64/v23_clang-18.1.0-rockylinux8/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/bin/clang")
set(CMAKE_CXX_COMPILER "/home/john/repos/Linux_Unreal_Engine_5.5.0/Engine/Extras/ThirdPartyNotUE/SDKs/HostLinux/Linux_x64/v23_clang-18.1.0-rockylinux8/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/bin/clang++")

# Disable system C++ standard library
set(CMAKE_CXX_FLAGS "${CMAKE_CXX_FLAGS} -nostdinc++")

# Use Unreal's libc++
set(UNREAL_LIBCXX_INCLUDE "/home/john/repos/Linux_Unreal_Engine_5.5.0/Engine/Source/ThirdParty/Unix/LibCxx/include/c++/v1")
set(UNREAL_LIBCXX_LIB "/home/john/repos/Linux_Unreal_Engine_5.5.0/Engine/Source/ThirdParty/Unix/LibCxx/lib/Unix/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu")

# Add libc++ includes manually
set(CMAKE_CXX_FLAGS "${CMAKE_CXX_FLAGS} -I${UNREAL_LIBCXX_INCLUDE}")
```

Note: there's probably some stuff not necessary that I added to cmake, was trying a bunch of things

2. Run command
`cmake -Bbuild/default -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DBUILD_SHARED_LIBS=ON BUILD_TESTING=OFF -S.
`

If build testing is on, the build will fail.

3. `cmake --build build/default/ -j14`

4. Now put the generated shared object and headers in your unreal project and link them like you normally would.

This dynamic linking works for me.

---


As a note, I tried using static linking by setting -DBUILD_SHARED_LIBS=OFF but first ran into linker errors with libstdc++ for many of the built third party libraries in MAVSDK (I fixed this by manually setting the same CMAKE options above for those other cmake files).

But even when fixing that, I always ran into the following error:
`0>ld.lld: Error  : undefined symbol: pthread_cond_clockwait
0>>>> referenced by mavsdk_impl.cpp`

Which appears to be caused by some incompatibility with MAVSDK and the glibc version unreal uses.

So, static linking doesn't seem to work for now. Will see what I can do (if it's worth the effort for me)

title: Trouble installing Python wrapper
author: joe-marrone
body:
Hello again, I have another issue.
The backend installed OK after some effort.  When installing the Python wrapper everything appeared to install OK. But when I tried to run the takeoff_and_landing script it threw this error:

```
joe@joe-VirtualBox:~/src/Firmware/DronecodeSDK-Python$ examples/takeoff_and_land.py
Traceback (most recent call last):
File "examples/takeoff_and_land.py", line 5, in 
from dronecode_sdk import connect as dronecode_sdk_connect
ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'dronecode_sdk'
```

What next?
Joe

PS.  I asked this same question in another thread that was closed, so it's probably best to create a new thread.
resolution_evidence: thread converges on a working answer

answer_comments.body:
Ok. So part of what you did before was to install `python3.6` and `pip3.6`. On your system, you should now have multiple versions of Python. `python` is some Python 2 (maybe 2.7?), `python3` is Python 3.X (maybe 3.5?), and `python3.6` is Python 3.6 (the one you just installed).

The script `run_protoc.sh` calls `python3` and `pip3`, because on more modern systems like Ubuntu 18.04, that would be fine. But on your Ubuntu 16.04, you need the script to explicitly call `python3.6` and `pip3.6`.

So you should open `run_protoc.sh`, and replace `python3` with `python3.6` everywhere. And also replace `pip3` with `pip3.6` everywhere. Then save your changes and run `run_protoc.sh`.

If you're using Gazebo, you can try to run it without graphics:
```
HEADLESS=1 make px4_sitl gazebo
```

If you haven't installed Gazebo yet, and have Docker, you can also try to run it directly from [this docker image](https://github.com/JonasVautherin/px4-gazebo-headless) (have a look at the documentation there).

I see. I guess you may want to try Gazebo (see Julian's comment above).

I'm closing this issue now, as the Python wrapper got installed.

@joe-marrone: Let me try to reproduce the setup on Ubuntu 16.04, I'll come back to you ASAP.

> Could it be that Python 3.6 broke something?

Make sure to re-install the requirements, and run `./other/tools/run_protoc.sh` again now that you have updated Python.

Below are the steps I followed for installing DronecodeSDK-Python on an Ubuntu 16.04 Docker container ([see the Dockerfile here](https://gist.github.com/JonasVautherin/0bdd08bf58a6f8022b7645b0a0415023)). Make sure to adapt those steps to your system if needed, and to read the output of those commands to make sure they don't fail.

1. Install prerequisites (in your case I believe you already have them):

```
$ apt install curl git software-properties-common
```

2. Clone the repository:
```
$ git clone https://github.com/dronecode/dronecodesdk-python --recursive <path/to/dronecodesdk_python>
```

3. Install Python 3.6:

```
$ add-apt-repository ppa:deadsnakes/ppa
$ apt update
$ apt install python3.6
```

Note that it won't replace `python` or `python3`, so `python3` will still point to `python3.5`. You can either change that (there are tutorials for this) or always call `python3.6` explicitly (which I do in these instructions).

4. I had to install pip3.6 manually:

```
$ curl https://bootstrap.pypa.io/get-pip.py | python3.6
```

5. Install `dcsdkgen`, needed to generate the Python SDK:

```
$ cd <path/to/dronecodesdk_python>/proto/pb_plugins
$ pip3.6 install -r requirements.txt
$ pip3.6 install -e .
```

6. Now we can generate the Python SDK:

Note the `sed` instruction below: it is replacing `python3` with `python3.6` in the generation script, because `python3` points to `python3.5` on Ubuntu 16.04, as mentioned above.

```
$ cd <path/to/dronecodesdk_python>
$ pip3.6 install -r requirements.txt -r requirements-dev.txt
$ sed -i 's/python3/python3.6/g' other/tools/run_protoc.sh
$ other/tools/run_protoc.sh
```

7. Finally, install the SDK:

```
$ cd <path/to/dronecodesdk_python>
$ pip3.6 install -e .
```

If everything goes right, you should be able to run the example, with:

```
$ python3.6 examples/takeoff_and_land.py
```

~/src/DronecodeSDK/DronecodeSDK-Python/dronecode_sdk/__plugins__ should not be empty. It means that `run_protoc.sh` failed.

Can you verify that the python calls in `run_protoc.sh` are `python3.6` (and not `python3`), and run `run_protoc.sh` again?

This is the `run_protoc.sh` file in my system.   I installed this several weeks ago when I started this thread.

Joe

`
#!/bin/bash
SCRIPT_DIR="$( cd "$( dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}" )" && pwd )"
WORK_DIR="${SCRIPT_DIR}/../../"
PROTO_DIR="${WORK_DIR}/proto"
GENERATED_DIR="${WORK_DIR}/dronecode_sdk/generated"
PLUGIN_DIR="${WORK_DIR}/dronecode_sdk/plugins"
PLUGIN_INIT="${PLUGIN_DIR}/__init__.py"
export TEMPLATE_PATH="${WORK_DIR}/other/templates/"

function generate {
    echo -e "# -*- coding: utf-8 -*-\n" > $PLUGIN_INIT

    for PROTO_FILE in `find ${PROTO_DIR} -name "*.proto" -type f`; do

        # Generate bindings for each file individually
        python3 -m grpc_tools.protoc -I${GENERATED_DIR} \
                                     --proto_path=$(dirname ${PROTO_FILE}) \
                                     --python_out=${GENERATED_DIR} \
                                     --grpc_python_out=${GENERATED_DIR} \
                                     ${PROTO_FILE}

        # For some reason the import is broken with Python3.5.x and works fine
        # with Python3.6.x, set an absolute path and everything is fine
        PROTO_IMPORT_NAME="$(basename -- ${PROTO_FILE%.*})_pb2"

        # We need to create the .original backup files, otherwise we're not compatible with
        # BSD sed.
        sed -i'.sedoriginal' -e "s/import ${PROTO_IMPORT_NAME}/from . import ${PROTO_IMPORT_NAME}/" \
            "${GENERATED_DIR}/${PROTO_IMPORT_NAME}_grpc.py"
        # Clean up the backup files.
        find ${GENERATED_DIR} -name '*.sedoriginal' -delete
        echo " -> [+] Generated protobuf and gRPC bindings for ${PROTO_IMPORT_NAME%_*}"

        # Generate plugin
        python3 -m grpc_tools.protoc -I$(dirname ${PROTO_FILE}) \
                                     --plugin=protoc-gen-custom=$(which dcsdkgen) \
                                     --custom_out=${PLUGIN_DIR} \
                                     --custom_opt=py \
                                     ${PROTO_FILE}

        WANTED_PLUGIN_NAME="$(echo ${PROTO_FILE} | sed "s#.*/\(.*\).proto#\1#g").py"
        # protoc generates java like filenames, we don't want that with python

        # @TODO: cleanup this script and figure out a way to make it cross-os friendly perhaps rewrite in python
        # capilalization as trivial as this needs a workaround for macos bash 3.2
        # this solution avoids using bash ^ substitution (from bash >4.0) and is using python 3 instead
        CAPITALIZED_PLUGIN_NAME=$(python3 -c "import sys;print(sys.argv[1].capitalize())" "$WANTED_PLUGIN_NAME")
        mv ${PLUGIN_DIR}/${CAPITALIZED_PLUGIN_NAME} ${PLUGIN_DIR}/${WANTED_PLUGIN_NAME}
        # Add to imports
        echo "from .${WANTED_PLUGIN_NAME%.py} import *" >> $PLUGIN_INIT
        echo " -> [+] Generated plugin for ${PROTO_IMPORT_NAME%_*}"

    done
}
function install_dcsdkgen {
    cd ${PROTO_DIR}/pb_plugins
    if [[ "$VIRTUAL_ENV" != "" ]]
    then
        pip3 install .
    else
        pip3  install --user .
    fi
}
echo "[+] Installing the DronecodeSDK autogenerator"
install_dcsdkgen
echo "[+] Done"
echo "[+] Generating plugins from "
generate
echo "[+] Done"
`

Ok. So part of what you did before was to install `python3.6` and `pip3.6`. On your system, you should now have multiple versions of Python. `python` is some Python 2 (maybe 2.7?), `python3` is Python 3.X (maybe 3.5?), and `python3.6` is Python 3.6 (the one you just installed).

The script `run_protoc.sh` calls `python3` and `pip3`, because on more modern systems like Ubuntu 18.04, that would be fine. But on your Ubuntu 16.04, you need the script to explicitly call `python3.6` and `pip3.6`.

So you should open `run_protoc.sh`, and replace `python3` with `python3.6` everywhere. And also replace `pip3` with `pip3.6` everywhere. Then save your changes and run `run_protoc.sh`.

It seems that my ubuntu 16.04 install does not like the graphics card on my PC because of incompatibilities with GNOME, so I am using the standard graphics shell from Microsoft, which does not run the sim.  Never a dull day!

@Ryanf55 sorry, I misunderstood that you wanted to do this and read it as you also wanted it. Feel free to make an implementation, feel free to take @bansiesta's as inspiration.

The example is already up at #2867 — it uses `intercept_incoming_messages_async()` to get raw `mavlink_message_t` structs (solving the parsed-vs-raw-bytes problem) and re-serialises them with `mavlink_msg_to_send_buffer()` before prepending the 8-byte big-endian µs timestamp. Did you consider how we will handle differentiating which interface packets were on?

Good question — the short answer is: the  spec has no per-packet interface field, so there's no clean way to embed that info in a single file.

A few options for multi-interface setups:

1. **Separate file per connection** — open one tlog writer per `MavlinkPassthrough` connection and name them after the interface (e.g. `udp_14550.tlog`, `serial_0.tlog`). This is probably the most practical approach and what tools like MAVProxy do when recording.
2. **STATUSTEXT marker packets** — inject a synthetic `MAVLINK_MSG_ID_STATUSTEXT` at the start of each interface's stream to label it. Hacky, but survives concatenation.
3. **Accept single-interface** — for the common case (one UDP link to a flight controller) the question doesn't arise, which is what the current example targets.

For the example in #2867, it uses a single connection and doesn't try to solve multi-interface. If determining per-interface origin matters for your router validation use case, option 1 (separate files) would be the most reliable. Happy to extend the example to support that if it would be useful.

comments.body: Do you use futures/promises in your code? Or is this happening in the MAVSDK side?

I do not use any futures in my code. I used a future in the system discovery before (like in the example) but I replaced it with busy waiting to narrow down the problem. 
So it must be on MAVSDK side as I could not imagine any side-effects with ROS2. 
It happens always when the result of `telemetry_->set_rate_battery()` is not success.
I have had this happen too when using the sync functions. It seems to be related to retrying commands

I did some further testing and figured out, that the result is `CommandDenied`before the error occurs. I can't say if the behavior is unique to this result though. 
I am currently testing it in SITL but it also happens when connected to a flight controller. 
To reproduce the described behavior I have a disarmed copter in SITL and restart the software until I get the error. It takes approximately 20 restarts until the error occurs - sometimes even more.
I have seen this happen in CI tests recently as well. Could not track it down yet.

After some investigating I tracked the error down to: https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/f4987b17a0f766969efb2593e28d57c2c46c000e/src/core/mavlink_commands.cpp#L48-L56 It seems as the first result is a ```CommandDenied``` as mentioned above. However, just a moment later another result of the type ```Success``` is provided. This leads to ```std::future_error: Promise already satisfied```.  During further investigating I found this LogWarn Message in a comment in the ```do_work()``` function, which handles the ```_work_queue```: https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/f4987b17a0f766969efb2593e28d57c2c46c000e/src/core/mavlink_commands.cpp#L290-L303
After uncommentating the Warning Message I discovered, that the Error always occurs after this Warning was sent. Makes sense, as a the result is set to ```CommandDenied``` in the same if-statement.

After also uncommenting https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/f4987b17a0f766969efb2593e28d57c2c46c000e/src/core/mavlink_commands.cpp#L99-L100 and https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/f4987b17a0f766969efb2593e28d57c2c46c000e/src/core/mavlink_commands.cpp#L280 one can see these Logging messages:
```
[11:31:25|Debug] Command 511 to send to 1, 1 (mavlink_commands.cpp:99)
[11:31:25|Debug] sending it the first time (511) (mavlink_commands.cpp:280)
[11:31:25|Debug] sending it the first time (511) (mavlink_commands.cpp:280)
[11:31:25|Warn ] A command cannot be sent if another command with the same command_id is still processing! Ignoring command 511 (mavlink_commands.cpp:291)
[11:31:25|Debug] sending it the first time (511) (mavlink_commands.cpp:280)
terminate called after throwing an instance of 'std::future_error'
what():  std::future_error: Promise already satisfied
```

In my opinion this is due to the fact, that ```do_work()``` realizes, that another command with the same ID exists and ignores it but why does it return ```CommandDenied```? Shouldn't it just skip and and during the next iteration (or whenever the previous command with the same ID is done) it takes care of this command?

I tried it by commenting out https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/f4987b17a0f766969efb2593e28d57c2c46c000e/src/core/mavlink_commands.cpp#L295-L300 and setting the rate worked consistently (at least for 100 consecutive tries). During these 100 tries the Warning due to another command with the same ID still being processed occured 8 times, which also leads to the question why this even happens in the first place.

It is expected that the second command receives a `CommandDenied` result. We don't want to retry it later, we delegate that to the user.

Now the thing is that there are two separate commands, and they should use two separate promises. Your bug suggests that maybe there is a confusion somewhere and that both results are sent to the same command :thinking:. Could it be?

> Now the thing is that there are two separate commands, and they should use two separate promises. Your bug suggests that maybe there is a confusion somewhere and that both results are sent to the same command thinking. Could it be?

That's an interesting thought.

@fas2037 do you have easy steps or a setup where it's easier to trigger this?

@JonasVautherin The rally point sequence is exactly the same as the [mission protocol](https://mavlink.io/en/services/mission.html) except that you need to specify a `mission_type` of `MAV_MISSION_TYPE_RALLY` (instead of `MAV_MISSION_TYPE_MISSION`) in most messages and the payload is always [MAV_CMD_NAV_RALLY_POINT](https://mavlink.io/en/messages/common.html#MAV_CMD_NAV_RALLY_POINT).

There is a protocol bit you can check for support: [MAV_PROTOCOL_CAPABILITY_MISSION_RALLY](https://mavlink.io/en/messages/common.html#MAV_PROTOCOL_CAPABILITY_MISSION_RALLY).

As to where it should go, the purist in me would like a separate plugin but the pragmatist says in mission plugin. 
- The pragmatist reasoning is that implementation-wise everything is the same, so it is easier development and maintenance. 
- The purist point of view is that conceptually a rally point and a mission are different things that apply in different ways. The fact they are the infrastructure in MAVLink and QGC treats them as part of the same "plan" is an incidental association.

mission // This is the actual mission plugin, with its own CMakeLists.txt creating libmavsdk_mission.so
rallypoint // This is the actual rallypoint plugin, with its own CMakeLists.txt creating libmavsdk_rallypoint.so
```

What do you guys think?

body:
Hello!

I would like to connect to the same PX4 sitl instance from multiple processes using an instance of _mavsdk::Mavsdk_.
When i add a udp connection with the option _ForwardingOn_, the terminal with the px4 sitl instance that i tried to connect to is flooded with the warning:
_WARN  [mavlink] ODOMETRY: estimator_type 8 unsupported_

The Mavsdk process also reports:
_MAVLink: critical: ODOMETRY: estimator_type 8 unsupported_

Any help would be much appreciated!
Kinds Regards!
resolution_evidence: thread converges on a working answer

answer_comments.body:
There is a difference between:

Listening on a port (on any network interface):
```
udp://:14530
```

Sending UDP to an IP and port:
```
udp://127.0.0.1:14530
```

Also see (https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/b87a21d9044b9385e570fe0dd3389b74a3d52c2d/src/mavsdk/core/include/mavsdk/mavsdk.h#L78-L81) (@JonasVautherin we need to fix this, people run into it again and again).

So, you need to change one of your two processes to:

```
ConnectionResult connection_result = mavsdk.add_any_connection("udp://:14530", ForwardingOption::ForwardingOn);
...
```

Glad I could help! By any chance, do both of your mavsdk instances have the same sysid, compid? I would try to set the configuration custom and vary it, so that you don't end up with conflicts, which is what these retries could be caused by.
242 would be a request for  [HOME_POSITION](https://mavlink.io/en/messages/common.html#HOME_POSITION).

If it's the former, you can use [MAVLink forwarding](https://mavsdk.mavlink.io/main/en/cpp/guide/connections.html#forwarding-mavlink-between-connections). And if it is the latter you should be able to just subscribe multiple times to a telemetry subscription.

Hello Julian,

yes, the followers would be separate MAVLink components running as own processes, e.g. on the follower-drones companion computer.
What i understood from the documentation is that port forwarding is used within the same program only?
When i try to connect to the same PX4 remote port (e.g. udp://:14540) from different processes with mavsdk::Mavsdk I always got a bind error:
`bind error: Address already in use (udp_connection.cpp:85)
Connection error: Bind error`

Sorry if Im slow on the uptake here,
Thanks again!

Oh, I see the confusion, no problem.

So what I mean is that you add two connections (or more) and you enable following between them. This means the messages are forwarded to another port, so that an additional MAVLink component (or MAVSDK process) can use it.

You can see an example here:
https://github.com/julianoes/siyi-a8-mini-camera-manager/blob/main/camera-manager/camera_manager.cpp#L73-L83

And to prevent bind errors, you will have to use different ports.

There is a difference between:

Listening on a port (on any network interface):
```
udp://:14530
```

Sending UDP to an IP and port:
```
udp://127.0.0.1:14530
```

Also see (https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/b87a21d9044b9385e570fe0dd3389b74a3d52c2d/src/mavsdk/core/include/mavsdk/mavsdk.h#L78-L81) (@JonasVautherin we need to fix this, people run into it again and again).

So, you need to change one of your two processes to:

```
ConnectionResult connection_result = mavsdk.add_any_connection("udp://:14530", ForwardingOption::ForwardingOn);
...
```

My bad, it is described very well [here](https://mavsdk.mavlink.io/main/en/cpp/guide/connections.html#behave-like-a-client) in the docs.
What i did now was on the forwarding process:
```
mavsdk.add_any_connection("udp://127.0.0.1:14530", ForwardingOption::ForwardingOn);
mavsdk.add_any_connection("udp://:14540", ForwardingOption::ForwardingOn);
```
for a bidirectional connection and on the subscribing process:
```
mavsdk.add_any_connection("udp://:14530", ForwardingOption::ForwardingOff);
```
So the system discovery is forwarded to the other process succesfully.
On the subscribing process however i got errors and warnings looking like this:
```
[02:57:07|Error] Retrying failed (520) (mavlink_command_sender.cpp:344)
[02:57:08|Error] Retrying failed (512) (mavlink_command_sender.cpp:344)
.
.
.
[02:58:52|Warn ] sending again after 0.509955 s, retries to do: 3  (512). (mavlink_command_sender.cpp:317)
[02:58:52|Warn ] Request was for msg ID: 242 (mavlink_command_sender.cpp:323)
```

So maybe it is better to use ```mavsdk::TelemetryServer``` instead of forwarding the entire mavlink traffic of one system just to create a Telemetry Plugin in a different process?

I was able to get something good enough running for my purposes, so i would feel bad holding you back with this issue any more.
Thanks again for your help and patience!

Glad I could help! By any chance, do both of your mavsdk instances have the same sysid, compid? I would try to set the configuration custom and vary it, so that you don't end up with conflicts, which is what these retries could be caused by.

You're right, after i set ```system_id``` and ```component_id``` explicitly, it did fix the error on the forwarding side.
On the mavsdk instance that is handed the forwarded connection i still get errors for msg 242:

```
[01:44:22|Warn ] Request was for msg ID: 242 (mavlink_command_sender.cpp:323)
[01:44:22|Error] Retrying failed (512) (mavlink_command_sender.cpp:344)
```
So the subscriber to the forwarded connection is requested to send a [MAV_CMD_PREFLIGHT_SET_SENSOR_OFFSETS](https://mavlink.io/en/messages/common.html#MAV_CMD_PREFLIGHT_SET_SENSOR_OFFSETS), which it keeps failing to send?
Both Configuration Types are set to ```ComponentType::Custom```

In the mean time i set up a ```TelemetryServer``` instead and it is working without problems so far.
242 would be a request for  [HOME_POSITION](https://mavlink.io/en/messages/common.html#HOME_POSITION).
Closing this. Comment again if it's still unclear.
Yes, this can be closed. Sorry for the late reply and thank you again very much!

title: ArduPilot - Problem identified that may be causing the mission module to fail (fly_mission example)
author: trolledbypro
body:
Hello, I have found a possible cause of this issue of the mission module failing in ArduPilot. 
Using Wireshark, I analyzed the network traffic between my ArduPilot SITL (running inside a WSL2 Docker container that runs the latest ArduPilot Docker image) and the MAVSDK example (running inside WSL2 as I was having issues running it in Windows 10). My MAVSDK library and my fly_mission binary were built in _debug_ mode using CMake through CMake Tools in VSCode (using VSCode WSL Remote session).

Here is my terminal output:  
![image](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/assets/57928210/31595d2e-923d-4817-aeea-85eb264c2683)

There is a debug message saying the gimbal version is v1, and that the mission is unsupported.
Examining Wireshark, the last message sent before the MISSION_ACK message containing the MAV_MISSION_UNSUPPORTED payload was MAV_CMD_DO_MOUNT_CONFIGURE (204). 

When gimbal angles are defined in a mission_item, the gimbal version is verified: https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/fadfe22e7c053945107201e2638be9a7f8b8ee5c/src/mavsdk/plugins/mission/mission_impl.cpp#L460
We then use the version above and send a version specific message containing the gimbal configuration. Below, we see that the unsupported message is sent if the gimbal version is assumed to be v1, as is the case in my console output:
https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/fadfe22e7c053945107201e2638be9a7f8b8ee5c/src/mavsdk/plugins/mission/mission_impl.cpp#L1188-L1221

It appears that MAVSDK is not finding out the supported gimbal version. Gimbal v1 is deprecated in ArduPilot as of version 4.3. Wireshark shows that no GIMBAL_MANAGER_INFORMATION (280) messages were sent from the AP and no MAV_CMD_REQUEST_MESSAGE (512) message from MAVSDK requesting the gimbal version was sent. The GIMBAL_MANAGER_INFORMATION message is what the gimbal module uses to set the gimbal version.

I propose the following two solutions. I think the latter is more inclusive to more ArduPilot versions but the former could be implemented quicker:
- default to v2 if ArduPilot is detected
- send a request for GIMBAL_MANAGER_INFORMATION if ArduPilot is detected

What do you all think?

Just remove the detection and default to v2, and you can also remove the v1 implementation files. Really it shouldn't be very hard.

comments.body:
Thanks @trolledbypro for looking into this! :rocket: 

I think I would be in favour of a third version: drop gimbal v1 entirely and always assume v2. There are many problems with the detection anyway.

One that I learn here is that the `mission` module needs to know about the gimbal protocol, so either we need to duplicate the detection that [we already have in the `gimbal` module](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/main/src/mavsdk/plugins/gimbal/gimbal_impl.cpp#L58-L62), or we need the `mission` module to depend on the `gimbal` one somehow (which we have never done with any plugin before).

But on top of that, the detection we have in the `gimbal` module is fundamentally flawed (and the root cause is in the MAVLink design): MAVLink does not offer a mechanism to differentiate between a timeout and an unsupported message (many modules just ignore commands they don't support, and the MAVLink specs allow a broadcast command which require this behavior). So we can be sure that a drone supports Gimbal v2 when everything works ("yay I received a v2 message, I know it supports v2"), but we can never be sure that it does not support v2 ("I did not receive a v2 message, is it because the drone does not support v2, or is it because the messages were lost?"). We could probably do more convoluted heuristics (like "I got 3 timeouts for the gimbal v2 requests while I received X messages from the drone, so I will say that I am reasonably confident that it was not a timeout"), but... well is it worth it?

I don't know of a single drone that uses Gimbal v1, and v2 has been out there for years. Maybe it is time to drop v1 entirely.

@julianoes what do you think?

![image](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/assets/57928210/092f3e29-bec1-4577-8fac-7296a6e025f8)

> Both the gimbal and mission modules experienced a gimbal mode timeout and defaulted to gimbal v1

Hmm, so the way we currently detect gimbal v2 is maybe not working with Ardupilot?

But that brings be back to my question above: no need to fix the detection for Ardupilot if we just default to v2 and drop v1 entirely. @julianoes what do you say?

@JonasVautherin I'll make a branch in my fork and get to work, should be doable for me (especially within 2 weeks)
Amazing, keep me posted!

I did more debugging, and setting up a gimbal on SITL allowed gimbal version 2 to be successfully detected (I am dumb and forgot the -M flag :( ). However, I still am getting a mission unsupported message even with gimbal version 2.
![image](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/assets/57928210/9217d52c-b9dd-4761-9ccd-e08b0d8b1c20)
It appears that gimbal being v1 was not the reason that the mission is failing.
Gimbal v2 sends MAV_CMD_DO_GIMBAL_MANAGER_CONFIGURE (1001) as a mission item. DO_GIMBAL_MANAGER_CONFIGURE has only recently been implemented in ArduPilot https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/pull/23737. This command is used here https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/e7657c2d87917df739186981f34f98a14c898893/src/mavsdk/plugins/mission/mission_impl.cpp#L1288-L1312 and is called here https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/e7657c2d87917df739186981f34f98a14c898893/src/mavsdk/plugins/mission/mission_impl.cpp#L459-L480
It looks like it has not yet been implemented to work as a mission item. This is something I maybe able to fix by adding the support into ArduPilot. I will discuss with the devs there.

These are two issues I made in ArduPilot that should make gimbal control work with MAVSDK (until I find new bugs):
https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/issues/24691
https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/issues/24691
ArduPilot has yet to implement acquiring and removing gimbal control as defined in gimbal v2 protocol, so my solution is to accept MAV_CMD_DO_GIMBAL_MANAGER_CONFIGURE as a mission_item and have it do nothing until gimbal control is implemented or I get the time to have it modify the gimbal control struct added by the ArduPilot PR mentioned in my previous comment (that is presently being unused). The MAV_CMD_IMAGE_STOP_CAPTURE is also not implemented, it looks like image handling with a photo interval is done differently in ArduPilot. I have also added that command as a do nothing command for now.

comments.body: In former case (above), Landing state was **NOT** received, but received in latter case.
@shakthi-prashanth-m hm, good observation, that's not optimal.

Possible solutions we talked about on the call:

1. Add `Action::is_armable()`.
2. Move landed/in-air state to core and get it in action plugin.
3. Cache last message received of each type and let action get the it to determine the state.
4. Do nothing, and just be aware that a plugin needs to be instantiated as early as possible.
Related to #65.

__EDIT: I changed my mind (see my comment below :P)__

I would vote for @julianoes 4th choice (do nothing) or another one: add a "state" callback in the Action plugin.

My reasoning is the following: 

1. `is_armable()` doesn't bring much, as it is another way to receive a negative `ActionResult` :-). When I want to arm, instead of calling `is_armable()`, I can always do `arm()` instead.
2. Keeping state there makes it more complex
3. Not sure I understand, but I think it also adds some caching in the action plugin, which means state and complexity

One use of `is_armable` that I can imagine on the user side is e.g. to enable a button in the UI. But instead of doing a `while (!is_armable())` in my code, as a user, I'd rather have a "state" callback in the action plugin (e.g. `registerIsArmable()`).

>1. Add Action::is_armable().

IMO, we can find a way to avoid adding an API if possible. If none makes sense, its last option.
>2. Move landed/in-air state to core and get it in action plugin.

We discussed that its better to remain in Action plugin. 

>3. Cache last message received of each type and let action get the it to determine the state.

This is interesting. Need to check.
>4. Do nothing, and just be aware that a plugin needs to be instantiated as early as possible.

Me @JonasVautherin had chat about it. I think, we can also add it in API description of `arm` that, when
it returns failure, retry after a second (like we do in case of `Telemetry::health_all_ok()`.)

I also think, we should add a note even in `Telemetry::health_all_ok()` about retry mechanism.

Actually, @julianoes just convinced me the opposite. Maybe `is_armable()` is good.

From my experience, before I started using streams (RxJava), I was really wanting to have blocking calls instead of callbacks. Then I moved to streams, and that was the opposite. Given that right now, we don't have streams in the core libs, I would vote for `is_armable()`.

Sorry for the confusion :D.
I vote for `is_armable()`.

> I vote for `is_armable()` 

OK, but can/should we correspondingly remove `health_all_ok()` as they effectively serve the same purpose.

@hamishwillee 
>The test there is telemetry->health_all_ok(). If that does not work, then either it needs to be:

[It did the work](https://github.com/dronecore/DroneCore/blob/e640114474a0cca738003cc207a5f29e89a2f824/plugins/telemetry/telemetry_impl.cpp#L436) by setting in-air status of the device.
But Action plugin will re-do the same work as it **can't** get in-air status from Telemetry plugin!

As we all know, Telemetry health check is done by all the examples (see below); so will be in all DroneCore applications ?
![telemetry_usage](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/26615772/36771013-bbed640a-1c73-11e8-818c-21b5a7756a9d.png)

I assume every application needs to perform health check before executing any business logic. If so, then we better move it to the core. Telemetry plugin may serve providing Telemetry info to applications. By moving it to the core, landing state issue will be resolved as well.
Makes sense ?

If it works as an `is_armable` check I don't really care where it lives because from a 3rd party app point of view you need Telemetry in most apps. I'm not sure you need to be able to do it before "arbitrary" business logic, but you do need it in this case.

I'm not completely convinced by the logic that it needs to be in core - unless you want to do that check before you allow an `arm()` command to be send (ie as part of our internal implementation).

How about blocking `Action::arm()` call for 1 sec (**only if landing state is unknown**) to receive landing status ? There's no harm in blocking for a _definite period of 1 sec_ even in async version; as this is a criteria for arming.
If so, we don't need `is_armable()` check, by doing health check as usual.

> How about `Action::arm()` call will be blocked for 1 sec

That's also an interesting idea. However, we then need to catch the case where we never receive the system state. So essentially we need to timeout.

I believe that sleeping one second in `arm()` solves a problem we don't have. When you `arm()`, there are many situations where you might receive a negative `ActionResult` (that's the point of the `ActionResult` in the first place, right?). So as a user, anyway you want to check the result and react accordingly.

What we don't have right now is the ability for the user to know that the drone is armable without calling `arm()` (because maybe I want to show an "arm" button on my UI, but I want it to be disabled when the drone is not ready. And actually in this case it is more a `is_initialized()` or `is_ready()` for the plugin, because we are only talking about the initialization time.

Telling people that they need the telemetry plugin in order to use the action plugin is a weird dependency to me. And again, we don't need the telemetry to `arm()` and receive the negative `ActionResult`.

Receiving an `ActionResult` that is not `SUCCESS` is not a bug, so there is no need for us to solve it :D.
@JonasVautherin I agree.

>Telling people that they need the telemetry plugin in order to use the action plugin is a weird dependency to me.

True. In that case, we should be able to replace `Telemetry::health_all_ok()` by `Action::is_armable()`.

Telemetry plugin is useful to get some info that can be shown in app. For eg. QGC shows Vehicle mode and Arming status:

I think it should be duplicated, that's a tradeoff when preventing dependencies.

title: Provided MAVLink headers are installed to the wrong directory
author: eastman-bechamo
body:
When supplying MAVLink C-header files and building from source, the build system installs the headers to a location that's not able to be found by `mavlink_include.h`.

Ubuntu 18.04 LTS
CMake v3.24.3

Configuration:
`cmake -B build/default -S . -DMAVLINK_DIALECT=all -DMAVLINK_HEADERS=../my_headers -H.`

Build and Install:
`sudo cmake --build build/default --target install -j8`

Resulting directory structure:
`/usr/local/include/mavsdk/plugins/mavlink_passthrough/**my_headers**/mavlink/v2.0/...`

Include line from `mavlink_passthrough/mavlink_include.h`:
`#include "mavlink/v2.0/all/mavlink.h`

---

To fix this, I edited `mavsdk/src/mavsdk/plugins/mavlink_passthrough/CMakeLists.txt`:
```
install(DIRECTORY
    ${MAVLINK_HEADERS} --> ${MAVLINK_HEADERS}/mavlink
    DESTINATION ${CMAKE_INSTALL_INCLUDEDIR}/mavsdk/plugins/mavlink_passthrough
)
```

---

Please let me know if I'm doing something incorrectly. If I'm not, please update that `install(...)` command in the next release. Thanks! :)

[This](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/main/src/mavsdk.pc.in) is what's being used to generate it. If I remember correctly, those variables are defined with `CMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX` and [GNUInstallDirs](https://cmake.org/cmake/help/v3.16/module/GNUInstallDirs.html).

I'm running typhoon_h480 or plane_cam from the Gazebo simulator and running the MavSDK camera.py.

answer_comments.body: When you take a picture from QGroundControl it just grabs a picture from the stream and saves it, as far as I remember.

> A camera is only sometimes discovered.

Hmm that's weird... I think it relies on the heartbeat, so would it mean that the camera heartbeat is unreliable? Just guessing here.

> I have no idea where the image is saved to?

It is not, it delegates that to you. What MAVSDK will give you is the URLs to access the pictures/video streams (see below).

> Another thing, how do I actually access the picture/ video frames from MAVSDK? 

When you take a picture, you receive a [`CaptureInfo` that contains a `file_url`](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK-Proto/blob/main/protos/camera/camera.proto#L314). If your drone exposes e.g. an HTTP server, that's the URL where you can get the picture. So you want to [`SubscribeCaptureInfo`](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK-Proto/blob/8966cf59029ac17d81654071ca6d3d27f0d8897d/protos/camera/camera.proto#L75) here, or [`ListPhotos`](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK-Proto/blob/8966cf59029ac17d81654071ca6d3d27f0d8897d/protos/camera/camera.proto#L59) to list all of them.

For the video stream, with the [`VideoStreamSettings` you get a `video_stream_uri`](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK-Proto/blob/main/protos/camera/camera.proto#L324). Typically that would be an `rtsp://` address that you can use to access the video. So you want to use [`SubscribeVideoStreamInfo`](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK-Proto/blob/main/protos/camera/camera.proto#L71) to get that.
I'm working on getting some of th camera/stream functionality developed. Stay tuned. Although for "server" plugins there is not a lot of support in languages other than X..

There has been lots of work around camera server.

There is also this example: https://github.com/julianoes/siyi-a8-mini-camera-manager

answer_comments.body:
So, the example works just fine on my Fedora Linux but stalls on macOS.

@hamishwillee when I ask latest latest, I mean: have you made sure that you have built and installed the latest?

Ok, after debugging this for several hours, I found that I had leftover library files in `/usr/local/lib/`.

Once I cleaned it up, did make clean, it all worked fine.

```
sudo rm -rf "/usr/local/lib/libdrone*"
make clean
make default
sudo make default install
(cd example/fly_mission && rm -rf build && mkdir build && (cd build && cmake .. && make && ./fly_mission udp://))
```

>  latest latest, I mean: have you made sure that you have built and installed the latest?

I would have said yes, but when I tried this again with a clean build, it is indeed working. I didn't have to delete "/usr/local/lib/libdrone*". 

I almost wish it hadn't worked so I would feel like I hadn't wasted your time. Sorry!

answer_comments.body:
Can you share the example, so I can reproduce it myself?

And maybe you can also share the stacktrace of all threads, in gdb it's `thread apply all bt`.

And you could also run it using `valgrind`, that sometimes tells you more.

Ok, I see the problem. You need to keep `Mavsdk` alive. You can put it in a `std::shared_ptr` or `std::unique_ptr`. In your current implementation it goes out of scope and is destructed.

Also see this comment:
https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/v2.12/src/mavsdk/core/include/mavsdk/mavsdk.h#L35-L36

It might not be the best wording. Probably should be something like:

```
 * An instance of this class must be created and kept alive in order to use the library.
 * The instance can be destroyed after use in order to break connections and release all resources.
```

title: Unsupported Mission Commands from QGroundcontrol created mission
author: ankitatcodingnebula
body:
Hi MAVSDK Team,

Any mission created from QGroundcontrol throws "UNSUPPORTED mission item" error for few of the MAVLink Commands (MAV_CMD). 
QGC mission creation adds the following MAV_CMD commands to the mission plan by default unless unchecked

1. MAV_CMD_NAV_TAKEOFF ([22](https://mavlink.io/en/messages/common.html#MAV_CMD_NAV_TAKEOFF) )
2. MAV_CMD_SET_CAMERA_MODE ([530](https://mavlink.io/en/messages/common.html#MAV_CMD_SET_CAMERA_MODE) )

When Download Mission api is called MAVSDK throws error which can be seen on mavsdk server console

```

[04:36:45|Debug] Assembling Message: 0 (mission_impl.cpp:612)
[04:36:45|Error] UNSUPPORTED mission item command (530) (mission_impl.cpp:743)
```

Looking at `DownloadMissionCallback` of `mission_impl.cpp` these commands are not part of the if else condition. Could you please confirm if there is a reason these have been left out? Is there any workaround to fix the UNSUPPORTED error on download mission?

answer_comments.body: I guess they should be added to the mavsdk mission plugin? Would you be willing to contribute that? :blush:

@ankitatcodingnebula thanks for the note.

First off: the mission plugin only supports a subset of commands. If you need all possible commands/mission items, you need to use the `MissionRaw` plugin instead.

Now, for your specific commands, I can see how it would be nice to have support for them:
1. MAV_CMD_NAV_TAKEOFF: there is work in progress to add support for this, see: #1628.
2. MAV_CMD_SET_CAMERA_ACTION: given we support taking photos and videos in CameraAction it would seem logical that we also implement/support switching between photo and video mode. It would be nice to add that capability. The first step would be to add it here: https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK-Proto/blob/0c4379fb476b41f5193de7cd602e24668c0fb268/protos/mission/mission.proto#L222.

The QGC import is now just done in MissionRaw, so we don't have all the compatibility.
Closing.

title: fly_qgc_mission issue: Mission int messages not supported
author: petergerten
body:
When trying to upload a QGC plan file via fly_qgc_mission I get the below error:

```
[07:50:24|Info ] MAVSDK version: 0.21.4 (mavsdk_impl.cpp:25)

Discovered system with UUID: 1
System ready
[07:50:25|Warn ] UNSUPPORTED mission item command (20) (mission_impl.cpp:1541)
Found 2 mission items in the given QGC plan.
Uploading mission...
[07:50:25|Warn ] Mission int messages not supported (mission_impl.cpp:366)
Mission upload failed: Error
```
What does "Mission int messages not supported" mean? (My mission is a trvial mission to fly to one waypoint created in QGC).

Is the "Mission upload failed: Error" due to the above warning or might be unrelated (as it is a warning and not an error)?
resolution_evidence: thread converges on a working answer

answer_comments.body:
Ok so here is what is happening:

1. The H520 sends heartbeats from the camera only at first.
2. MAVSDK does not send heartbeats back unless it manages to initialize an autopilot component which it doesn't see.
3. Once H520 camera receives a heartbeat it starts forwarding packets from the autopilot.

@petergerten a quick hack is to comment out this line:
https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/d9c09d238ed496a44cfe9b9213c240ab1d4b2cef/src/core/system_impl.cpp#L323

For the longer term, I want to refactor some of this discovery/connection logic and clean it up. It then should send out heartbeats even if only a camera and no autopilot has communicated yet.
@petergerten I doubt you correctly did the hack then. Did you make sure to rebuild the library and install it again? You will likely run into other problems with your hack.

Ok MAVSDK needs to receive the message [AUTOPILOT_VERSION](https://mavlink.io/en/messages/common.html#AUTOPILOT_VERSION) once because it needs to know about the `capabilities` flags.
One of those flags is [MAV_PROTOCOL_CAPABILITY_MISSION_INT](https://mavlink.io/en/messages/common.html#MAV_PROTOCOL_CAPABILITY_MISSION_INT).

This flag means that the vehicle supports the `_INT` version of the [mission protocol](https://mavlink.io/en/services/mission.html) which has better accuracy than the legacy one.

The fact that you get the `does_support_mission_int() = false` is because you have not received the `AUTOPILOT_VERION` message indicating the capabilities but does not actually mean that `_INT` messages are not allowed. Therefore, I've been trying to fix the problem of not receiving `AUTOPILOT_VERSION` instead of removing the check for mission int which is just a symptom but not the root cause!

title: Changing mode to GUIDED
author: ygratz
body:
Hi,

In some cases it did not takeoff. Now, I figured out that this was because the arducopter wasn't in GUIDED mode.
What can be the easiest way to command it to GUIDED mode ? 
At what class (Action, System,  ?) is that implemented.
Thanks

answer_comments.body:
[Here is](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/main/src/mavsdk/plugins/action/action_impl.cpp#L387) the ardupilot implementation of the takeoff. My understanding is that if it is not in GUIDED mode (which MAVSDK calls "offboard"), then it should set it to GUIDED and then takeoff.

Which version of MAVSDK are you using?

Oh, it is fixed in the main branch (which will become MAVSDK v2 at some point), but not in the v1.4.13 branch (which is the latest release): https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/v1.4.13/src/mavsdk/plugins/action/action_impl.cpp.

So you have two solutions:
1. Build MAVSDK from source from the main branch, so that you get the fix
2. Open a PR backporting the fix from main to the v1.4 branch, and then we could make a v1.4.14 release

I don't know how many similar fixes are in `main` and not in `v1.4` (apparently `v1.4` is currently 438 commits behind `main`: https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/tree/v1.4). If I was using Ardupilot, I would personally build MAVSDK from source to make sure I don't miss other similar fixes.

But that's your choice :blush:.

Hi Oliver, thanks for reporting the issue. Could you maybe try by changing the takeoff code in your local MAVSDK to switch to Stabilize flight mode instead of guided mode before takeoff? Please check it on SITL ;) Relevant code is here.

https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/48f1ad0325ecdcb8075d7ffd0cd7a8323af12fb3/src/mavsdk/plugins/action/action_impl.cpp#L387

Stabilize mode does not need position so should not create this particular issue:
https://ardupilot.org/copter/docs/stabilize-mode.html#stabilize-mode

What is your use-case? You would need position fix anyways before carrying out an auto mission right? In such a case waiting for a good fix before activating takeoff should be prudent. Or are you flying indoors?

Arducopter allows to takeoff in a selected number of flight modes out of which Guided was selected since MAVSDK is supposed to control the drone from such a mode. But I am open to discussing this further to find the best suitable mode for takeoff for most scenarios. Would also discuss this with the ArduPilot Dev team shortly.

title: Work to get v2.0 out the door

body:
I have been working on various refactoring and changes towards the next major revision. For visibility, let me list the remaining work that I would like to get done before shipping v2:

Required:

title: Dynamic plug-in infrastructure
author: shakthi-prashanth-m
body:
DroneCore has its functionality built with compile-time plug-ins such as `Action`, `Mission`, `Telemetry`, etc. When DroneCore is built, we can choose which plug-ins we're interested in. Build chooses plug-ins in `plugins` directory and generates `DevicePluginContainer` class and methods to access to the "choosen" plug-in objects. It is necessary to build DroneCore if we wanted to add a new plug-in to it.

We're interested to add new plug-ins which DroneCore will pick it up run-time. Theoretical approach for this is [here](https://px4.slack.com/archives/C68J8H32A/p1506435370000733).

However, as we're interested to developing language bindings using gRPC; gRPC requires `.proto` files for each of the plug-in to be known at compile-time.
We're yet to investigate the feasibility of both (gRPC & dynamic plug-in). 

Updates on this activity will posted here.

If you compile MAVSDK from source, you should run the corresponding examples. Say you compile MAVSDK from `main`, you should use the examples on `main`.

If you try to use the examples in `main` with an older version (e.g. v0.13), then it may fail because MAVSDK has evolved since then.

Does that make sense?

title: How to add "src/core" functions to example projects
author: felix-west
body:
I'm currently trying to add some functionality to my drone. To do that I first need to be able to give the drone different commands over the serial link. However, the functionality provided in the various plugins found in ".../MAVSDK/src/plugins/" is not enough for this. I found various pieces of code in the ".../MAVSDK/src/core/" directory.

answer_comments.body:
You are changing all over the place here and mixing internals of the library with externals. That's really not how this should be done and I don't know how to help you.

Can we take a step back and you can explain to me high level what you're actually trying to achieve and then maybe I can guide you how to do that?

Ok still sounds messy but I can somewhat get a glimpse. But all in all it sounds like you need some custom functionality.

Therefore, my suggestion would be to write your own custom plugin and put all the functionality in there. Then you can e.g. use the existing mission or mission_raw plugin for your missions but use your own plugin for your custom commands.

To create a new custom plugin you would copy an existing plugin folder and then change the filenames and class names etc to your custom plugin. Then you also need to add the plugin to the [CMakeLists.txt](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/develop/src/plugins/CMakeLists.txt) file so it gets compiled.

So what I'm saying is that you should extend the library (MAVSDK) itself from within and not try to add more functionality inside the example which is using the API from external. The way you started including random header files etc. is going to be a disaster!

One more thing, if you also need your own mavlink messages that are not in the standard but added by you e.g. in a separate mavlink dialect like mydialect.xml or added to common.xml then you need to generate the C headers for your messages and then replace the existing ones of this library.

The place to change this would be in the [mavlink_include.h](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/develop/src/core/mavlink_include.h) once and for all.

I hope that helps.

And one more thing:
Before you change all of how PX4, MAVSDK, MAVLink etc. works, think if you can make your use case work within the existing ways of doing things. You're going to have a much easier time.
For instance, for control from a companion computer you could use offboard control, just as an example.

> So far I've been able to issue simple commands such as takeoff and loitering by manually sending the corresponding command and filling out the 7 parameters on my own.

Right, that's good but note that you don't get command retransmission etc. this way. The way to get that is to use the methods that are used in plugins.

> it should send a message with the corresponding data to every system and every component according to the documentation.

I think so too but you would have to debug in detail what is happening. One thing is that the message might not be sent out because MAVSDK thinks it doesn't know who 0 is and doesn't send it at all.

> Like you said, it's best to write my own plugin using whatever functions I need and then calling the plugin functions in the actual code.

title: Getting HTTP 503 when attempting to subscribe to telemetry but works after connecting with QGroundControl
author: tltanlum
body:
When I connect with `mavsdk_server_bin` to my drone running `ArduPilot`, I cannot subscribe for telemetry as my web client is receiving 503 from `mavsdk_server_bin`. It is the same behavior with `APM Planner` and I connect through the serial port in both cases(`mavsdk_server_bin` and `APM Planner`) mutually exclusively.

Once I connect with `QGroundControl` through the serial port, all the data starts streaming. From there on I can connect with either `APM Planner` or `mavsdk_server_bin` and they both receive the data just fine; and my web client can subscribe to telemetry just fine through `mavsdk_server_bin`.

I am not sure what triggers the data to start streaming through `QGroundControl `and I would expect this to be the norm to be honest. I am wondering if there is an `ArduPilot` setting to have this behavior enabled by default for all clients connecting to `mavlink` through serial/tcp/udp?

If I hardware reset the `ArduPilot` the same problem comes up as I need to run `QGroundControl` which somehow triggers the `mavlink` streaming.

APM-Planner v2-2.0.30-rc3
QGrountControl v4.3.0
