title: Simplify build process
author: dakejahl
body:
**Issue**
It's not super easy to build the library, and I'm not sure how to do a clean build without removing the dependencies added via FetchContent. It would be nice to be able to remove only the source build files so that we don't have to always redownload the dependencies (right now I just delete build/ and install/)

**Solution**
For my C++ projects I always add a Makefile to wrap the CMake commands. I like doing this because for every project I know I can run `make`, `make clean` and `make install`. The underlying actions of each recipe could vary, but it makes it easy for me to switch between projects without having to remember specifics of how they're built/deployed.

answer_comments.body:
> @JonasVautherin: Makefile wrapping CMake that PX4 used to have

Still has it, and I don't like it.

> @dakejahl: I shouldn't need to know all these details

I agree, except:
1. Dependencies are hard, and C++ doesn't have support for this, so it's up to the build system you choose or whatever else you do. We opted for cmake which means you need to learn/understand cmake. Yes, it's not just one command, but that's because we don't just support one OS or one setup.
2. And that is the second point. We could use something like vcpkg, conan, hunter, etc. and that might simplify things, however, as far as I'm aware that doesn't work for cross compilation builds that we support using dockcross, iOS, etc.. If we didn't have any cross-compilation it likely could be simpler.

> sane defaults that I can use for every project.

That's exactly what it would be: it would be defaults **for you** (and probably me) but not for everyone and so it can also create confusion. Having a `Makefile` would suddenly mean people will try to just use make, not realizing it's cmake, so I wouldn't want that. What I could see is a `build_linux.sh` sort of thing. However, you will end up adding arguments to this (MAVSDK bespoke) script that you will have to remember (e.g. build type). Over time you end up with this script encoding all sorts of cmake options, at which point we could just use [cmake-presets](https://cmake.org/cmake/help/latest/manual/cmake-presets.7.html), and maybe that would be worthwhile. Last time I checked it wasn't quite supported for the cmake version we were targetting but by now it could be ok. I don't think I'd use it personally, mostly because it's yet another layer on top of cmake when I can just use the cmake configure lines that I have in my zsh history.

> @JonasVautherin I do that, too. That's why I want projects to use their tools in a standard way, so that I need to learn how to use Autotools, Meson, CMake, SwiftPkg, Carthage or Gradle only once, instead of having to learn a new build.sh for each project (which may call a Makefile wrapping CMake with custom functions that call Python scripts below).

That's exactly it. You put it better than I could @JonasVautherin.

> @dakejahl I don't want to learn anything, I don't want to read the docs

Sorry, you have to read the one page on how to build it, and take around 10s to type it out. I'm sorry we don't know how to make it simpler. (And no a git submodule mess is not going to happen.)

A dumb user should install the package from deb. A contributor needs to know the 3 arguments to cmake.

Here is another take on why I don't want a Makefile:

If I open the project in an IDE, say VSCode or CLion, I want it to detect that it's just cmake, and it will just work. If it also has a Makefile, it will ask you, and you need to know which one is the correct option. A developer new to it will be confused and not know which one to use.

And PX4 as an example: there is duplicated cmake logic in two places because of the "easy" Makefile:

1. https://github.com/PX4/PX4-Autopilot/blob/4215e20120706221ce6f4cd0fab332a55f3bbeac/Makefile#L178-L196
2. https://github.com/PX4/PX4-Autopilot/blob/4215e20120706221ce6f4cd0fab332a55f3bbeac/.vscode/cmake-variants.yaml#L4-L8
Fair enough. I understand where you're coming from and actually appreciate you bringing up friction points! This one is unfortunately one where it's not so easy, and we have opinions :).

> I thought if it's annoying for me it's probably annoying for others and thought it would be a good suggestion... wasn't trying to criticize or spark a debate.

And I didn't want to sound emotional or offended, sorry if that's how I came across :see_no_evil:. I guess my point is that I spent a lot of time trying different things and I haven't found a silver bullet :shrug:. Even modern language package managers come with their issues (often making it easier for developers but terrible for distro maintainers and security in general).

comments.body:
I have [opinions](https://www.acarg.ch/posts/cmake-deps/) [on that topic](https://www.acarg.ch/posts/cmake-superbuild/) :grin:.

> I'm not sure how to do a clean build without removing the dependencies added via FetchContent.

We don't use FetchContent, we use ExternalProject_Add. I find the difference important because we use `find_package` where FetchContent encourages the use of `add_subdirectory()` which I find awful for dependencies.

> For my C++ projects I always add a Makefile to wrap the CMake commands.

I would strongly discourage that. In my experience it tends to end up in a weird Automake/CMake mix that nobody understands (PX4 used to be like that).

What you should be able to do (and if that doesn't work, then it needs to be fixed) is:

1. Build the third parties separately from [third_party/](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/tree/main/third_party). Something like:

```cmake
cmake -DCMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX=/path/to/where/you/want/third/parties -DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH=/path/to/where/you/want/third/parties -Bbuild -S.
cmake --build build --target install
```

This should build and install the dependencies in `/path/to/where/you/want/third/parties`. This only needs to be done once. You may even skip that and install the dependencies from your system package manager if that works.

This is basically what is described [here](https://www.acarg.ch/posts/cmake-deps/), but our superbuild makes it a bit more convoluted.

2. Build MAVSDK with `-DSUPERBUILD=OFF` and `-DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH=/path/to/where/you/want/third/parties`. This will completely skip the superbuild and fetch the dependencies you built in the previous step.

[I wish we didn't have a superbuild](https://www.acarg.ch/posts/cmake-superbuild), but the fact is that most people don't know how the basics of CMake and therefore we need a superbuild. I'm already happy that we don't have the same kind of Makefile wrapping CMake that PX4 used to have :innocent:.

But MAVSDK does work without the superbuild (`-DSUPERBUILD=OFF`), and this is tested in the CI (to some extent) when we build system packages.

Does that help?

I think you illustrated my point :grin: I shouldn't need to know all these details. It would be nice to have a default obvious way to build/install/clean.

> I would strongly discourage that. In my experience it tends to end up in a weird Automake/CMake mix that nobody understands

I use `make` basically as a wrapper for bash. You could use bash too **install.sh** **build.sh** **clean.sh**. The idea is a one line command that is stupid easy to remember. It would make it easier to work on the project.

Anyway, my opinion... one could argue that you shouldn't work on a project without knowing exactly how it works. I end up bouncing around between a lot of projects and it's a lot easier to remember just one build/install/clean command with sane defaults that I can use for every project.

> I shouldn't need to know all these details.

Depends on what details you mean. As I said, I don't like superbuilds (even though I wrote this one) because they only work in specific situations and are generally not standard (even Meson tries to have a first class superbuild which is admittedly nicer when you want it, but also even more annoying when you don't want it).

IMHO, if you use a C++ project that uses CMake, you should know that:

1. CMake has a configure step (e.g. `cmake -Bbuild -S.`) and a build step (e.g. `cmake --build build`).
2. CMake will try to find dependencies that are included with `find_package()`, either on your system or in a custom path if you set `CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH`.
3. The project may try to provide helpers for you to build the dependencies, e.g. in the form of a superbuild.

By having a superbuild, we make it easier for people who don't want to ever see `-DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH`, but at the cost of making it harder for you (because now there is an indirection with `-DSUPERBUILD=OFF`).

> You could use bash too install.sh build.sh clean.sh.

Say we have that. I assume that `build.sh` builds all the dependencies + MAVSDK, and `clean.sh` removes all of those. How does that solve your problem, which is "I'm not sure how to do a clean build without removing the dependencies"?

Should we have `build.sh`, `build_dependencies_only.sh`, `build_mavsdk_only.sh`, `install.sh`, `install_dependencies_only.sh`, `install_mavsdk_only.sh`, `clean.sh`, `clean_dependencies_only.sh`, `clean_mavsdk_only.sh`, ...?

My solution is this: choose a build system (in this case we chose CMake) and use it the way it's meant to be used (no Makefile wrappers, no magic superbuilds like the one I wrote here, ...). And then agree on the fact that developers should know the two commands they need to build a CMake project (or at least how to Google for them). :innocent: 

> I end up bouncing around between a lot of projects

I do that, too. That's why I want projects to use their tools in a standard way, so that I need to learn how to use Autotools, Meson, CMake, SwiftPkg, Carthage or Gradle only once, instead of having to learn a new `build.sh` for each project (which may call a Makefile wrapping CMake with custom functions that call Python scripts below).

Think of this issue report as coming from a "dumb user". I don't want to learn anything, I don't want to read the docs, I just want to build/install/clean in a way that could be considered the most standard way possible (you can assume I'm not modifying dependencies, because dumb users don't do that). It's not that I can't learn or remember how to do things the "standard" way for a given toolchain, I just shouldn't need to. Especially if it's a single LOC change. I think we probably have a difference of opinion here. Honestly even remembering `cmake -Bbuild -S.` is asking too much :laughing:  

I guess what I'm getting it is I personally like to be able to Do The Thing with a single command I can type in less than 2 seconds.

Well we could have a `build.sh` that just builds everything, and a `clean.sh` that cleans everything. It would only solve the first half of the first sentence of this issue, but we could do it.

Actually I would be happier without a superbuild and with `build.sh` and `clean.sh` instead (though I'm nervous with scripts that run `rm -rf`, and in our case cleaning is really just `rm -rf build/`). I tried to remove the superbuild [a while ago](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/compare/main...cmake-reorg) but the conclusion was that we were losing the "easy way".

I would be happier if I could say "if you just want to build everything, run `build.sh`, and if you want to have control just use it as a CMake project".

> I guess what I'm getting it is I personally like to be able to Do The Thing with a single command I can type in less than 2 seconds.

If you manage to fully solve this issue (including the partial cleaning you mention) with a single command you can type in less than 2 seconds, please open a PR! I would be very happy to have that, but I don't see how to do it.

> @JonasVautherin: Makefile wrapping CMake that PX4 used to have

Still has it, and I don't like it.

> @dakejahl: I shouldn't need to know all these details

I agree, except:
1. Dependencies are hard, and C++ doesn't have support for this, so it's up to the build system you choose or whatever else you do. We opted for cmake which means you need to learn/understand cmake. Yes, it's not just one command, but that's because we don't just support one OS or one setup.
2. And that is the second point. We could use something like vcpkg, conan, hunter, etc. and that might simplify things, however, as far as I'm aware that doesn't work for cross compilation builds that we support using dockcross, iOS, etc.. If we didn't have any cross-compilation it likely could be simpler.

> sane defaults that I can use for every project.

That's exactly what it would be: it would be defaults **for you** (and probably me) but not for everyone and so it can also create confusion. Having a `Makefile` would suddenly mean people will try to just use make, not realizing it's cmake, so I wouldn't want that. What I could see is a `build_linux.sh` sort of thing. However, you will end up adding arguments to this (MAVSDK bespoke) script that you will have to remember (e.g. build type). Over time you end up with this script encoding all sorts of cmake options, at which point we could just use [cmake-presets](https://cmake.org/cmake/help/latest/manual/cmake-presets.7.html), and maybe that would be worthwhile. Last time I checked it wasn't quite supported for the cmake version we were targetting but by now it could be ok. I don't think I'd use it personally, mostly because it's yet another layer on top of cmake when I can just use the cmake configure lines that I have in my zsh history.

> @JonasVautherin I do that, too. That's why I want projects to use their tools in a standard way, so that I need to learn how to use Autotools, Meson, CMake, SwiftPkg, Carthage or Gradle only once, instead of having to learn a new build.sh for each project (which may call a Makefile wrapping CMake with custom functions that call Python scripts below).

That's exactly it. You put it better than I could @JonasVautherin.

> @dakejahl I don't want to learn anything, I don't want to read the docs

Sorry, you have to read the one page on how to build it, and take around 10s to type it out. I'm sorry we don't know how to make it simpler. (And no a git submodule mess is not going to happen.)

A dumb user should install the package from deb. A contributor needs to know the 3 arguments to cmake.

Here is another take on why I don't want a Makefile:

If I open the project in an IDE, say VSCode or CLion, I want it to detect that it's just cmake, and it will just work. If it also has a Makefile, it will ask you, and you need to know which one is the correct option. A developer new to it will be confused and not know which one to use.

And PX4 as an example: there is duplicated cmake logic in two places because of the "easy" Makefile:

1. https://github.com/PX4/PX4-Autopilot/blob/4215e20120706221ce6f4cd0fab332a55f3bbeac/Makefile#L178-L196
2. https://github.com/PX4/PX4-Autopilot/blob/4215e20120706221ce6f4cd0fab332a55f3bbeac/.vscode/cmake-variants.yaml#L4-L8

Ah yeah didn't think about non-linux. I don't use an IDE so I didn't think about the IDE auto-detect case. I guess it's not easy to implement a general solution. Anyway I only brought this up because it's a minor pain point for me, I thought if it's annoying for me it's probably annoying for others and thought it would be a good suggestion... wasn't trying to criticize or spark a debate.

I'll just keep using my out of tree Makefile :+1:
Fair enough. I understand where you're coming from and actually appreciate you bringing up friction points! This one is unfortunately one where it's not so easy, and we have opinions :).

> I thought if it's annoying for me it's probably annoying for others and thought it would be a good suggestion... wasn't trying to criticize or spark a debate.

And I didn't want to sound emotional or offended, sorry if that's how I came across :see_no_evil:. I guess my point is that I spent a lot of time trying different things and I haven't found a silver bullet :shrug:. Even modern language package managers come with their issues (often making it easier for developers but terrible for distro maintainers and security in general).

title: Example Fly mission uses hard-coding of mission points
author: shakthi-prashanth-m
body:
Fly mission example uses[ hard-coding](https://github.com/dronecore/DroneCore/blob/develop/example/fly_mission/fly_mission.cpp#L73) of waypoints. It is hard for someone to compute longitude, latitude, etc and use this example.

comments.body:
Thanks for the issue. This has been requested several times actually and it would be a good thing to have.

The only catch is that not all mission items are currently supported in DroneCore, so we won't be fully compatible. We would have to just ignore unsupported items and warn the user about it.

@julianoes @shakthi-prashanth-m 

> Fly mission example uses hard-coding of waypoints. It is hard for someone to compute longitude, latitude, etc and use this example.

The solution to this problem is NED based mission points - as per #100.
I really think it makes sense to implement this ourselves, sooner rather than later.

> The only catch is that not all mission items are currently supported in DroneCore, so we won't be fully compatible. We would have to just ignore unsupported items and warn the user about it.

My take on this is that mission import should completely bypass whatever we do with the API. It would be something to add flexibility over the top of our existing API. So perhaps:
- Allow upload and download of files *or strings* in generic waypoint format. Users can then dynamically construct the messages if they want.
- Provide an API to send a generic waypoint message or custom message - so the user can send whatever message they like. 

Yes I know it removes some of the "clean-ness" of the API, but if we don't do this then I personally as a user would be forced to write my own plugin to do this.

title: Timesync message warning spam
author: depauwjimmy
body:
Continued from : https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/issues/955

Summary

1 test program connected on TELEM1 with an FTDI cable to act as GroundStation
1 companion computer connected on TELEM2
AP is running using current PX4 beta firmware on master branch.
A Here2 GPS unit is connected.

GS receives the following message at a regular interval

` [12:02:24|Warn ] RTT too high for timesync: 1.57917e+12 ms`

CC receives the same message but sometimes with "1.57917e+12 ms" and sometimes a normal amount of time below 100ms

answer_comments.body: I need to look into the timesync stuff at some point. Right now I don't understand what it really does, so I rather not comment.

Just for help if you or something else will need to understand tymesync mechanism:

- MAVLink have an a simple message called [`TIMESYNC`](https://mavlink.io/en/messages/common.html#TIMESYNC):
It have only two fields:
 `ts1` - the one who needs (**Client**) to synchronize time with other side (**Server**) [put in this field his own time](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/develop/src/core/timesync.cpp#L29) (in nanoseconds)
 `tc1` - **Server** [put in this field his own current time](https://github.com/PX4/Firmware/blob/07d656e971a72d1202651dfd3b4642736fb078d7/src/modules/mavlink/mavlink_timesync.cpp#L66) in response message (see below).

- Algorithm of timesync in common words (**Client**: MAVSDK, **Server**: Autopilot):

1. **Client** [send](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/develop/src/core/timesync.cpp#L29) `TIMESYNC` message (request) with `tc1: 0; ts1: current_client_time`.
2. **Server** [receiving](https://github.com/PX4/Firmware/blob/07d656e971a72d1202651dfd3b4642736fb078d7/src/modules/mavlink/mavlink_timesync.cpp#L55) this message.
3. **Server** [create response TIMESYNC message](https://github.com/PX4/Firmware/blob/07d656e971a72d1202651dfd3b4642736fb078d7/src/modules/mavlink/mavlink_timesync.cpp#L64-L67) with `tc1: current_server_time; ts1: current_client_time`. `current_client_time` received in request message - **Server** [just make copy of it](https://github.com/PX4/Firmware/blob/07d656e971a72d1202651dfd3b4642736fb078d7/src/modules/mavlink/mavlink_timesync.cpp#L67)
4. **Server** [send response message](https://github.com/PX4/Firmware/blob/07d656e971a72d1202651dfd3b4642736fb078d7/src/modules/mavlink/mavlink_timesync.cpp#L69) to **Client**
5. **Client** receive `TIMESYNC` message and [see that](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/develop/src/core/timesync.cpp#L48) `tc1` is not eq `0`, so this is response message.
6. **Client** calculate time diff (`tc1 - ts1`) and [set time offset](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/develop/src/core/timesync.cpp#L51).
@depauwjimmy is this issue still actual or PX4/Firmware#14016 resolve it?
I think this is resolved unless when PX4 runs faster than realtime. For that case we can probably open a new issue.

title: Move deps like tinyxml and jsoncpp to plugins
author: devbharat
body:
Now that its possible to selectively enable/disable building plugins with the plugins.txt file, dependencies(like openssl, CURL, tinyxml and json) that are only needed by certain plugins can perhaps move to the needed plugin's own CMakeLists.txt file?

CMake also [allows that](https://stackoverflow.com/a/75246115). Perhaps this is too much of an optimization, but if someone just wants to use core library (and no plugins) downloading and installing these takes a bit of time and seems unnecessary.
resolution_evidence: thread converges on a working answer

answer_comments.body:
> If you are doing a local build and install of mavsdk with externalproject_add(), you’d need to clone & build for every fresh build

No you don't. Just:

1. Build the [third_party](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/tree/main/third_party) deps and install them somewhere (either by running from `./third_party` with `-DCMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX=/path/to/where/you/install/deps` or with the MAVSDK option [-DDEPS_INSTALL_PATH](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/main/CMakeLists.txt#L52) which does exactly that).
2. Then when building your project, add `/path/to/where/you/install/deps` to `-DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH`. Whether or not you install mavsdk with the deps or use `externalproject_add` doesn't matter, the MAVSDK CMakeLists will look into `CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH` at configure time.

That works when cross-compiling, too :+1:.

Dependency management is often over-estimated and wrapped into layers of tooling, I find. But it's pretty simple: you need your dependencies "installed" somewhere, and then you need to tell your build system where to find them. The build system looks on your system by default, but if you install them locally somewhere, you can tell your build system to look there (with CMake that's with `-DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH`).

I admit that the wrappers in MAVSDK are a bit convoluted (my bad :see_no_evil:), but now I do it [like this](https://www.acarg.ch/posts/cmake-deps/), if you are interested.
What about the find_package calls? Do you just move them to the plugins too?
@Consti10 I'd love a PR that removes the `std::filesystem` hack. I would be glad to have that gone.
jsoncpp as an example is used in core now anyway, so the discussion is moot.

comments.body: So, there is now an option to disable cURL. However, tinyxml2 and jsoncpp are going to get more important in many parts in a couple of component information features that are coming up, so I'm less motivated to move them.
Unless there is an actual use-case, I'd say we can keep it the way it is. We provide helpers to help build them, they can be linked statically, and they are really not big :+1:.

Makes sense. The use-case is rather straightforward, say you just want to use mavsdk passthrough plugin (say for integration testing of another code-base) you shouldn't need much.

Or perhaps you'd want to add your own plugins and build on top of the "core" mavsdk outside the mavsdk repo (not sure if we already can or if it needs a bit more modification to enable such 'external' plugins, need to check) after including it as a library in another project, it seems weird to have to install dependencies for plugins you are not even building. But i agree tinyxml and jsoncpp are not too much. Feel free to close!

What about the possibility to manually disable the dependencies like we did it for cURL?

I think that might be easier than having it flow out of the CMakeLists.txt configure step.

The problem I see is that if we move the `find_package` into the plugin's CMakeLists.txt then we also need to set some sort of variable to signal to third_party/CMakeLists.txt that it's not required. title: When multiple vehicles are connected, all systems get data from all vehicles, regardless of sysid.
author: poli0048

answer_comments.body: Sorry for just doing it but it bugged me enough that I wanted to do it rightaway.

I first tried 2. but it turns out that didn't work for commands. The reason was that the initial system gets initialized with target 0. At that point the MavlinkCommandSender registers for any messages, in this case for 0. Then, once a system is discovered, the system ID is set to 1 but the MavlinkCommandSender's subscription is still 0, and it doesn't receive the acks.

I therefore went back to 1, so we now have MavlinkMessageHandlers in MavsdkImpl for components and in SystemImpl for systems.

title: Structure Cmake for Cpp package managers
author: bazfp
body:
It would be useful to be able to use MAVSDK with cpp package managers (Hunter, Conan etc) for automatic dependency resolution. Instead of depending on a `SUPERBUILD` or local dependencies.

I've been implementing this library with [hunter](https://github.com/cpp-pm/hunter) and have found success by doing the following:

0. `SUPERBUILD=OFF`
1. Remove git commands from Cmakelists.txt, such as getting version from git tags
2. Don't use git submodules 
3. Remove Find modules provided by https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/main/src/cmake/Modules/
4. Use common lib names when linking: 
`JsonCpp::jsoncpp` -> `jsoncpp_lib`
`tinyxml2::tinyxml2` -> `tinyxml2`


This won't work for `mavsdk_server` but it is a start. There is likely to be more changes to this to get it to work (for Hunter I have included Hunter_gate but obviously this differs for each manager :) )

title: server plugins should not be limited to a single system
author: dlech
body:
As I have been working on the camera server plugin, I've noticed a problem with the way the current plugin architecture creates a plugin instance per system (i.e. `CameraServerImpl::CameraServerImpl(System& system) : PluginImplBase(system)`). The problem is that the plugin state is per system when really it needs to be global. This means that consumers of MAVSDK have to do lots of extra work to ensure that each plugin instance for a single camera remains in a consistent state with the others. Example: https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/pull/1699/commits/1528f0cf05fcae55be6941694f7d935d0fa378b0.

I suppose other server plugins haven't noticed this problem before since they probably only communicate with one system. However, cameras need to communicate with both an autopilot and a ground station at the same time.

I think a solution to this would be to create a new "server" plugin type that is initialized with `CameraServerImpl::CameraServerImpl(Mavsdk& mavsdk) : ServerPluginImplBase(mavsdk)` instead. Then a single plugin instance could receive and send messages to any number of systems. (And broadcast to multiple systems as required by [CAMERA_IMAGE_CAPTURED](https://mavlink.io/en/messages/common.html#CAMERA_IMAGE_CAPTURED).)

Otherwise, we should reconsider https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK-Proto/pull/274#issuecomment-1039591231, particularly the `Set*` methods. Basically, the camera server plugin should have no state and everything is handled by callbacks to user code. I'm not sure this is really possible though since the callbacks themselves are considered part of the state.

title: Link libc statically for Android
author: JonasVautherin
body:
From @Katawann on [discuss](https://discuss.px4.io/t/failed-to-run-mavsdk-server-in-react-native-app-on-android/20607):

### Context:
I’m trying to build an app on Android with React Native and using MAVSDK in it. It works like a charm if I run MAVSDK-Java client on the react app (on my device) and mavsdk_server running on a linux host. However my goal is to have both client and server on the app.

### Error:
When I add mavsdk_server in my app with implementation 'io.mavsdk:mavsdk-server:0.6.0', it fails with the following error:

```
More than one file was found with OS independent path 'lib/arm64-v8a/libc++_shared.so'. If you are using jniLibs and CMake IMPORTED targets, see https://developer.android.com/studio/preview/features#automatic_packaging_of_prebuilt_dependencies_used_by_cmake
```

### Root cause:
It seems that React Native already have a libc++_shared.so library and don’t know which one to load (supposition). I tried some solutions on React Native side but none of them work (same issue for other SDK that MAVSDK).

linked_issues.title: Missing filesystem symbols when linking libc on Android

comments.body:
@Katawann: I think that you may be right in that MAVSDK-Java should not bring `libc++_shared.so` with it, and that's the reason for your issue. I do believe that the solution would be to build `libmavsdk_server.so` as a static library. We already do that for `mavsdk_server` (that we build as a static executable), so that should be similar (where instead of building a static executable `mavsdk_server`, for Android we want `libmavsdk_server.so` to link everything statically).

If you look e.g. [here](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/main/src/mavsdk_server/src/CMakeLists.txt#L102-L107), you'll find this `BUILD_STATIC_MAVSDK_SERVER` that we use in our CMakeLists.txt.

But [this is not done for Android or iOS](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/main/src/mavsdk_server/src/CMakeLists.txt#L92), where we only build `libmavsdk_server.so`. Maybe you could try to make it such that for Android, it does link statically into `libmavsdk_server.so`.

Does that make sense?
Closing due to inactivity. Feel free to reopen if necessary.

title: Mavlink header install using ExternalProject_Add
author: jperez-droneup
body:
When building MAVSDK using CMake's ExternalProject_Add, with SUPERBUILD on, it will properly pull and build all of MAVSDK's dependencies. However, I get errors for missing mavlink headers and indeed [this commit](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/commit/04e78f163d3dd630103a353cca8d04fd943f8486#diff-4c224720c825bc0b47c1375867b1f0eb0f7943639c4ef77d1d7ef38e9792ccb6) changed where the files were installed to. It would be great if we could either have the mavlink headers installed alongside the mavsdk ones automatically, or at least have a CMake option to change where dependencies are installed to.

I would suggest possibly setting `DEPS_INSTALL_PATH` to `CMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX` on [this line]( https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/0338c3e5eb86ec6c00a11ae99b019c97646b907a/CMakeLists.txt#L56) . Alternatively, you could make `DEPS_INSTALL_PATH` an optional argument, so users can place it to their needs, and it would be accessible via ExternalProject_Add.

answer_comments.body:
Just build your project with `CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH=path/to/mavsdk/src/mavsdk_proj-build/third_party/install`, right? That would be clean.

It would even allow you to build mavlink yourself separately, install it somewhere, and point CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH to that (instead of the mavsdk one) if you like it better.

The default for `find_package` is to look for the package on the system. CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH just says "btw, look here first because I have some packages installed here". It's perfectly legal and very convenient.

> To a degree, yeah, if I wanted to put mavlink specifically into my cmake code. I was trying to keep it generic.

Well MAVSDK transitively depends on MAVLink in its public interface (before #2084), and therefore `find_package` must find MAVLink somewhere. It's not about "putting mavlink specifically into your cmake code", it won't actually change your CMake code. You just have to tell your CMake project where to find the dependencies with `find_package`. Either you install MAVLink on your system, or you point CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH to it.

When you install the MAVSDK `.deb` package, it depends on stuff like openssl, and it will require you to install them on your system. Still you don't consider that you are "putting openssl specifically into your cmake code", right? That's exactly the same for MAVLink, except that MAVLink is not available with `apt install libmavlink-dev`.

> I somewhat reverted this to the previous behaviour: https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/pull/2084.

Yeah I guess that solves the confusion around the transitive dependency :+1:

comments.body:
I wonder if `-DDEPS_INSTALL_PATH` when you build MAVSDK doesn't just allow you to set it. But probably it should rather be an `option()` to make this clear...

Note that in your project that depends on MAVSDK (let's call it `my-project`), you can set the `CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH` to the install path of the MAVSDK third parties. Something like this:

```cmake
cmake -DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH="your/cmake/prefix/path;path/to/mavsdk/build/third_party/install" -Bbuild -S.
```

This said, after some experience with CMake superbuilds, my more recent opinion is that we should provide helpers, but not a superbuild (see my blog post [here](https://www.acarg.ch/posts/cmake-deps/)). That's much less confusing in the sense that it makes it clear to the user that they should handle their dependencies.

But well, doesn't change the fact that MAVSDK uses this superbuild, and many users don't want to know about how they should handle their dependencies :see_no_evil:. So probably your best bet is what I wrote in my previous message.

Yeah, for the time being I am just using:
```
target_include_directories(my-project PUBLIC
    ${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR}/mavsdk/src/mavsdk_proj-build/third_party/install/include
)
```
An option would be nice to have still, just so it's not quite so hacky.

Just build your project with `CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH=path/to/mavsdk/src/mavsdk_proj-build/third_party/install`, right? That would be clean.

It would even allow you to build mavlink yourself separately, install it somewhere, and point CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH to that (instead of the mavsdk one) if you like it better.

The default for `find_package` is to look for the package on the system. CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH just says "btw, look here first because I have some packages installed here". It's perfectly legal and very convenient.

To a degree, yeah, if I wanted to put mavlink specifically into my cmake code. I was trying to keep it generic. When using ExternalProject_Add, the code is not yet in CMake at generation time, so I can't use find_package on a target which is not installed yet. If I pulled the full repo and had it as a submodule instead (before calling any CMake), then yes I could use the CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH.
I somewhat reverted this to the previous behaviour: #2084.

> To a degree, yeah, if I wanted to put mavlink specifically into my cmake code. I was trying to keep it generic.

Well MAVSDK transitively depends on MAVLink in its public interface (before #2084), and therefore `find_package` must find MAVLink somewhere. When you install the MAVSDK `.deb` package, it depends on stuff like openssl, and it will require you to install them on your system. Still you don't consider that you are "putting openssl specifically into your cmake code", right? That's exactly the same for MAVLink, except that MAVLink is not available with `apt install libmavlink-dev`.

> I somewhat reverted this to the previous behaviour: https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/pull/2084.

Yeah I guess that solves the confusion around the transitive dependency :+1:

title: question: how can I get the RC inputs from mavsdk_server ?
author: imindude
body:
I'm making some autocontrol in use of the mavsdk_server and C#.
I think almost feature is exist that I need, except one.
In emergency situation, I want to stop the drone's auto control and change the manual control by RC's toggle switch.
Mavsdk, it support the mavlink_passthrough feature. So I was using this and implemented emergency stop feature.
But I think mavsdk_server did not support the passthrough or callback of RC input.
How can I know the RC input in C# application? mavsdk_server can handle the RC input?

answer_comments.body: PX4 should switch out of an auto mode automatically if you move the sticks in RC.
Aha, so you are saying offboard mode from MAVSDK keeps switching back to offboard? Can you share a log where that happens? I think that would not be intentional.

Oh, I think you understand. So instead of detecting it in MAVSDK, you should directly check that switch in PX4, either using [RC_MAP_OFFB_SW](https://docs.px4.io/master/en/advanced_config/parameter_reference.html#RC_MAP_OFFB_SW), or using the [RC_MAP_FLTMODE](https://docs.px4.io/master/en/advanced_config/parameter_reference.html#RC_MAP_FLTMODE). You can configure these in QGC.

Also, do enable or disable override from the sticks, there is a param that you can use: [COM_RC_OVERRIDE](https://docs.px4.io/master/en/advanced_config/parameter_reference.html#COM_RC_OVERRIDE).

> 'MD_DynamicRelease' doesn't match value 'MDd_DynamicDebug'

That's your issue. Some conflict between _some_ libraries being built in Release mode and _some_ in Debug mode.

Can you try maybe those two?

```
cmake --build build --config Release
```

and

```
cmake --build build --config Debug
```

Much better! So the MAVSDK you installed is a Release version, meaning that you should build your example in Release mode.

Now I suspect that you are trying to build an example from the `main` branch, but you installed MAVSDK 1.4.x. That would usually work, but we are in the process of moving to MAVSDK v2, meaning that `main` is not compatible with `1.x.x`.

Can you try to build the `takeoff_and_land` example from https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/tree/v1.4.6 (instead of the one from `main`?
Just a comment: make sure never to match Release and Debug builds on Windows as the ABI of std::string is not compatible.

Which version of clang do you have? 

    $ clang --version

It actually looks like #481. You could try either to update clang, or to remove `-Wno-unused-lambda-capture` [here](https://github.com/Dronecode/DronecodeSDK/blob/develop/cmake/compiler_flags.cmake#L28-L31).

> I removed the line you told me to but still no luck and got a similar error message.

What was that message? Another unknown flag?

> I got this error while running it on the second MacBook

You have permission errors there. Can you try to clean and build again?

```
make distclean
make
```

Great for the clang 9 laptop!

Now for the clang 10 laptop, I believe you need to keep `-Wno-unused-lambda-capture` (because it is complaining exactly about that :sweat_smile:).

title: Generalizing MAVSDK for non-autopilot control
author: coderkalyan
body:
Traditionally, MAVSDK has been used to connect solely to a drone in order to control it; connecting to other peripherals has been more of an addon than a main feature. While this is definitely the main use case of MAVSDK, I think it would be nice to be able to use MAVSDK as a more generic high level platform for any MAVLink communication. This would increase the number of use cases and platforms MAVSDK can be deployed to, and also allow some very interesting new possibilities. Below are some comments on what the current state of affairs is and what can be done to improve this without sacrificing ease-of-use.

The base `Mavsdk` class define the source system and component, which defines the local side of the communication. With the recent addition of the `Configuration` class, this is fine - the system and component ID can be changed without restrictions, and there are sane defaults. From here on, though, things get a bit more complicated.

The `System` class, although designed to connect to any MAVLink compatible system, is in reality only tailored to connect to a single autopilot. This causes problems, obviously, when connecting to anything *other* than the autopilot. Peripherals such as gimbals and cameras are supported; however, they are all connected to the parent `System` rather than a parent `Mavsdk`, which makes more sense to me. As a result, you need to connect to an autopilot before getting access to any peripherals. Additionally, although MAVSDK can be used to control an autopilot from a companion computer, how MAVSDK handles connecting to a different component on the same system is uncertain and definitely undocumented.

To be completely honest, from looking into the core source code, I feel the code to handle system and component ids is very messy; a good portion of it is probably very old code, but I think we can do better. For example, there is a lot of hard-coding "let's throw away messages from these ids", "lets assume this component ID means this", etc. This leaves very little room for anything that deviates from the standard "I have a ground station which connects to my drone, both with standard IDs." I'd like to be able to use MAVSDK for more complex things including intra-system (inter-component) communication. I'm happy to take charge of cleaning some of it up + documenting it, if we can agree on what to do! For starters, I think we should all read https://mavlink.io/en/guide/routing.html :smile: 

I'm not sure the best way to do this, since I don't want to break the current API (create a System from a Mavsdk, create plugins from the System). One idea I had was to create a `Component` or similar, which is a more high level representation of a target that MAVSDK can connect to. The `Mavsdk` class can then search for and connect to multiple `Components`, and the existing `System` would be a type of `Component` (not sure if System is even the right word for it, in that sense, but I'm hesitant to break the current API). Or we could rename `System` to `Component`, and enable different plugins based on the type of `Component`, such as Autopilot, Companion Computer, Gimbal Device, Camera, custom component, etc.

Anyway, let me know what you guys think! Again, I'm happy to implement the changes!

Then we can have multiple types of Nodes, including the most obvious, `Autopilot`. We can also have a `Gimbal` and `Camera` node, for example. Plugins that interact with a node can then connect to any kind of node, and some plugins may or may not be able to interface with a node depending on its characteristics.

title: Bug in MissionRawImpl::set_current_mission_item_async()
author: steveb2014

answer_comments.body: Do you feel like opening a PR for it, so that you get the credit? :innocent:

Just ping me here if you need help or decide to give up. But I think it's worth it. It's something like this:

1. Fork the repo
2. Clone your forked repo (that will be your `origin` remote)
3. Create a new branch for your fix, say `git branch fix-mission-set-current-item`

When `mavsdk_server_address=None`, which is what happens when you do:

then `await drone1.connect()` starts the embedded `mavsdk_server` for you. As @julianoes mentions, there is currently no way to set the port on this one, so you cannot run multiple instances of `mavsdk_server` this way (it's actually undefined behavior, I think).

Here, `mavsdk_server_address="localhost"`, so it's not `None`, and therefore `connect()` will not start the embedded `mavsdk_server` for you. In that case you have to run it manually, with something like:

Thank You guys for Your help.

@JonasVautherin typing:

We do provide a windows executable, too: For v0.27.0 we have [mavsdk_server_win32.exe](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/releases/download/v0.27.0/mavsdk_server_win32.exe), and v0.28.0 will be packaged soon. You should be able to run that from the command line, right?

There are two sides in `mavsdk_server`. Let's see it like this:

```
MAVSDK-Python <-----> mavsdk_server <-----> drone
```

In other words, MAVSDK-Python talks to `mavsdk_server` (over gRPC), which talks to the drone (over MAVLink). Let's add this information:

```
MAVSDK-Python <-- gRPC --> mavsdk_server <-- MAVLink --> drone
```

Now, 50040 and 50041 are the ports exposed to both instances of MAVSDK-Python. On the other side, you are using `udp://:14540` twice. Which fails, because two instances of `mavsdk_server` cannot bind to `14540` at the same time. You need two different MAVLink ports there, too. Something like this:

```
MAVSDK-Python <-- gRPC (50040) --> mavsdk_server <-- MAVLink (udp://:14540) --> drone
MAVSDK-Python <-- gRPC (50041) --> mavsdk_server <-- MAVLink (udp://:14541) --> drone
```

Which means that you need to run `mavsdk_server` twice, like this:

```
./mavsdk_server udp://:14540 -p 50040 # mavsdk_server1
./mavsdk_server udp://:14541 -p 50041 # mavsdk_server2
```

In other words:

* drone1 will send MAVLink messages over UDP on port 14540, mavsdk_server1 will receive those MAVLink messages and MAVSDK-Python1 will connect to mavsdk_server1 over gRPC on port 50040
* drone2 will send MAVLink messages over UDP on port 14541, mavsdk_server2 will receive those MAVLink messages and MAVSDK-Python2 will connect to mavsdk_server2 over gRPC on port 50041

Of course, you also need to make sure that drone1 sends to UDP 14540, and drone2 sends to UDP 14541.

title: Mission feasability check status
author: jperez-droneup

comments.body:
Discussed this in the MAVLink call. 

Proposal is a message that provides information about a feasibility check. The message is emitted whenever the feasibility checker is run - after an upload or when the user decides they want to start a mission. We might also have a command to explicitly run the feasibility checker.

@jperez-droneup Would you be interested in defining such a message in development.xml - and possibly providing an implementation?

Note, an alternative would be to standardize the format of STATUSTEXT or event messages for this purpose. That is a valid approach too, but given it would have to happen in two places is more problematic.
@bkueng could this be covered by events already?

Yes as part of the arming reporting. You can check generically if you can run the mission mode. If it fails you get a list of reasons why you cannot run the mission. One of them is a missing valid mission: https://github.com/PX4/PX4-Autopilot/blob/main/src/modules/commander/HealthAndArmingChecks/checks/modeCheck.cpp#L120

If I recall correctly there was also a push in PX4 to directly run feasibility checks on upload and fail the upload accordingly.

> fail the upload accordingly.

Interesting. but we don't have an error to report that, see: https://github.com/mavlink/mavlink/pull/1710

> @bkueng could this be covered by events already?

ArduPilot don't use events yet - they use STATUSTEXT of some format for most things. While I'd be very happy to use events for this kind of thing if it was standardized, until events is widely supported AND the particular events for feasibility are standardized in some way, not sure how we can do so.

So I'm still keen on a message, and possibly a command to trigger feasibility checks on request. Happy for some kind of counter proposal.
It seems like a message would be the easiest way to implement this given the current infrastructure and taking into account Ardupilot. Is this something you would be able to put together?
I'm not opposed but I'm busy on other work. If you need to move this up my priority list, you can always consider [sponsoring](https://github.com/sponsors/julianoes/) me.

@hamishwillee and I just talked about this on the MAVLink call and found that the events system would be the right way to go about this. We might need @bkueng's help to get this drafted properly though.

Re the comment above, the idea is inspired by @bkueng implementation of prearm checks in PX4 using Events. From [the docs](http://docs.px4.io/main/en/advanced_config/prearm_arm_disarm.html#pre-arm-checks):

> Note that internally PX4 runs arming checks at 10Hz. A list of the failed checks is kept, and if the list changes PX4 emits the current list using the [Events interface](http://docs.px4.io/main/en/concept/events_interface.html). The list is also sent out when the GCS connects. Effectively the GCS knows the status of prearm checks immediately, both when disarmed and armed.

I would say **might** be the right way to address this.

What events give us is a way to define both standardized and custom feasibility checks. The events can also be translated and shared with the ground station in a standard way.
What continuously running the checks does is give us a way to clear the failed checks as needed.

It's cool, but only PX4 has implemented Component Information and EVENTs. I'm also not sure that the mission checks can be run continuously at high enough rate.

Instead of events you could have a message with bitmask fields for standard and custom checks failing and stream this, or emit on change.
Instead of continuously running checks you could have a command  that triggers the check to be run and emits either events or above message.

I think events are a really good way to go for this, but not sure what it means to "standardize" this behaviour so flight stacks and GCS can implement to it without having to know about each other. Perhaps it is as simply as defining an event category.

> but not sure what it means to "standardize" this behaviour so flight stacks and GCS can implement to it without having to know about each other

There's a common event namespace intended for that: https://github.com/mavlink/libevents/blob/main/events/common.json#L52

comments.body: I think you're right: right now MAVSDK can only add one remote. This would need to be updated in the implementation :+1:. Open for contributions, though :innocent:

All right, I will try to implement it in few days.
Thank you for the confirmation 👍🏼

To summarize the UDP connections system in Mavsdk.
- add_udp_connection("IP:PORT"):
    Create a new UdpConnection instance listening to IP:PORT.
    When the first message coming from a new endpoint (IP_ENDPOINT:PORT_ENDPOINT) is received, a new remote is created to send messages to IP_ENDPOINT:PORT_ENDPOINT.
    
- setup_udp_remote(IP, PORT):
    Create a new UdpConnection instance listening to 0.0.0.0:0 (port 0 = random port).
    Then a remote is created to send messages to IP:PORT

When sending a message, the mavsdk_impl iterates over all connections to send the message.
However, if one of the connections is a UDP connection and has no remote, the loop will break even if other connections could send the message.

see [add-multi-udp-remotes](https://github.com/yhabib29/MAVSDK/tree/add-multi-udp-remotes)

In addition, could it be interesting to add a vector of available system IDs for each connection ?

When sending a message to a specific system ID, this will allow to ignore connections which have never see the corresponding system ID.

The reason is that for radio connections, it might be better to preserve the bandwidth from useless messages.

> However, if one of the connections is a UDP connection and has no remote, the loop will break even if other connections could send the message.

> When sending a message to a specific system ID, this will allow to ignore connections which have never see the corresponding system ID.

title: Why don't we use exception handling ?
author: shakthi-prashanth-m

answer_comments.body:
The example wouldn't be quite this simple - you still have to wait for arm to complete before doing takeoff, and takeoff to complete before doing land. I'd also much rather wait on arming than have an exception.

Would exceptions play nice with the protobuf stuff?

@shakthi-prashanth-m there are pros and cons to using exceptions in C++.
https://hackernoon.com/error-handling-in-c-or-why-you-should-use-eithers-in-favor-of-exceptions-and-error-codes-f0640912eb45
https://stackoverflow.com/questions/253314/exceptions-or-error-codes
https://google.github.io/styleguide/cppguide.html#Exceptions

I decided to go without exceptions when I started it. Initially the C++ API needed to be simple and clean in order that it can easily be wrapped (manually) by other languages.

Right now I'm very reluctant to change everything that we have so far. I think we should stabilize the gRPC work and refrain from other refactoring that aren't absolutely necessary.
Ok, I'll close this then, thanks @shakthi-prashanth-m for raising this though, appreciated.

title: Cannot use QGroundControl simultaneously with an active mavsdk script in hardware testing

body:
In hardware testing, QGroundControl accesses the serial port of my telemetry radio. This does not allow me to launch a MAVSDK script. The output from the MAVSDK script is that it discovers many systems and components.
Is there any way to find out the correct system/component ID of the flight firmware?
Are there any alternative ways of enabling port forwarding/ keeping QGC open while being able to run a MAVSK script?
It happens smoothly in SITL where the MAVSDK script connects to the local PX4 flight firmware being launched on my system while QGC remains connected to it.

title: Incombatibility issues with PX4's most recent firmware
author: may-ay
body:
Hello all, 

When using PX4's most recent firmware ([1.13.0](https://github.com/PX4/PX4-Autopilot/releases/tag/v1.13.0), px4_fmu-v2_default.px4), I am unable to create [a MAVSDK object](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/b1b0d698baea3fc4c77a7244a3cae1fd3d2981d9/examples/takeoff_and_land/takeoff_and_land.cpp#L29). 

If I update a PX4 (using PX4 mini at the moment) to the most recent version (1.13.0) using QGC, disconnect it from USB, plug it back in, and then attempt to create a MAVSDK object, it fails to create the object. 

However, if I connect the same updated PX4, open up QGC, go through the "Downloading Parameters" portion, quit QGC, and then attempt to create a MAVSDK object, it will work. 

Disconnecting the PX4 again will go back to the original issue of failing to create a MAVSDK object.

This issue occurs on MAVSDK 1.4.2 and 1.4.6. 

If I revert my PX4 back to 1.12.0, I do not experience this issue. 

Screenshot and example walk-through: 

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/23709837/194159390-3efd9296-efa1-4238-8269-f78b29d58876.png)

The first attempt was after updating the PX4 but the PX4 is still connected to QGC. 

The second attempt was after updating the PX4, exiting out of QGC, but not unplugging the USB cable from the PX4. 

The third and fourth attempt were after updating the PX4, exiting out of QGC, unplugging the USB cable from the PX4, and then connecting the USB cable back into the PX4.

I can test a different laptop with Ubuntu 22 today. 

Also, is there a way to generate a more verbose log to maybe understand why the serial connection is failing?

I tried with a laptop running Ubuntu 22 using the .deb: libmavsdk-dev_1.4.16_ubuntu20.04_amd64.deb. 

It worked out of the box. So now I need to debug what is going on with the serial connection on the other laptop.

So something strange is going on on one of my laptops (the original one that I noticed the problem on). 

I spent several hours modifying the udev settings, trying several cables (USB A-C, USB C-C), trying several USB ports on my computer, rebooting, trying bash without modifications (bash --noprofile --norc), and I think that I am narrowing in on a culprit... 

There seems to be a very narrow window, where I can get the example to work. Specifically, if I connect the Pixhawk, and then see the Green PWR indicator on the ethernet side, then I have about literally 1 to 3 seconds to start the example, and it will work. Too soon or too late, and it will not work. My guess is that on the new laptop where I am seeing the issue, that if the laptop doesn't get a signal from the Pixhawk within some specific period, then it is putting that USB port to sleep or something. And that time is probably a few seconds longer than the Pixhawk boot sequence. 

I don't know though. That's my best guess for now. 

On the old laptop, I don't see this behavior.

Ah yes. I think that that was the issue... 

It appears that the new laptop I have is putting the USB ports to sleep faster than my other machines (or not putting them to sleep at all). This is strange because the USB port is clearly still getting power, and clearly you can "connect" to the Pixhawk because there is a tty connection available, but somehow the link is down. 

The fix was simply this: Modify grub to not put the USB ports to sleep. 

Specifically, this file: 

`/etc/default/grub`

I modified the line:

`GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX_DEFAULT="quiet splash"`

to read: 

`GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX_DEFAULT="quiet splash usbcore.autosuspend=-1"`

Then you 

```
sudo update-grub
sudo reboot
```

and viola...
Oh wow, tricky! Nice detective work and thanks for following up and providing a workaround!

@julianoes I did notice one strange thing when debugging the udev rules... some places in the docs mention the pixhawk vendor ID as 26ac (if memory serves me right), but when I was debugging the USB logs, I saw 3185. Do you know why there is a discrepancy? 

Also, if memory serves me right, the Ardupilot examples would crash when I tried to set the rate. Maybe I can reflash the Ardupilot firmware tomorrow to double check, but it wasn't working out the box. I believe I calibrated the sensors in QGC.

So the message requested is [HIGHRES_IMU](https://mavlink.io/en/messages/common.html#HIGHRES_IMU), which is 105, and that's answered with `No ap_message for mavlink id (105)` here:
https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/blob/36ffe42f01b3789d6351039264405d936f18b5bd/libraries/GCS_MAVLink/GCS_Common.cpp#L2831

So it looks like HIGHRES_IMU is not in the list supported to get at a certain rate? I wouldn't know...

title: Create MAVSDK Logo
author: hamishwillee
body:
We need to have a new logo (and tagline) for the MAVSDK.

This should share "common design language" with MAVLink logo, and possibly both should be updated.

If this logo has a "tagline" included (like the current MAVLink logo, then this will have to be chosen

There are some discussions of this in #749 - e.g.:
https://github.com/Dronecode/DronecodeSDK/issues/749#issuecomment-494126762
https://github.com/Dronecode/DronecodeSDK/issues/749#issuecomment-493264694

answer_comments.body: I think all of these are just confusing and not to the point. If we update it, it should say what it is doing. It also doesn't make sense to me that the TLA is SDK and then the tagline says something else - if there is any tagline, then it needs to be software development kit.

I would really vote for "no tagline".

I believe that "drone SDKs" are now quite known. People will refer to the "DJI SDK" and the "Parrot SDK". So I don't feel a need to explain further what a "drone SDK" is. The fact that it looks similar to the MAVLink logo is probably enough for people who know MAVLink, and people who don't know MAVLink would not understand the tagline anyway, right? :sweat_smile:

title: TCP connection drop causes high CPU usage
author: fklabach
body:
I connected DroneCore to a TCP server using `add_tcp_connection()`. If the added TCP connection drops, DroneCore will just spin in `receive()` of `TcpConnection`, because `recv()` returns immediately with 0. This causes 100% CPU load and shouldn't be desired behavior when the socket is disconnected.

I've fixed the issue by just setting `_should_exit` flag when `recv()` returns with 0 in receive thread. Certainly not the best solution but does the job for me. The dead connection still stays in DroneCore's connection list, so it would be nice if it could either be reopened manually through API or DroneCore tries to keep up connections itself.

body:
Hi @julianoes 

I found https://discuss.px4.io/t/is-it-possible-to-set-other-flight-modes-stabilized-hold-etc/17338/2 and would like to follow up here, in the context of MAVSDK.

I was looking for the same functionality and I think I have a use case: when I am in mission mode and I pause the mission, the flight mode is implicitly put into Hold. And that means that the drone will return to the location where it was when pause was issued, and it will turn around too.

I want to go into Position flight mode and accept that the drone is not exactly in the location where the pause cmd was issued. For me, it's not an issue to back up a bit manually after the mission has been paused.

Raymond

title: Who should initiate TIMESYNC?
author: JonasVautherin
body:
This is related to #1169. Looking at MAVSDK's timesync implementation, it seems like we send TIMESYNC messages in two situations:

1. In `process_timesync`, where we receive a TIMESYNC message and answer to it
2. In `do_work`, where we actually initiate the TIMESYNC exchange

Is it meant to be like this, or do different components have different needs? E.g. the "master" (I would guess the autopilot) could be the one initiating the sync, and he other components may or may not answer depending on their needs, right?

@irsdkv: your insights would be appreciated :slightly_smiling_face:!
resolution_evidence: thread converges on a working answer

answer_comments.body:
> please say why this is a problem to save this functionality enabled by default?

Because it's not clear to me how TIMESYNC supports more than 2 components doing the synchronization. Hence, if you have more than 2 components, I'm currently assuming that you will have to disable TIMESYNC in the extra ones, and you will have to know which one needs to enable it. In that case, it seems more legit to have it disabled by default IMO.

My reasoning is the following: the TIMESYNC message is a broadcast message (because it doesn't have `target_system` and `target_component`). Therefore, a component cannot know who the message was destined to. So if you have, say, the FCU synchronizing with a module M1 on the companion, and at the same time a module M2 on the companion synchronizing with the ground station, then I can't imagine how the FCU can make the difference between the response coming from M1 (which it is interested in) and the response coming from the ground station (which is destined to M2).

@AlexisTM Yes. There is a little discussion of this message here: https://github.com/mavlink/mavlink-devguide/issues/194#issuecomment-512037079

And one day I will find time to document it.
I would vote that we make this feature opt-in for use cases where it is required, and supported.
Ok, that answers my question, and TIMESYNC is now disabled by default in MAVSDK. Closing this.

comments.body:
This is the same implementation as in MAVROS:

For the FCU to sync, the FCU sends a message and waits for the onboard computer to answer.
For the onboard computer to sync, it sends a message and waits for the FCU's answer.

This could be in tri-way protocol two-way, where the onboard computer sends a request, FCU replies and the onboard answers to the FCU. The onboard computer will have its sync from the 2 first messages, the FCU from the 3 last messages. This would remove one message but add one time to the TIMESYNC message. I do not know it would improve bandwidth.

https://github.com/mavlink/mavros/blob/de9f39a719b091b8448214a17d27b3b1c415d0dc/mavros/src/plugins/sys_time.cpp#L334-L346


Precision Time Protocol 2: [NOT PX4's version]
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/6976744/90625099-59fc7b00-e219-11ea-8277-8522f899d45d.png)

Oh it was a long time ago and unfortunately I don't remember all important details now :(

But @AlexisTM explanation is correct.

Also I would to say that [this code change](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/pull/1169/files#diff-ec4205b6bc1adbc844894d870f234adaR9) disables ability to answer to `TIMESYNC` requests from other devices in common with disabling MAVSDK's own requests.

I think that it is a good idea to save the opportunity to sync time by default in case of other device want to do it.

What are you think about that, @AlexisTM ?

UPD:
Also I think that disabling by default MAVSDK's initiated timesync is not a bad idea, because it is needed only for positioning using external vision for now as I know.

I am personally not using MAVSDK at the moment.

But indeed, it would make sense to have it disabled by default as only experienced users make use offboard control and need Timesync.
If the user uses advanced functions, I would either auto-enable timesync or give a feedback that timesync is not enabled and should for advanced usage. (advanced usage would be offboard control or external vision)

I checked out #1034 and found that it is only way to disable `do_work` and `process_timesync` both simultaneously.

And as @AlexisTM said this functionality really needed only for advanced usage.

So this PR seems like a good choice.

But @JonasVautherin please say why this is a problem to save this functionality enabled by default? Is it add payload or brings some other troubles?

> please say why this is a problem to save this functionality enabled by default?

Because it's not clear to me how TIMESYNC supports more than 2 components doing the synchronization. Hence, if you have more than 2 components, I'm currently assuming that you will have to disable TIMESYNC in the extra ones, and you will have to know which one needs to enable it. In that case, it seems more legit to have it disabled by default IMO.

My reasoning is the following: the TIMESYNC message is a broadcast message (because it doesn't have `target_system` and `target_component`). Therefore, a component cannot know who the message was destined to. So if you have, say, the FCU synchronizing with a module M1 on the companion, and at the same time a module M2 on the companion synchronizing with the ground station, then I can't imagine how the FCU can make the difference between the response coming from M1 (which it is interested in) and the response coming from the ground station (which is destined to M2).

@JonasVautherin I fully agree, this protocol was designed out of necessity for a time synchronization between two devices to allow better control. 

I believe it is useless in most of the use-cases and instead will be a problem to the user if multiple endpoints are connected.

TIMESYNC only works if:
* There are **only** two devices
* The synchronization time is computed & filtered in **each** receiving end (the pixhawk for vision estimation input & the computer for position output)
* The link should be high speed with low jitter, probably only using hardware serial (USB-Serial has up to 20ms spikes)

@AlexisTM Yes. There is a little discussion of this message here: https://github.com/mavlink/mavlink-devguide/issues/194#issuecomment-512037079

And one day I will find time to document it.
I would vote that we make this feature opt-in for use cases where it is required, and supported.
Ok, that answers my question, and TIMESYNC is now disabled by default in MAVSDK. Closing this.

title: RC_Status and mavlink remote health
author: aminballoon
body:
MAVSDK `RcStatus` will return `is_available = False` while autopilot has can't be armed

[PX4 manualControlCheck.cpp](https://github.com/aminballoon/PX4-Autopilot/blob/v1.15.0-alpha1/src/modules/commander/HealthAndArmingChecks/checks/manualControlCheck.cpp)

In this case if **Kill switch engaged** *RCStatus::is_available will be False** by this Flag


[RC_OK Flag check](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/2304566ad9d1b7aa98bf0f12baee5f7151613589/src/mavsdk/plugins/telemetry/telemetry_impl.cpp#L1029-L1030C87) ``` const bool rc_ok = sys_status.onboard_control_sensors_health & MAV_SYS_STATUS_SENSOR_RC_RECEIVER; ```

In my opinion, when the kill switch is engaged, it doesn't mean that the RC is not available; it's available, but it just can't be armed.

The `rc_ok` Flag should not be check only MAV_SYS_STATUS_SENSOR_RC_RECEIVER or I need to contribute manualControlCheck in PX4 . 

I can add proto [Mavlink RC_CHANNELS_RAW](https://mavlink.io/en/messages/common.html#:~:text=UINT8_MAX%3A%20invalid/unknown.-,RC_CHANNELS_RAW,-(35)) for check the latest RC input by Timestamp and solve this issue.
What do you think about this issue and my solution ?

set(ENV{CMAKE_POLICY_VERSION_MINIMUM} 3.13)
```
or run configuration like:

env CMAKE_POLICY_VERSION_MINIMUM=3.16 cmake -S . -B buld
```

title: MAVSDK connection freezes when using mavsdk_server_win32.exe when using python subprocess with stdout=subprocess.PIPE
author: SabrCat
body:
I've been having a strange issue: On windows I run a mission planner SITL simulation to which I connect with mavsdk_server and then talk to via python. If and only if stdout=subprocess.PIPE is set in the launch command and the mission planner simulation is started **after** mavsdk_server was started waiting for connection, the incoming packets freeze after exactly 13 seconds. 

#### Reproduction steps
- Tested on Windows 10.0.19045 with pycharm 2024.2.4 community
- Download mavsdk_server_win32.exe https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/releases/download/v3.6.0/mavsdk_server_win32.exe (version 3.6.0) into the folder of my example script
- Run my example script
- Open mission planner, start a plane SITL simulation with stable
- Press CTRL-F -> Mavlink -> Set up forwarding to UDP Outbound 14552 127.0.0.1 with write access on
- Observe that the script starts printing position packets for some seconds, often exactly 13, then stops permanently. 
- Relaunch the script unchanged and observe it now continuously prints data as it was launched after a SITL connection was immediately available

This issue does not occur if the stdout line is not set. This however makes mavsdk print into the normal python console. 

I have confirmed this issue exists with the following combinations of versions:
mavsdk-python / mavsdk_server
3.5 / 3.6
3.6 / 3.6
3.6 / 3.7.2

example script:
```py
import asyncio
import subprocess
from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import List

from mavsdk import System


@dataclass
class Settings:
    mavlink_vehicle_address: str
    mavsdk_server_file_name: str
    mavsdk_server_port: int


async def telemetry_worker(drone: System, stream_name: str) -> None:
    async for msg in getattr(drone.telemetry, stream_name)():
        print(msg)


async def main(settings: Settings, selected_streams: List[str]) -> None:
    with subprocess.Popen(
            [settings.mavsdk_server_file_name,
             f"-p {settings.mavsdk_server_port}",
             settings.mavlink_vehicle_address],
            stdout=subprocess.PIPE  # if this is uncommented, mavsdk really likes to freeze up.
    ) as mavsdk_server_process:
        await  asyncio.sleep(2)

        drone = System(mavsdk_server_address="localhost", port=50051)
        await drone.connect()
        print("connected")
        tasks = [
            asyncio.create_task(telemetry_worker(drone, s))
            for s in selected_streams
        ]
        await asyncio.gather(*tasks)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    settings_ = Settings(
        mavlink_vehicle_address="udp://:14552",
        mavsdk_server_file_name="mavsdk_server_win32.exe",
        mavsdk_server_port=50051
    )
    # possible streams can be found at https://mavsdk.mavlink.io/main/en/cpp/guide/telemetry.html
    streams = [
        "position",
        # "fixedwing_metrics",
        # "raw_imu",
        # "battery",
        # "armed",
        # "attitude_euler",
        # "flight_mode", # not compatible with ardupilot flight modes
        # "health",
        # "rc_status"

    ]

    asyncio.run(main(settings_, streams))

```

title: Failed to compile custom app on Mac
author: mzahana
body:
Hi,

I compiled the SDK on Mac OS (Sierra) and did system-wide install. However there is no `sudo ldconfig` (which is used on Linux to update the linker cache) in Mac. **What is the equivalent way to do it in Mac?**

I also followed the sdk guide (https://sdk.dronecode.org/en/guide/toolchain.html) in order to compile a custom C++ app, and created a custom app and the corresponding CMakeLists.txt.

However, when I run `make`, I get,
```bash
[ 50%] Building CXX object CMakeFiles/formation_gs.dir/formation_gs.cpp.o
/Users/abdkadma/Desktop/src/DroneCode_apps/formation_gs.cpp:15:10: fatal error:
      'dronecode_sdk/action.h' file not found
#include <dronecode_sdk/action.h>
         ^~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
1 error generated.
make[2]: *** [CMakeFiles/formation_gs.dir/formation_gs.cpp.o] Error 1
make[1]: *** [CMakeFiles/formation_gs.dir/all] Error 2
make: *** [all] Error 2
```

So, what could be the problem here? Is it because the linker cache is not updated?

comments.body:
Issue is solved by specifying the include and lib system directories in the CMakeLists.txt.

Would the tutorials need to be updated in order to account for this?

```bash
if(NOT MSVC)
    add_definitions("-std=c++11 -Wall -Wextra -Werror")
    include_directories(/usr/local/include)
    link_directories(/usr/local/lib)
else()
    add_definitions("-std=c++11 -WX -W2")
    include_directories(${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/../../install/include)
    link_directories(${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/../../install/lib)
endif()
```
Also, I would like to mention that I used the `develop` branch.

> Also, I would like to mention that I used the develop branch.

That is the correct branch to use. Develop is for ongoing development, master is for the last official release.

Regarding the install directories, did you install dronecode system wide or locally?  If you installed locally, then you do need to tell the system where the includes are: https://sdk.dronecode.org/en/guide/toolchain.html#sdk_local_install
My understanding is that if you installed system wide you shouldn't have to. 

IF you did and this is needed then yes, we will have to update a bunch of things, including test scripts and docs.

> So, what could be the problem here? Is it because the linker cache is not updated?

If an include file is not found, the include directories are wrong. This has nothing to do with the linker.

> However there is no sudo ldconfig (which is used on Linux to update the linker cache) in Mac. What is the equivalent way to do it in Mac?

https://stackoverflow.com/questions/1451047/ldconfig-equivalent-in-mac-os-x

It is common practice that in development libraries are installed to `/usr/local/lib` and `/usr/local/include`.

I tried to address your confusion in https://github.com/dronecore/sdk_docs/pull/136.
Please re-open if this is still a problem.

title: Intermittent issue of all gimbal control erroring with Pixy LR gimbal
author: jnomikos
body:
~~From my experience, MAVSDK does not detect a system is lost on soft reboot. Which is fine for most things I am doing. camera_server, param, and mavlink_passthrough seem to work fine for me even after the soft reboot.~~

~~The problem is that gimbal does not work after the reboot. Giving any gimbal control after soft rebooting will result in a failure to do so, with it returning the result as "Error". ~~

~~My assumption is that MAVSDK still thinks it has control of the gimbal, when it doesn't, since it did not know the autopilot was rebooted. I am not able to make it so that MAVSDK detects reboots, even if I increase BRD_BOOT_DELAY. 
In my application, this will be fine, because I have a background thread that detects when we last received telemetry position, so I can use that to detect a reboot, but I still wanted to make an issue here, just to give a heads up of the issue I found.~~



System:

MAVSDK v3.2.0
ArduCopter 4.5.6
Pixy LR gimbal

Note: MAVSDK is connected to flight controller via UART



**Edit:**

I fixed this issue. The problem was not due to rebooting.

The Pixy LR gimbal sends GIMBAL_MANAGER messages from comp id 154 and the autopilot sends GIMBAL_MANAGER messages from comp id 1. I hard coded MAVSDK to completely ignore comp id 154 and the intermittent problem is gone. 

As a note, it would constantly request GIMBAL_MANAGER_INFORMATION from 1/154. I know MAVSDK has a retries mechanism, but it didn't seem to stop this. So my hardcoding got rid of that.

title: unix_epoch_time subscription not working in C++ and Python
author: LarsLeferenz
body:
Hello, 

I'm currently trying to sync time between an external application and my mavlink device in C++. To do this I'm trying to subscribe to the "unix_epoch_time" telemetry.
Sadly, the callback is never called. To explore the issue, I also created a simple python script to display the telemetry message:
```python
import asyncio
from mavsdk import System

async def run():
    # Connect to the MAVSDK system
    system = System(mavsdk_server_address='localhost', port=50051)
    await system.connect()

    await system.telemetry.set_rate_unix_epoch_time(1)
    # Subscribe to time updates
    async for time in system.telemetry.unix_epoch_time():
        print(f"Time: {time}")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    asyncio.run(run())
```
Python isn't outputting anything. The Mavsdk server output is as follows:
```
PS C:\Users\Lars\Downloads> .\mavsdk_server_win32.exe -p 50051 serial://COM5:57600
[04:46:05|Info ] MAVSDK version: v1.4.17 (D:\a\MAVSDK\MAVSDK\src\mavsdk\core\mavsdk_impl.cpp:20)
[04:46:05|Info ] Waiting to discover system on serial://COM5:57600... (D:\a\MAVSDK\MAVSDK\src\mavsdk_server\src\connection_initiator.h:20)
[04:46:05|Debug] New: System ID: 1 Comp ID: 1 (D:\a\MAVSDK\MAVSDK\src\mavsdk\core\mavsdk_impl.cpp:496)
[04:46:05|Debug] Component Autopilot (1) added. (D:\a\MAVSDK\MAVSDK\src\mavsdk\core\system_impl.cpp:377)
[04:46:05|Warn ] Vehicle type changed (new type: 2, old type: 0) (D:\a\MAVSDK\MAVSDK\src\mavsdk\core\system_impl.cpp:225)
[04:46:05|Debug] Discovered 1 component(s) (D:\a\MAVSDK\MAVSDK\src\mavsdk\core\system_impl.cpp:578)
[04:46:05|Info ] System discovered (D:\a\MAVSDK\MAVSDK\src\mavsdk_server\src\connection_initiator.h:63)
[04:46:05|Info ] Server started (D:\a\MAVSDK\MAVSDK\src\mavsdk_server\src\grpc_server.cpp:53)
[04:46:05|Info ] Server set to listen on 0.0.0.0:50051 (D:\a\MAVSDK\MAVSDK\src\mavsdk_server\src\grpc_server.cpp:54)
```

I also looked into the mavlink messages through QGroundControl and I am receiving SYSTEM_TIME and TIME_SYNC messages:
![image](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/assets/37025379/a0c608df-fd3e-4bc4-8e1e-6f7f240e3548)

My FC is a Cube Orange running PX4 v1.14 connected via USB. I'm using mavsdk-python 1.4.9., mavsdk-server 1.4.17 and I my C++ solution utilized v1.4.16.

I should also mention that I don't have a GPS connected at the moment.

Am I using unix_epoch_time wrong or do I have to set a parameter in PX4 perhaps?
resolution_evidence: maintainer points at the fix: 'Fixed with #2294'

answer_comments.body:
It looks like the `UnixEpochTime` method is based on [UTM_GLOBAL_POSITION](https://mavlink.io/en/messages/common.html#UTM_GLOBAL_POSITION).time.

https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/v1.4/src/mavsdk/plugins/telemetry/telemetry_impl.cpp#L1328-L1343

So this probably means it only works with GPS working.

Are you trying to get UTC time, or boot time? I assume UTC?
