title: Building with a non-default dialect is broken?
author: reedev
body:
Hi,

As an example, I am trying to build current main branch (also tried v3.15.0 with same outcome) on Linux (for the record Debian 13 on x86_64) via

cmake -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug -DMAVLINK_DIALECT=development -Bbuild -S.
cmake --build build -j8

and it's broken with errors that mavlink messages are unknown, e.g. MAVLINK_MSG_ID_REMOTE_LOG_DATA_BLOCK

Am I now supposed to build in a different way?

In general, when creating a custom dialect, I use a similar way as the development.xml and therefore only include common.xml. Is this the usual way to do it?

Thanks, best regards,
Raymond

answer_comments.body:
Oh thanks for the issue. I realize now that we now depend on ardupilotmega.xml messages for ArduPilot log streaming support: https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/pull/2728/changes#diff-1e7de1ae2d059d21e1dd75d5812d5a34b0222cef273b7c3a2af62eb747f9d20a.

For now, you either have to include ardupilotmega.xml in your dialect, or you disable the log streaming plugin by removing it from this list: https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/main/cpp/src/plugins.txt#L19

Maybe in the future, I could just do an ifdef if the messages are available, and disable ArduPilot log streaming otherwise.

author: nickatblueflite
body:

Using the code out of the logfile_download.py example I have no trouble downloading the full set of files with a serial connection.

In fact, the "connection" goes down fully and the only way to reconnect is to reboot the pix. I've run the mavsdk_server manually to watch its output and the only thing that happens is the heartbeats timed out message appears and then nothing.

The connection seems stable otherwise and works well when using mavlink-router to forward to a GCS over the network.

> 10.223.129.101 is the Jetson, 10.223.129.102 is the pixhawk

So it looks like there is also 10.223.129.103 and all traffic is forwarded to that one. Not sure if that matters or not, but does it also happen without that forwarding on?

The only thing I see is that the MAVLink UDP receiver goes to 0 CPU, so presumably it stops receiving anything.

> `1127 mavlink_rcv_if1                 0  0.000  2732/ 5976 175 (175)  w:sem  5`

I have found an interesting new failure mode that takes mavsdk out of the loop (I think).

Pix -> eth udp to Jetson -> mavlink-router to Halo LTE Network (udp) -> Halo Mavlink Forward to Local computer over VPN udp -> Local QGC -> QGC log download

Logs start to download but eventually stall and require pix restart

Unless Halo is using mavsdk or QGC? 

Still working on a setup without the jetson in between

More success modes:

Pix -> eth to macOS -> QGC log download WORKS
Pix -> eth to macOS -> mavsdk based log download WORKS

It's starting to really seem like its an issue with the Jetson networking setup/stack

Finally got Wireshark w/ MAVLINK hooked up. When the stall happens the Jetson continually sends out LOG_REQUEST_DATA packets but gets no response from the pix, in fact, the pix stops sending anything at all. Does this sound like its actually a PX4 issue?? 10.223.129.101 is the Jetson, 10.223.129.102 is the pixhawk
Interesting! So what's the last response by the Pixhawk that you see? Or what's the first message that triggers the Pixhawk to stop?

[wireshark full jetson setup fail capture.pcapng.zip](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/files/11931672/wireshark.full.jetson.setup.fail.capture.pcapng.zip)

Here is the full wireshark capture. You can see the LOG_DATA and LOG_REQUEST_DATA going back and forth normally for a while, then the LOG_DATA decrease and the LOG_REQUEST_DATA increase until eventually the LOG_DATA messages stop coming.

I've been trying  dome PX4 builds with some PX4_WARNs in various places to see where if the LOG_REQUEST_DATA messages are coming through the stack and so far I have been able to determine that the Mavlink Receiver is not seeing the anything on the fds in the MavlinkReceiver::run() loop.

```c
int ret = poll(&fds[0], 1, timeout);
```

ret is always 0 after the stall happens, so it looks like the issue is deeper in the network stack? I don't even know where to begin to look into that...

Ok, I'm having a look at the wireshark dump, thanks for that.

Random thought: does it also happen when remote and local port numbers are not the same? They generally don't have to be, and I'm wondering if that could cause problems somewhere.

> 10.223.129.101 is the Jetson, 10.223.129.102 is the pixhawk

So it looks like there is also 10.223.129.103 and all traffic is forwarded to that one. Not sure if that matters or not, but does it also happen without that forwarding on?

> I don't even know where to begin to look into that...

Neither. I never had to look into the NuttX network stack so far.

This would be a start: https://cwiki.apache.org/confluence/display/NUTTX/Networking

> Random thought: does it also happen when remote and local port numbers are not the same? They generally don't have to be, and I'm wondering if that could cause problems somewhere.

It does happen with different port numbers.

> So it looks like there is also 10.223.129.103 and all traffic is forwarded to that one. Not sure if that matters or not, but does it also happen without that forwarding on?

It does happen without this as well.

> This would be a start: https://cwiki.apache.org/confluence/display/NUTTX/Networking

Will see what I can find. Do you know who might be most familiar with this part of the stack that I could reach out to?
When it comes to NuttX, that would be @davids5.

One more interesting data point, I was able to replicate the issue on an older Jetson Nano as well, except on the Nano it runs much much longer before it stalls. And interestingly it maintains a faster and much more consistent download speed while it is working.
I ran into the same(?) issue and diagnosed it be in the NuttX networking stack. I reported it [here](https://github.com/apache/nuttx/issues/17299).
Can you try with #2654
This is likely fixed with #2654. For me, the loopback UDP buffer overflowed because PX4 sends too much at once.

title: Zoom Support missing (Camera/Gimbal)
author: petergerten
body:
Is there support for zoom (e.g. Yuneec E90 digital zoom or Yuneec E30Z optical zoom) already?
I could not find it so far and even on raw MAVLink level this seems to be very unclear how to do.
https://developer.yuneec.com/documentation/125/Supported-mavlink-messages does not mention it either.

answer_comments.body: @darioxz would be great if you could update all xmls to what is released by Yuneec.

I can download the file from http. However, we had disabled that in order to support the H520 G where the Swift app connects via MFi to the controller and http was not exposed through MFi.

The correct way to deal with this would be to use MAVLink FTP. MAVSDK supports it and also has code for the server side which could serve as inspiration for the camera side.

> The correct way to deal with this would be to use MAVLink FTP. MAVSDK supports it and also has code for the server side which could serve as inspiration for the camera side.

So the drone would give an URI like `mavftp://`, and MAVSDK would know that it should get it using mavlink ftp, right? And the drone could still give `http://`, and MAVSDK could download it over HTTP. Is that correct?

comments.body:
It's currently not supported. And I'm not sure if the E30Z is supported at all.

There is a MAVLink message: [MAV_CMD_SET_CAMERA_ZOOM](https://mavlink.io/en/messages/common.html#MAV_CMD_SET_CAMERA_ZOOM) but I'm not sure if that one is already implemented on the H520 side.

Let me ping @darioxz, he might know more.

Generally I agree that it would we worthwhile to add zoom to the camera plugin.

@julianoes I already tried to send the MAV_CMD_SET_CAMERA_ZOOM message, but could not make it work yet.
I was thinking of sniffing the MAVLink traffic between remote control and H520 camera - but as this is probably not intended to be a secret by Yuneec I wanted to ask here :)
It definitely makes sense to ask here! :smile: Unfortunately, I don't remember. @dogmaphobic do you remember how to set zoom for H520?
@petergerten I would assume it works the same way. I will try to obtain an updated XML for the E90 (and other cameras).

If it doesn't work, try the following parameter:
```
        <parameter name="CAM_ZOOM" type="uint32" control="0">
            <description>Camera Zoom</description>
        </parameter>
```
It needs to be added in the E90.xml file. I am sorry for the lousy documentation. 

... and don't forget the generator after changing the xml.

> @dogmaphobic do you remember how to set zoom for H520?

Yup, @darioxz already responded above. It's done using parameters. Zoom support for the Yuneec cameras came before there were any zoom commands in MAVLink. For simple zoom control (zoom in/out), the commands work fine. If you need precise zoom control (change optical focal length to 75mm or digital zoom to 1.25X for example), that can only be done using parameters. I don't remember how the E90 handled zoom (it has a fixed focal length lens).
@darioxz would be great if you could update all xmls to what is released by Yuneec.

@julianoes Jep, I will try to get them. 

Does the SDK still have the capability of downloading the camera definition files directly from the camera?

I can download the file from http. However, we had disabled that in order to support the H520 G where the Swift app connects via MFi to the controller and http was not exposed through MFi.

The correct way to deal with this would be to use MAVLink FTP. MAVSDK supports it and also has code for the server side which could serve as inspiration for the camera side.

> The correct way to deal with this would be to use MAVLink FTP. MAVSDK supports it and also has code for the server side which could serve as inspiration for the camera side.

So the drone would give an URI like `mavftp://`, and MAVSDK would know that it should get it using mavlink ftp, right? And the drone could still give `http://`, and MAVSDK could download it over HTTP. Is that correct?
@darioxz Sorry, but unfortunately I don't have access to a Z30 anymore to test it. I am going to test 'digital zoom' with a E90 though.
Fixed in #2094.

title: Missing stropts.h is stopping the installation of  cURL
author: shrit
body:
Hello,

Since glibc version 2.30, `stropts.h` has been removed. At the same time, this curl version should not require stropts.h to exist as described in the source code https://github.com/curl/curl/blob/28b5b1c20a7f38b079b8828d06423d4b7a3ed439/lib/if2ip.c#L46. 
```
/meta/MAVSDK/build/default/third_party/curl/curl/src/curl/lib/if2ip.c:47:12: fatal error: stropts.h: No such file or directory
   47 | #  include <stropts.h>
      |            ^~~~~~~~~~~
```
This is blocking the entire installation of MAVSDK on Arch Linux.

answer_comments.body: I'm on Arch Linux, I have glibc 2.30, and curl builds without an issue for me :thinking:. Do you have an idea how I could reproduce?

It builds fine for me, and I'm on latest Arch Linux and I do not have `stropts.h` on my system either.

The place where it fails for you it actually has a define if `stropts.h` is available:

https://github.com/curl/curl/blob/curl-7_67_0/lib/if2ip.c#L46-L48

and the configure step correctly determines that for me:
```
-- Looking for 41 include files stdio.h, ..., stropts.h
-- Looking for 41 include files stdio.h, ..., stropts.h - not found
```

Have you tried wiping the `build` folder and trying fresh?

title: Get a vector of systems
author: mzahana
resolution_evidence: thread converges on a working answer

answer_comments.body:
If something is automated in software UUID is more "convenient" because you it's unique.

I suggest you implement the method to get all system IDs yourself since you're already changed the API to work with system IDs instead of UUIDs.

> @julianoes Would exposing get_system_id in system.cpp do any harm?

I guess it doesn't :smile:, so we might as well add it.
This has been added, see: https://mavsdk.mavlink.io/develop/en/cpp/api_changes.html#v0330

linked_issues.title: what is DroneCores's uuid with multiple vehicles?

comments.body:
You should be able to get all system like described here:
https://sdk.dronecode.org/en/guide/connections.html#iterating-all-systems

However, for now you need to make sure yourself that all vehicles have different system IDs.
@mzahana is it not possible to use the UUIDs?

If something is automated in software UUID is more "convenient" because you it's unique.

I suggest you implement the method to get all system IDs yourself since you're already changed the API to work with system IDs instead of UUIDs.

@julianoes Would exposing [get_system_id](https://github.com/Dronecode/DronecodeSDK/blob/develop/core/system_impl.cpp#L518) in [system.cpp](https://github.com/Dronecode/DronecodeSDK/blob/develop/core/system.cpp) do any harm?

> @julianoes Would exposing get_system_id in system.cpp do any harm?

I guess it doesn't :smile:, so we might as well add it.
Work in progress here: #694.
This has been added, see: https://mavsdk.mavlink.io/develop/en/cpp/api_changes.html#v0330

The current Makefile is sort of a wrapper script around cmake and that's a bit confusing.

Especially annoying is actually the hard-coded `-j8` argument for make. It would be better if this was taken from the CPU count or your settings for make (`MAKEFLAGS`).

https://github.com/Dronecode/DronecodeSDK/blob/ef45e4ddb7a8c5dcd0ac20df9a330afdaa9a7be6/Makefile#L22

title: How to connect a drone using system id with mavsdk
author: Kutbip
body:
Hello Everyone,

I am using MAVSDK-Java to monitoring drones.
Currently, MAVSDK java only exposes to connect drones using UDP or TCP which is working perfectly.
Now, to connect with multiple drones, the app requires connecting using the system id which I am not able to do.

Later I came to know that the C++ library can do the task.
I have tried to build a C++ library  [here](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK.git) to use with Android, but I can't make a build due to some errors. followed as per the documentation.

So the questions are 
1. Can I achieve the above(connect the drone with system id) using C++ lib.
2. Can I get the .so file of this C++ lib so that I can use it in android through JNI.

FYR: @JonasVautherin @julianoes

answer_comments.body:
What about using MAVSDK-Java, but running multiple instances of `MavsdkServer`? Say one that listens on UDP:14540, and one that listens on UDP:14541. Then your two drones should broadcast on 14540 and 14541 respectively.

I am personally not a big fan of having all the drones connecting to the app on 14540, to be honest. IMO, on the app side, it should be "one drone, one socket", and my suggestion above does exactly that :+1:.

> Is there any way with mavsdk java?

No, there isn't. We would need to discuss how we would want to expose that. I know that not everybody has the same opinion as I do, but I would push for doing what I suggested above, and if there was the need for a discovery protocol, I would do that separately, and not by sending everything on the same UDP port on the client :see_no_evil:.
Do you have a fixed number of drones in the real environment, or do you have "n drones" and you don't know how many at build time?

> Not a fixed number of drones but we have a max of 5-6 drones.

The solutions I see (none of which is straightforward):

1. Using MAVSDK-Java: implement a discovery protocol, have your app discover the drones and their UDP port, and start one `MavsdkServer` instance for each drone
2. Using MAVSDK-Java: let the user enter the UDP ports for each drone manually and create a `MavsdkServer` instance for each
3. Use MAVSDK-C++ and its multi-systems feature

title: Issue with SITL Arming
author: eanmikale
body:
Getting the following errors running Python3.7 on Ubuntu 16.04. I believe it is a porting issue. Any assistance would be appreciated. 

await drone.action.arm()
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.7/site-packages/aioconsole-0.1.16.dev0-py3.7.egg/aioconsole/execute.py", line 95, in aexec
    result, new_local = yield from coro
  File "<aexec>", line 2, in __corofn
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.7/site-packages/mavsdk/generated/action.py", line 167, in arm
    raise ActionError(result, "arm()")
mavsdk.generated.action.ActionError: COMMAND_DENIED_LANDED_STATE_UNKNOWN: 'Command denied, landed state is unknown'; origin: arm(); params: ()

answer_comments.body:
> COMMAND_DENIED_LANDED_STATE_UNKNOWN

I would say that the system is just not ready, i.e. we don't know yet the "landed state" of the drone. What if you wait a bit and try again?

> I believe it is a porting issue.

Nope, it's just an error message because you cannot arm in this state :wink:. Just like you would get an error message if you tried to arm while the drone is flying, or if a command timed out because of a bad connection.

You can just `try... catch` it if you want, and e.g. retry later.

title: Choosing reference over pointer
author: shakthi-prashanth-m
body:
It is recommended to use references when we can, and pointers when we have to.
(Reference: https://isocpp.org/wiki/faq/references#refs-vs-ptrs)

We can replace `Device *_parent` to `Device & _parent` as I see that, its possible. We initialize while activating plugin and never modify it. Also, we have a method (below) that actually gives, **a reference to a device**, not pointer. 
```cpp
Device &device(uint64_t uuid);
```

Consider, below piece of application code:
```cpp
Device &device = dc.device(); // we get reference to device
auto action = std::make_shared<Action>(&device); // why pass its address ?

// Why not pass it as-is?
auto action = std::make_shared<Action>(device);
```
I just noticed this.
@julianoes, was it done intentionally for some vital reason? If not, then we can find similar usages and replace them properly.

The range in the switch...case statement goes from 1 to 6 while the range of the module function (index % 6) goes from 0 to 5.
So, param6 will never be set and if (index==6), then param7 will be equal to 1 and the whole command will be ignored by PX4 [handle_message_command_both](https://github.com/PX4/PX4-Autopilot/blob/1c8ab2a0d7db2d14a6f320ebd8766b5ffaea28fa/src/modules/mavlink/mavlink_receiver.cpp#L557) function.

If I understood correctly, at the moment PX4 only pays attention to 3 AUX outputs, namely param1, param2 and param3... so this bug should not have any effect on the whole system behavior.

```
    func uploadMission(){
        let cancelMissionUploadRoutine =
            CoreManager.shared().drone.mission.cancelMissionUpload()
                .do(onError: { (error) in
                    print("Error canceling mission upload \(error)")
                }, onCompleted: {
                    print("Success canceling mission upload.")
                })
        
        let uploadMissionRoutine =
            CoreManager.shared().drone.mission.uploadMission(missionItems: missionExample.missionItems)
            .do(onError: { error in
                self.displayFeedback(message:"Mission uploaded failed \(error)")
                
            }, onCompleted: {
                self.displayFeedback(message:"Mission uploaded with success")
            })
                
       let uploadRoutine = cancelMissionUploadRoutine.andThen(uploadMissionRoutine)
        uploadRoutine
            .subscribeOn(SerialDispatchQueueScheduler(qos: .background))
            .observeOn(MainScheduler.instance)
            .subscribe()
            .disposed(by: disposeBag)
    }

title: How to use MAVSDK with QgroundControl
author: tbago
body:
Hi support:
I know the MAVSDK provide simple access the mavlink protocol like the following architecture：
```mermaid
flowchart LR
	MAVSDK-Python & MAVSDK-Swift-.GRPC.->MAVSDK-Server-.Mavlink protocol.->Backend
```
And I want use the MAVSDK as the following architecture:
```mermaid
flowchart LR
	QGroundControl-.Mavlink.->MAVSDK-Server-.GRPC.->Backend
```
Just like reverse the input and output protocol. Dose the **MAVSDK Server** support this architecture.
resolution_evidence: thread converges on a working answer

answer_comments.body:
I am not sure I understand your question. Typically MAVSDK is used as a ground station, to communicate with a drone (is `Backend` the drone, in your first diagram?).

If you want to connect both MAVSDK and QGC to the drone, I think the typical way is to use `mavlink-router` (there are other solutions, though). Is that what you want to do?

Or do you want to write the drone side with MAVSDK, and have QGC talk to it like it would talk to a normal drone?

Have you seen the camera server and autopilot server examples?

https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/tree/main/examples/camera_server
https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/tree/main/examples/autopilot_server
Yer, it needs some work, some things are indeed missing. Feel free to add PRs to add functionality that you find missing.
That's right! And best is to make a PR in MAVSDK-Proto first so that we can have a discussion about the API first up.

> > So if u could please guide me about how we are receiving callbacks.

linked_prs.title: Set RUNTIME DESTINATION to fix Windows install

comments.body: How did you build and install it? Can you copy the commands here?

These are the commands I used:

```
git clone https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK.git
git submodule update --init --recursive
cmake -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug -Bbuild/default -H.
runas cmake --build build/default --target install
```

After the build, in your `MAVSDK` directory, can you search for `mavsdk.dll`? Not in `C:\Program Files`, but really in the build folder (so `path/to/MAVSDK/build/default`).

Maybe the system install is not installing the DLL correctly...
mavsdk.dll is in build/default of the MAVSDK directory. Is the MAVSDK directory supposed to be inside my C++ project? That could be why it's returning this error.

> Is the MAVSDK directory supposed to be inside my C++ project? That could be why it's returning this error.

No. The right files from `build/default` should be installed on your system (in `C:\Program Files`) when you run `cmake --build build/default --target install`. It seems to me that we don't install `mavsdk.dll` correctly on Windows, which ends up in your error.
Should I try a local install and see if the mavsdk.dll can be found there?

[This](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/main/src/mavsdk/core/CMakeLists.txt#L94) is (I believe) where we say where the library should be installed. On Linux it gets into `lib/` (more specifically `lib/libmavsdk.so`, `lib/libmavsdk.so.0`, `lib/libmavsdk.so.0.50.1`).

Somehow it seems like on Windows the `.dll` (which should be the equivalent to the `.so` on Linux) is not installed correctly.
So after doing a local install I was still not able to find mavsdk.dll within the `install` directory. Only see it `build/default`.

Could you try to debug it? For instance, you could try to print `${CMAKE_INSTALL_LIBDIR}` [here](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/main/src/mavsdk/core/CMakeLists.txt#L94) to see if it looks correct on Windows. With something like:

```
message(FATAL_ERROR "CMAKE_INSTALL_LIBDIR: ${CMAKE_INSTALL_LIBDIR}")
```

I modified the CMakeLists.txt to include that line of code and was given this: ```CMake Error at src/mavsd/core/CMakeLists.txt:98 (message): CMAKE_INSTALL_LIBDIR: lib```. Not sure which "lib" directory it's referring to though.
That looks fine to me :thinking:
Do you think the previous releases have this problem? It seems like other Windows users haven't had this problem or have had the issue resolved.

https://cmake.org/cmake/help/v3.0/variable/CMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX.html

What about passing the directory where you need/want it?

```
cmake -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug -DCMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX=install -Bbuild/default -H.
cmake --build build/default --target install
```
But it seems like it's installing "stuff" already, just not that one dll :thinking:. Do you think that a local install would help?
Is it's installing it into `C:\Program Files\lib`? That would be a bit awkward. (And maybe it would not have permission to do so.)

I was assuming something like `C:\Program Files\mavsdk\lib`, but I don't know what CMake does on Windows really :sweat_smile:. However from this:

> So after doing a local install I was still not able to find mavsdk.dll within the install directory. Only see it build/default.

my understanding was that `mavsdk.dll` is not installed correctly, even locally

> mavsdk.dll within the install directory

The question is which one that is.
Although this is technically incorrect, I was able to temporarily fix the dependency problem by moving a copy of mavsdk.dll into the same directory as my project executable.
@Tzhao7 ok, do you have any suggestions what we should change? I really don't know how linking works properly on Windows.

> Also I noticed that the installed library found in C:\Program Files only contains mavsdk.lib and does not contain any .dll.

> mavsdk.dll is in build/default of the MAVSDK directory

Given [this information](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/913691/dll-and-lib-files-what-and-why):

title: Changing from offboard mode to mission mode
author: MrPrietix
body:
Hi 

I am loading a mission to the drone, then I am starting offboard mode and when it has reached an altitude I change to mission mode, these changes of different modes are done with an onboard computer. All of this is performed without the RC connected. Furthermore, the arming is done with the onboard computer. 

Nevertheless, when the drone changes to mission mode, it wants to reach a higher altitude different that the initial 5 meters specified on QGC when designing the mission. When it comes to the mission mode I am just running the `MissionRaw::Result start_mission_result = mission_raw->start_mission();` without loading any mission with mavsdk. I am supposing that when I run `MissionRaw::Result start_mission_result = mission_raw->start_mission();` the drone automatically takes the mission in the flight controller.

Can anybody help me?

answer_comments.body:
The waypoints are saved in the Autopilot, MAVSDK cannot change them without re-uploading the mission (in which case you could download it from QGC and see that the altitude changed).

> All of this is performed without the RC connected.

Are you sure the drone doesn't just go to RTL as a failsafe? To me that would explain why it gains altitude :thinking:

I was guessing an RC loss, but really I don't know. I just don't see how MAVSDK would change the mission altitude. It's not really a thing: mission items ("waypoints") are uploaded to PX4, and then when you tell PX4 to go in `mission` mode, it executes them. MAVSDK should put PX4 in mission mode just like QGC does :thinking:.

I guess my question was: are you sure that it is in mission mode, or could it be in another mode (like RTL, which is a mode that could start by gaining altitude in some situations)

Just while looking at your log I saw that [thrust correlates with your mag](https://logs.px4.io/plot_app?log=0d0df6e7-1248-495d-9a1d-67cd14af68e1#Nav-Thrust-and-Magnetic-Field) which means that you mean is too close to your power wiring or motors. I'd suggest using a GPS mast, or if you're already doing that, make sure that the external mag in the GPS board is used.

---
Now that aside, if you look at the [altitude plot](https://logs.px4.io/plot_app?log=0d0df6e7-1248-495d-9a1d-67cd14af68e1#Nav-Altitude-Estimate) you can see that it sets a altitude setpoint at around 175m (this tiny yellow circle), and then climbs to it.

My assumption is that this is really the mission you set it to. Can you show the mission that you set? E.g. the QGC mission plan file, or a screenshot of it. I would be interested in the altitude that you set, as well as the frame. Unfortunately, the mission is not logged to ulog, so I can't see that.

I'm confused. I'm looking at a plan with 2 items and a doJumpId of 2 and 3 respectively. I don't even know how this works. The altitude itself looks like just 5m for both of them.

> they created a takeoff item that does not send the takeoff command but sends the altitude to be taken into consideration during the takeoff.

I don't know how you are doing that but I would guess something is wrong with that.

Or to put it differently: you are telling me that you are doing some magic with the mission items but the altitude is not correct but you also don't actually show me in detail what you're doing so I can't really help.

title: How to arm drone without GPS
author: mjemv
body:
We are trying to do a BVLOS operation indoors, in this case we dont have a GPS lock but LTE is available.
But without GPS arming is not possible even in offboard mode.

How to get over this in MAVSDK if GPS lock is not available.

comments.body:
Hm, arming should still be possible, however, not in position control.

Offboard mode would have to be attitude control, unless you have something for a position estimate, such as flow. For BVLOS I would be convinced that you need something that helps you with position estimation indoors, otherwise this would be very hard fly.

The modes supported by the pixhawk firmware are
```
`GUIDED> mode
GUIDED> Available modes:  dict_keys(['STABILIZE', 'ACRO', 'ALT_HOLD', 'AUTO', 'GUIDED', 'LOITER', 'RTL', 'CIRCLE', 'POSITION', 'LAND', 'OF_LOITER', 'DRIFT', 'SPORT', 'FLIP', 'AUTOTUNE', 'POSHOLD', 'BRAKE', 'THROW', 'AVOID_ADSB', 'GUIDED_NOGPS', 'SMART_RTL', 'FLOWHOLD', 'FOLLOW', 'ZIGZAG', 'SYSTEMID', 'AUTOROTATE', 'AUTO_RTL'])

GUIDED> mode GUIDED_NOGPSAP: PreArm: GPS 1: Bad fix

GUIDED> Got COMMAND_ACK: DO_SET_MODE: ACCEPTED
GUIDED_NOGPS> Mode GUIDED_NOGPS
Got COMMAND_ACK: REQUEST_AUTOPILOT_CAPABILITIES: ACCEPTED
Got COMMAND_ACK: SET_MESSAGE_INTERVAL: ACCEPTED
Got COMMAND_ACK: DO_SET_MODE: ACCEPTED
GUIDED> Mode GUIDED
Got COMMAND_ACK: REQUEST_MESSAGE: ACCEPTED
Got COMMAND_ACK: DO_SET_MODE: ACCEPTED
Got COMMAND_ACK: COMPONENT_ARM_DISARM: FAILED
`
```

I had manually set GUIDED_NOGPS, but the offboad start sets it to GUIDED.
dronekit supports a GUIDED_NOGPS though...

Just note that you can't compare jMAVSim with what you have on your Pixhawk as it looks like you're using ArduPilot which is a different software from PX4.

MAVSDK mostly supports PX4 but compatibility with ArduPilot is work in progress, so you'll have to work through details and debug what doesn't work.

I have radiolink pixhawk fmuv3. While dronekit python has a GUIDED_NOGPS, which is found also in the supported modes by firmware, there is no specific non_gps mode in px4 i believe. Is offboard mode + attitude means non_gps?

Since we are trying to make a very small and realtime code that manages mavlink, we cant use python.
That was reason for choosing C++.

We have seen some issues with MAVSDK and this pixhawk, In GPS mode, sometimes the copter arms for a second and disarms for no reason 

There are now 2 ways a) use dronekit python or b) add stubs in MAVSDK.
What would it take to add compatability with fmuv3?

As @julianoes mentioned in his first comment, you are missing some sort of position estimation which could be using optical flow in indoors scenario. Without that and a proper configuration of the firmware (Ardupilot or PX4) the vehicle has no way of knowing where it is and therefore cannot go where it should. Therefore your issue seems unrelated to MAVSDK.

More info on non-GPS flights for ArduPilot: https://ardupilot.org/copter/docs/common-non-gps-navigation-landing-page.html

Similar with PX4: https://docs.px4.io/main/en/ros/external_position_estimation.html

Closing for now.

- https://docs.dronecore.io/v/develop/en/contributing/build.html#dronecore_system_wide_install
- https://docs.dronecore.io/v/develop/en/examples/#linux-error-loading-shared-libraries

If this could happen automagically as part of doing system wide installation that would be even better.
@hamishwillee  Thanks.

title: Including the SDK inside a Node C++ Addon
author: aokholm
body:
I’m trying to integrate the DronecodeSDK C++ lib into an electron (nodeJS) app.

I have had success running the offboard_velocity example. I have copied the almost all of the code from the offboard example into Nod  C++ addon. [Complete code example](https://github.com/aokholm/nodeDronecodeSDK)

I have the following std::out::

```
before running[34m[11:47:48|Info ] [0mDronecodeSDK version: 0.15.0-14-g531a55b9 (dronecode_sdk_impl.cpp:25)
Wait for system to connect via heartbeat
[34m[11:47:48|Info ] [0mNew system on: 127.0.0.1:14580 (udp_connection.cpp:225)
[32m[11:47:48|Debug] [0mNew: System ID: 1 Comp ID: 1 (dronecode_sdk_impl.cpp:338)

[32m[11:47:49|Debug] [0mDiscovered 1 component(s) (UUID: 5283920058631409231) (system_impl.cpp:548)
```

The code fails when I  try to initialise the shared `auto action = std::make_shared<Action>(system);` or `auto offboard = std::make_shared<Offboard>(system);`

`EXC_BAD_ACCESS (code=EXC_I386_GPFLT)`

Is there something I should be aware of? Any hints for further  debugging? Do you know someone who managed to integrate the SDK into a NodeJS app?
resolution_evidence: thread converges on a working answer

answer_comments.body:
Thanks for the repo with the source to reproduce this, that's really nice!

Unfortunately this does not crash on my Arch Linux. I can try reproduce it next week on the Mac at work.

Ok, I tested this and it doesn't crash on macOS either for me.

![Selection_020](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1419688/56567830-07c03100-65b6-11e9-9317-83f943b783f7.png)

One thing I noticed is that in order to run it I needed to set the path where the libs are to link to:
```
export LD_LIBRARY_PATH=./lib/DronecodeSDK/install/lib
```
Otherwise it did not find `libdronecode_sdk_*.so/dylib`.

Could it be that you are loading libraries that you have previously installed in your system, e.g. in `/usr/lib/` or `/usr/local/lib`? This could explain the crash that you're seeing.

> I will try to setup the binding-gyp file correctly so the dylibs can be found at runtime.

I found this:
```
'libraries': ['-L/path/to/libraries', '-lA', '-lB'],
```

Here: https://github.com/nodejs/node-gyp/issues/892#issuecomment-197459165

title: What problems will we encounter by using Ardupilot + MAVSDK ?
author: mommotti
body:
My team is willing to employ Ardupilot over PX4, since the drone we are using comes with Ardupilot by default...
We acknowledge this thread https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/issues/728
but we are still wondering the future effects of using Ardupilot. ( takeoff_and_land works for us! )

answer_comments.body:
Two important things that are not (yet) compatible:
- mission upload/download (AP: 0 item is home, PX4: 0 item is first item)
- flight modes

One thing that would be cool would be to have some easy way to run SITL with Ardupilot. I'm sure it exists, but I am not very familiar with Ardupilot. For instance with PX4, there is [px4-gazebo-headless](https://github.com/jonasvautherin/px4-gazebo-headless) that is just a headless docker container running PX4 and gazebo.

Having an equivalent for Ardupilot would be a first step towards adding integration tests for it, and slowly modify the code where needed to support woth Ardupilot and PX4 :+1:.

title: Mission generation should use NAV_DELAY instead of sending two waypoints on the same location
author: LorenzMeier
body:
From @julianoes:
> The reason MAVSDK sends the same lat/lon twice in a row is because it adds a LOITER_TIME right after a NAV_WAYPOINT. The right approach would be to use NAV_DELAY [...].

Which is implemented in PX4 for quite some time (I verified). The reason PX4 rejects now waypoints that are on top of each other is because the path between those waypoints is not defined (zero distance). Often we however need to know where the vehicle is coming from geometrically and allowing N waypoints on the same location would force us to traverse the mission multiple times and quite a bit forward and backward, increasing the complexity of the autopilot in terms of memory, execution time and also in terms of our ability to QA and certify the code.

So in short: This is undesirable in principle and navigation commands should not exist in the same physical location one after the other.

answer_comments.body:
> So in short: This is undesirable in principle and navigation commands should not exist in the same physical location one after the other.

If this is a hard rule it should also be added to the MAVLink standard.
@dayjaby I suppose for this case we should be using WAYPOINT, DELAY, IMAGE_START_CAPTURE, DELAY, but maybe that's not possible given the current implementation.

body:
`create_mission_item` has `_frame` parameter which is set to 3 ([MAV_FRAME_GLOBAL_RELATIVE_ALT](https://mavlink.io/en/messages/common.html#MAV_FRAME_GLOBAL_RELATIVE_ALT)) though `lat` and `lon` are converted as if they are prepared for 6 ([MAV_FRAME_GLOBAL_RELATIVE_ALT_INT](https://mavlink.io/en/messages/common.html#MAV_FRAME_GLOBAL_RELATIVE_ALT_INT)).

I understand that x,y,z params are integer anyway and it looks like they should be multiplied by `1e7` (i.e. converted to int) in both cases, but then what is the difference between those 2 frame types?

title: Segfault if port failed to open
author: bresch
body:
I have a piece of code using the SDK that binds to an UDP MAVLink port generated by the MAVLink router.
Unfortunately, the port where I wanted to connect is already used by an other application. Since the connection failed, sending an action to the drone resulted in a segfault.
Would it be possible to throw an error to prevent that segfault?

```
[10:20:34|Error] bind error: Address already in use (udp_connection.cpp:82)
Connection failed: Bind error
[...] // some code running and using const Action::Result ams_result = _action->...
Segmentation fault (core dumped)
```

Thanks!

answer_comments.body: Would be great if you could add a stacktrace. Just add `gdb --args` before the command that you're running and then copy `backtrace` once it crashed.
`auto_maneuver_system` that's not a thing I recognize? :astonished:

You can avoid the problem by checking the return value of creating the connection, and exit early if that happens.

However, it still probably should not crash if no valid connection is available. I'm checking that now.
The problem was in the software using this which did not initialize `action` if the connection failed.

title: Reading the Status of RC switches with MavlinkPassthrough
author: Decerguyer
body:
Hi, I currently have a setup with a drone, RC switch, and companion computer.
I want to be able to read the status of RC Channel 8 on the companion computer, so I have the companion computer listen in on mavlink commands with mavlinkpassthrough.

I used the subscribe_async command to receive RC_CHANNEL related RC messages. My code looks as follows:
![Screen Shot 2022-11-24 at 1 27 46 AM](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/76597563/203709947-12c3a25c-7938-4bd0-be7d-1920f69c970e.png)

For some reason, the output has no output like this:
![Screen Shot 2022-11-24 at 1 28 49 AM](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/76597563/203710095-1e87cfa2-8bcd-4967-b57d-224ef75eba54.png)

On the bright side, the companion computer is receiving mavlink messages, the value is just always zero regardless of the switch position. I am however, able to control the drone with the RC switch just fine.
It should be noted I also tried reading the voltage_battery using the system_status mavlink message, and that is reading zero as well despite the real voltage being around 22.7V.

I don't know why every real reading I try to receive is zero, and would appreciate some guidance with this.
Thanks

comments.body:
Can you share a minimal example for me to reproduce this?

Alternatively, check the message in QGroundControl -> Analyze tools -> MAVLink inspector and check what the value is there.
Ok, so channel 8 is 0. Are the other channels 1..7 different from 0?

[10:43:02|Error] Retrying failed for REQUEST_MESSAGE command for message: 148, to (50/1) (mavlink_command_sender.cpp:361)

comments.body: That's likely just warnings you can ignore. Are you using PX4 or ArduPilot? And are you trying anything that's not working?

Error] Retrying failed for REQUEST_MESSAGE command for message: 148, to (50/1) (mavlink_command_sender.cpp:361)
is this a warning?

I used MAVSDK to communicate with a flying module device mounted on a drone. This module device is a product I bought from a drone flight control hardware manufacturer. The manufacturer said that the module supports the MAVLink protocol, and I successfully simulated it using their own ground station and non air and simulation equipment. However, when I connected their flight control to MAVSDK, there was a problem. The exception message is as follows: Error] Retrying failed for REQUEST_MESSAGE command for message: 148, to (50/1) (mavlink_command_sender.cpp:361)

Message 148 is [AUTOPILOT_VERSION](https://mavlink.io/en/messages/common.html#AUTOPILOT_VERSION).

It sounds like this module is implementing MAVLink but might not be implementing the REQUEST_MESSAGE command yet.

Is this module "faking" to be a drone?

On the MAVSDK side, we probably have to fall back to the old command which is [MAV_CMD_REQUEST_AUTOPILOT_CAPABILITIES](https://mavlink.io/en/messages/common.html#MAV_CMD_REQUEST_AUTOPILOT_CAPABILITIES). That might help. I can try that some time.

Does it work at all, or not? I suspect not because it doesn't see an autopilot unless it gets that message.
No more answers, closing.

title: Expose full mission list
author: sanderux
resolution_evidence: maintainer points at the fix: 'Done in #644'

answer_comments.body: Yes, we could have a small plugin just to convert, and upload from/download to these mission format files.

> Wouldn't that fit in the current mission plugin?

Not really because the mission items don't support all the settings and commands so then part of the file that you want to import is not supported which is actually the case right now as we already support the mission plan file.

comments.body:
> get a signal when the mission changed (finished uploading)

Is that in MAVLink? Say if I connect two instances from QGC and upload a mission from one, the other currently doesn't know about that, right?

> a way to read all items (not just then ones known to DC)

I guess that would be a new "mission" plugin, as it probably doesn't fit in the current one (or does it?)

> get a signal when the mission changed (finished uploading)

You can get completion from the SDK `upload_mission_async()` but there is no MAVLink message to notify of a full mission upload: https://mavlink.io/en/services/mission.html

> I guess that would be a new "mission" plugin, as it probably doesn't fit in the current one (or does it?)

It doesn't fit into the current plugin model of a "simple" API. Options are to add support for all types of mission item, to add an API to set or query the underlying mission params (ie allow a generic option for unknown params). I like the flexibility, but I bet @julianoes won't :-)

> I guess that would be a new "mission" plugin, as it probably doesn't fit in the current one (or does it?)

Yes I'd rather have some duplication than one complicated one with all the options that is just as hard as mavlink itself.

IMO a reasonable compromise option might be to add a mission API to download/upload to file or text buffer using the standard [plaintext format](https://mavlink.io/en/file_formats/#mission_plain_text_file). Then anyone who wanted to be "clever" could manually edit and round-trip the file.

> IMO a reasonable compromise option might be to add a mission API to download/upload to file or text buffer using the standard plaintext format. Then anyone who wanted to be "clever" could manually edit and round-trip the file.

My concern is that if we go down this road, we will quickly end up allowing "plaintext mavlink" a bit everywhere, and that's going against the SDK. We can try say "well, you can use that feature, but we may break it and we won't support you in using it", but people will probably still complain when it breaks, and they will still expect support for that.

I don't know, just a concern :-).

I don't think this breaks the SDK, because the plaintext mission format is defacto standard for mission file storage/retrieval. Entirely up to you guys though. The alternatives are to my mind not as clean.
I see. Well that could be a possibility. @julianoes do you have an opinion on that?
Yes, we could have a small plugin just to convert, and upload from/download to these mission format files.
Wouldn't that fit in the current mission plugin?

> Wouldn't that fit in the current mission plugin?

Not really because the mission items don't support all the settings and commands so then part of the file that you want to import is not supported which is actually the case right now as we already support the mission plan file.

> Is that in MAVLink? Say if I connect two instances from QGC and upload a mission from one, the other currently doesn't know about that, right?

We now listen for MISSION_ACK to know if the mission was updated
Done in #644.

title: [Rtk] Data above 180 bytes length not working
author: Katawann
body:
Hi,

I tested the new RTK plugin and it works like a charm ! Thank you @julianoes for the job.

In my working setup I have something like this:
Ntrip caster <---> Internet <---> Linux Ubuntu 20.04 <---> C++ app with MAVSDK and Ntrip Client <---> USB <---> Pixhawk 4

I noticed that if I send a data with length of 4*180 bytes (accepted by the plugin) it will never turn to RTK position, but sending 180 bytes works fine. Not sure to understand the logic around the fragment ID. Maybe the plugin should only accept 180 bytes maximum or is there a logic I missed ?

answer_comments.body:
The maximum length of the mavlink payload is 255 bytes. Not sure what happens if you write 4*180=720 bytes into the message (that would happen here: https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/main/src/mavsdk/plugins/rtk/rtk_impl.cpp#L60), but I guess if it doesn't crash, maybe it's just ignoring whatever is exceeding.

My feeling is that the rtk plugin should check the length of the data and return an error if it's bigger than 180 (which is what is specified here: https://mavlink.io/en/messages/common.html#GPS_RTCM_DATA

Oh, I misread the code, sorry :see_no_evil:. The specs read:

> RTCM message (may be fragmented)

And the code is apparently trying to split the data in multiple messages. So that's something to debug indeed :+1:.

To me it feels like [this line](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/main/src/mavsdk/plugins/rtk/rtk_impl.cpp#L60) is wrong, as it always sends `rtcm_data.data.c_str()`, and it should instead take the right part of it for each message.

title: Exposing Flight mode APIs in core/device_impl.h
author: shakthi-prashanth-m
body:
We have [methods](https://github.com/dronecore/DroneCore/blob/develop/core/device_impl.h#L86-L89) in `DeviceImpl` for PX4 param get/set; but we don't have methods to know/change flight mode in `DeviceImpl`. These methods are useful for plugins. 

Below are the plugins each of which maps to a **PX4 flight mode**:
- [Offboard plugin](https://github.com/dronecore/DroneCore/blob/develop/plugins/offboard/offboard_impl.cpp#L48)
- [FollowMe plugin](https://github.com/dronecore/DroneCore/blob/develop/core/device_impl.h#L86-L89)
- [Mission plugin](https://github.com/dronecore/DroneCore/blob/develop/plugins/mission/mission_impl.cpp#L682)

As of now (in above plugins), we're doing the hard way by using  `MAV_CMD_DO_SET_MODE`. I think it makes sense to expose a method for the same as part of `DeviceImpl` interface. 

At present we've a [public API to get flight mode](https://github.com/dronecore/DroneCore/blob/develop/plugins/telemetry/telemetry.h#L392) is part of `Telemetry `plugin. If other plugins want to know flight mode, they can't call `Telemetry` plugin API (which creates plugin dependency). So it is suitable and intuitive to move some of the useful flight mode APIs from `Telemetry` plugin to `Device` as well.

answer_comments.body:
Having this in the `DeviceImpl` for plugins makes sense to me. I would keep the public API in telemetry -
 that is where I would expect to look for it as an API user.
So the answer is Yes. Feel free to close  - and add the functionality/or change this to an issue and keep open.

dronecore/plugins/action/action.h
```
instead of:

dronecore/action.h

title: Get current speed of the drone and Change heading when drone in hold mode
author: YalamareddyChaitanya
body:
Hi,

I would like to get the current speed of the drone as telemetry when it is doing a mission. Could not find it in telemetry API. Is the ground velocity the current speed of the drone?
And I would also like to change the current heading of the drone when it is in HOLD mode.  Is there anyway to do it ?

Thanks in advance.

answer_comments.body:
> Is the ground velocity the current speed of the drone?

I guess there are two speeds you may be interested in:
1. The [ground speed](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK-Proto/blob/main/protos/telemetry/telemetry.proto#L38)
2. The airspeed (which comes with the [`FixedwingMetrics`](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK-Proto/blob/main/protos/telemetry/telemetry.proto#L755)).

Now if what's unclear is the meaning of "ground velocity":
* The ground speed is the speed relative to the ground. So if you are on the ground and the ground speed says "2 m/s", then for you the drone is moving at 2 m/s in some direction.
* The airspeed is the speed relative to the air. So if the drone flies against the wind at 2 m/s, and the wind speed is 2 m/s, then the ground speed will be 0, but the airspeed will be 2. The drone is flying at 2 m/s, but from your perspective on the ground, it is not "moving".

Does that help?

title: Velocity issue with set_velocity_body() function
author: shrit
body:
Hello,

I am using iris quadcopter in a SITL simulation. I am asking a quadcopter to move forward for 2 seconds at 1m/s. In this case I expect the quadcopter to move 2 meters. However, when calculating the traveled distance between the starting and the end positions, I have noticed that the quadcopter moves only for around 1.3 meters instead of 2 meters. This is the case for all actions executed on x and y plane (Forward, backward, left, right). However if I ask the quadcopter to move Up or Down (z axis) it will move correctly for 2 meters. 

Do anyone have an idea about what is happening?? Did I not understood the SDK correctly or this issue is related to PX4?

Best regards,

answer_comments.body:
This behavior is expected because a quadcopter does not have infinite acceleration. You need to get up to the required speed first.

If you want to move 2 meters forward either use [position offboard control](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/7cd87db701d3ddd2cda1dfcca4b777991138125a/src/plugins/offboard/include/plugins/offboard/offboard.h#L208-L213) or write your own cascaded controller around the velocity controller which closes the loop around a position and outputs a velocity setpoint.
Integrating velocity will be more accurate though than integrating accel values because you're adding up more noise when double integrating.

title: Android: camera definition fails to load, Camera.getCurrentSettings() returns UNAVAILABLE
author: rkganeri
body:
## Description
I'm using MAVSDK Java / Android with `mavsdk_server` on an Android controller. The vehicle has a MAVLink camera component that advertises a camera definition (`camera_definition-ILX-LR1_Sony-40847.xml`). The camera is discovered correctly, but the MAVSDK Camera plugin never seems to load the camera definition, and `Camera.getCurrentSettings(componentId)` returns `UNAVAILABLE`.

This prevents reading the current camera settings through the Camera plugin. Setting camera params through other paths can still affect the camera, but MAVSDK cannot read back the settings.

After camera discovery, I can see the failure logs:
```
D/Mavsdk  : Component Camera 1 (100) added.
E/Mavsdk  : Cannot open file "/data/data/com.dronebase.af.app.px4
D/Mavsdk  : Cache hit for camera_definition-ILX-LR1_Sony-40847.xml
E/Mavsdk  : Failed to open "/data/data/com.dronebase.af.app.px4
I/Mavsdk  : Using cached file "/data/data/com.dronebase.af.app.px4
E/Mavsdk  : tinyxml2::LoadFile failed: Error=XML_ERROR_FILE_READ_ERROR ErrorID=5 (0x5) Line number=0
E/Mavsdk  : Failed to load camera definition: "/data/data/com.dronebase.af.app.px4
...
io.mavsdk.camera.Camera$CameraException: UNAVAILABLE: Unavailable
	at io.mavsdk.camera.Camera$19.onNext(Camera.java:2006)
	at io.mavsdk.camera.Camera$19.onNext(Camera.java:1999)
	at io.grpc.stub.ClientCalls$StreamObserverToCallListenerAdapter.onMessage(ClientCalls.java:468)
	at io.grpc.internal.ClientCallImpl$ClientStreamListenerImpl$1MessagesAvailable.runInternal(ClientCallImpl.java:667)
	at io.grpc.internal.ClientCallImpl$ClientStreamListenerImpl$1MessagesAvailable.runInContext(ClientCallImpl.java:654)
	at io.grpc.internal.ContextRunnable.run(ContextRunnable.java:37)
	at io.grpc.internal.SerializingExecutor.run(SerializingExecutor.java:133)
	at java.util.concurrent.ThreadPoolExecutor.runWorker(ThreadPoolExecutor.java:1100)
	at java.util.concurrent.ThreadPoolExecutor$Worker.run(ThreadPoolExecutor.java:624)
	at java.lang.Thread.run(Thread.java:1572)
```

## Potential Source
This looks like it may be related to the `ANDROID` branch of the `get_cache_directory()` [function here](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/main/cpp/src/mavsdk/core/fs_utils.cpp#L70). That code reads `/proc/self/cmdline`. On Android this is NUL-separated, and in our app the first arg includes a trailing NUL:
```
/proc/self/cmdline first-arg="com.dronebase.af.app.px4?" (hasEmbeddedNul=true)
```

The resulting cache path appears to be truncated to `/data/data/com.dronebase.af.app.px4`. This is the package root but not the MavSDK cache directory `/data/data/com.dronebase.af.app.px4/mavsdk_cache`.  Because the process name still contains the NUL separator from `/proc/self/cmdline`, native file operations appear to truncate the path before `/mavsdk_cache`. 

There is already a [comment](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/main/cpp/src/mavsdk/core/fs_utils.cpp#L75) indicating that the trailing `\0` should be stripped, but the current check appears to dereference `line.end()`. Since `end()` is one past the last character, this does not reliably test the trailing byte. The package name can retain the NUL separator and produce a path that is later truncated by native file operations.

title: calibration without STATUSTEXT commands
author: michprev
body:
While building my own flight stack I have hit an issue with calibration.

```C
void calibration_callback(const Calibration::Result result, const Calibration::ProgressData progress)
{
cout << "progress " << progress.progress << " result " << (int)result << endl;
}

...

auto calibration = make_shared<Calibration>(system);
calibration->calibrate_accelerometer_async(calibration_callback);
```

The situation is:

1. my quad receives [COMMAND_LONG](https://mavlink.io/en/messages/common.html#COMMAND_LONG) with [MAV_CMD_PREFLIGHT_CALIBRATION](https://mavlink.io/en/messages/common.html#MAV_CMD_PREFLIGHT_CALIBRATION) id
1. it starts sending [COMMAND_ACK](https://mavlink.io/en/messages/common.html#COMMAND_ACK) with MAV_RESULT_IN_PROGRESS as result
1. In the end it sends one [COMMAND_ACK](https://mavlink.io/en/messages/common.html#COMMAND_ACK) with MAV_RESULT_ACCEPTED

I am not sending [STATUSTEXT](https://mavlink.io/en/messages/common.html#STATUSTEXT) commands

The issues are:

1. The callback is never called. I think that it is related to
https://github.com/Dronecode/DronecodeSDK/blob/e5d4e0e8510cd02bfbfe5d629e1a2e4ff49549c9/core/mavlink_commands.cpp#L180-L198
Commands with MAV_RESULT_IN_PROGRESS result do not get propagated - that it known issue. The problem is that `calibration_callback` is not called even when the last command with MAV_RESULT_ACCEPTED is received. That can be fixed by inserting something like
`call_user_callback(_calibration_callback, Calibration::Result ::SUCCESS, Calibration::ProgressData(false, NAN, false, ""));` here:
https://github.com/Dronecode/DronecodeSDK/blob/e5d4e0e8510cd02bfbfe5d629e1a2e4ff49549c9/plugins/calibration/calibration_impl.cpp#L203-L205
1. It is not possible to run the calibration for the second time simply because `_state` is still set to `State::ACCELEROMETER_CALIBRATION`. It should be cleared `_state = State::NONE;` here:
https://github.com/Dronecode/DronecodeSDK/blob/e5d4e0e8510cd02bfbfe5d629e1a2e4ff49549c9/plugins/calibration/calibration_impl.cpp#L203-L205

If the current implementation is working for you then it is probably because the flight stack also sends [STATUSTEXT](https://mavlink.io/en/messages/common.html#STATUSTEXT) commands.
https://github.com/Dronecode/DronecodeSDK/blob/e5d4e0e8510cd02bfbfe5d629e1a2e4ff49549c9/plugins/calibration/calibration_impl.cpp#L261-L338

answer_comments.body:
Your own flight stack? :astonished: Is it  open source?

So your observation is correct, and the implementation using these statustexts is really clunky in PX4. We would like to come up with a protocol of MAVLink messages that make the communication of a calibration easier and clearer but still flexible for different sensors, calibration methods, airframes, etc.. That's a big todo but will probably take some time.
The events interface will eventually fix this. @bkueng is working on it.

title: error messages on actions do not reveil error reason
author: petergerten
body:
For example if I arm:
```
try:
  await drone.action.arm()
except mavsdk.action.ActionError as err:
  print(err)
```
The error result is:
`COMMAND_DENIED: 'Command Denied'; origin: arm(); params: () `

But I don't know what caused the error. The PX4 SITL shell in this case shows:

`WARN  [commander] Preflight Fail: High Accelerometer Bias`

This seems to also propagate via MAVLink as I can see it in QGC.
But it seems there is no way at the moment to get this message via MAVSDK - or am I missing something?

answer_comments.body:
Good point. The problem is that in MAVLink these "error messages" are only statustext information but the ack itself does not tell the reason.

You could subscribe to statustext in Python (https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK-Proto/blob/8b7dc4e1e8f34de9a8dbf9f66e1e832104f26d21/protos/telemetry/telemetry.proto#L47-L48) to get that information but that's awkward.

Alternatively, we could enable these printfs to happen in Python no matter if you subscribed or not but it's a bit ugly too.

The optimal real solution would be an interface like `is_armable` that gives you a detailed report of what is green and what is still red in order to arm. There is the MAVLink message [SYS_STATUS](https://mavlink.io/en/messages/common.html#SYS_STATUS) for it and we should try more and more rely on it (instead of statustext messages), so more work is needed on the PX4 side but also MAVSDK side. And even more long term there is an [events interface](https://docs.google.com/document/d/18qdDgfML97lItom09MJhngYnFzAm1zFdmlCKG7TaBpg/edit) planned which would address that even better.

title: Device never gets connected again after heartbeat timed out
author: fklabach
body:
When heartbeats time out of a connected `Device`, the `Device` gets disconnected and never connected again. So both `is_connected()` (with only one device) and `is_connected(uuid)` (with uuid of previously connected device) never return true again. This also affects at least the `Device` thread update rate (100ms instead of 10ms).

Looking at the `device_impl` code, ` set_disconnected()` resets `_target_uuid_initialized`, but not `_target_uuid`. Now autopilot version is not requested again in `process_heartbeat()`, because `_target_uuid` was previously set to a nonzero value. Target uuid is never initialized and `Device` never gets connected again.

Fixes I tried, both work for me:

- `set_disconnected()` resets `_target_uuid_initialized`, `_target_uuid` and `_target_uuid_retries`.

-  `set_disconnected()` just doesn't reset  `_target_uuid_initialized`, keep the uuid of the prevously connected device (an obtained uuid never changes in my application, this might not work for others).

I use PX4 SITL too (with Gazebo) and it sends a nonzero uuid.
Does your SITL send autopilot version at regular intervals? For me, autopilot version is only sent when requested.
Once `_target_uuid` was set nonzero, autopilot version is never requested again in `process_heartbest()`.
To get connected again would require `process_autopilot_version()` to set `_target_uuid_initialized`. This never happens when we  don't request and receive the autopilot version.
Ok I think I understand, thanks.

title: UDP reconnect logic with PX4
author: al2950
body:
I think this issue has probably caught a few people out in the past. But when using UDP with PX4, PX4 will record the port & ip address of the first heartbeat it receives. It will then send any status and responses to this address. This address is set once, and only once, and so if you disconnect and reconnect with a different local port (on client), you will not receive any messages until the PX4 is rebooted.

Suggest adding a default port to MavSDK which it attempts to bind to, currently it is set to 0 so OS picks a 'sensible' random port.

comments.body: Isn't that a PX4 issue? If PX4 only supports one UDP client and needs to be rebooted to move to a new one, then it has to be fixed on the PX4 side, doesn't it?
One thing to note is that PX4 re-uses the same ports, so they are both set statically, while MAVSDK chooses the local port randomly.

> Isn't that a PX4 issue? If PX4 only supports one UDP client and needs to be rebooted to move to a new one, then it has to be fixed on the PX4 side, doesn't it?

Maybe, but I dont think its a bug in PX4.

Firstly (in PX4) most of the logic assumes a single client, allowing multiple clients would add complexity (which in turn decreases reliability)  Secondly adding logic to monitor a client, and potentially drop it if it does not hear from it may result in unintended dropped clients due to a network hitch... which would be a safety concern. 

I have not discussed this on the PX4 github, but my pov was that it would be way easier to just allow a user to specify a local port with MAVSDK. If not then i suggest adding this note to the troubleshooting docs

Disclaimer: I am not the one who needs to be convinced, I'll leave the final word to Julian 😇. But I'd like to share my opinion, which is that PX4 having to reboot in order to swap to a different client is a bug. And allowing to set the local port with MAVSDK would be a hack. The way I see client-server connections is that the server exposes a port and the client contacts it over this port. When I connect to GitHub, my browser does not set a local port to make it easier for GitHub to answer, and I don't need to reboot GitHub between two calls 🙈.

This said, without changing anything, I'm pretty sure that you can solve your problem with mavlink-router. Did you consider that?

I agree with @JonasVautherin but I'm also aware that we can't just change the way PX4 is set up, and we want to be compatible with it, so we should find a way.

@al2950 can you describe what steps I would take to reproduce this? I need to play with this to figure out exactly what is happening and then think through it.
I think I tried to fix this in PX4 a while ago: https://github.com/PX4/PX4-Autopilot/pull/21608

> I agree with [@JonasVautherin](https://github.com/JonasVautherin) but I'm also aware that we can't just change the way PX4 is set up, and we want to be compatible with it, so we should find a way.
> 
> [@al2950](https://github.com/al2950) can you describe what steps I would take to reproduce this? I need to play with this to figure out exactly what is happening and then think through it.

Hi @julianoes, thanks for the reply. I am currently away and I dont have any access to a computer (and trying to limit any screen time). I will put together a test for you when I get back in a couple of weeks.

However it would be useful what, if any, PX4 hardware you have access to? Or if you are comfortable setting up PX4 SITL with gazebo or similar

> [@julianoes](https://github.com/julianoes) fmtlib is just a formatting library, spdlog is a logger with sinks, levels etc. It uses fmtlib or std::format under the hood. Also, if you are planning to use c++20 than std::format is supported from gcc13, but not sure if there are issues for other platforms like android/ios. IMHO `std::format` performance is much worse across the board. Actually I don't know If this white elephant is used anywhere in production. Benchmark code link - https://godbolt.org/z/WY7vP9b8n . P.S `std::format` is supported from `GCC 13` and `NDK r27+ (Clang/libc++)`, though iOS/Apple Clang may still have gaps. `fmtlib` remains the portable fallback.

> > [@julianoes](https://github.com/julianoes) fmtlib is just a formatting library, spdlog is a logger with sinks, levels etc. It uses fmtlib or std::format under the hood. Also, if you are planning to use c++20 than std::format is supported from gcc13, but not sure if there are issues for other platforms like android/ios. > > IMHO `std::format` performance is much worse across the board. Actually I don't know If this white elephant is used anywhere in production. Benchmark code link - https://godbolt.org/z/WY7vP9b8n . > > > P.S `std::format` is supported from `GCC 13` and `NDK r27+ (Clang/libc++)`, though iOS/Apple Clang may still have gaps. `fmtlib` remains the portable fallback. You forgot the main thing for benchmarks: build with full optimizations (`compiled with -O2` is just a cout in your link). The ratios dropped down to average around 0.3x, std::format is a winner. Me personally, I am not for or against fmt/std formatting, std is based on fmt at the end. For such low difference in performance I would rather not use external libs if possible for sake of simplicity. However, as mavsdk need to support some old compilers and systems fmtlib is a choice. The main idea is to propose spdlog which will simplify logging.

You guys are a bit late to the party. See more rational in https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/pull/2815#issue-4161803549.

Initially, I wanted to just use C++20 std::format but quickly discovered that support for the platforms we currently support was patchy. (We build with GCC 9 for some older platforms.)

Claude Code quickly added a "fallback" to go back to std::ostream based printing and manual parsing for `{}` for older platforms but I did not want to have two implementations to track where the slower one was likely used on older (and likely) slower platforms. Therefore, I decided to end the `std::format` experiment and use `fmt` instead.

I see. I wonder if this would solve the issue with platforms like Android where you can't (or at least not easily) set the env variable in the first place. Presumably, spdlog would help with that. I'm a bit reluctant to change this myself but I would consider a pull request.

title: Remove `-Werror` except for CI
author: julianoes
body:
We should probably disable to error on warnings (`-Werror`) except for CI runs.

Currently, `-Werror` is included here:
https://github.com/Dronecode/DronecodeSDK/blob/ef45e4ddb7a8c5dcd0ac20df9a330afdaa9a7be6/cmake/compiler_flags.cmake#L13

but it would be better if this was not set by default and added in CI.

answer_comments.body: Why is that? If warnings are errors at the CI level, they are effectively errors at all levels. I don't get why we would disable it. For development? :thinking:

Because you don't want to error just because someone is using an odd or newer version of a compiler.
E.g. when someone is installing via brew or from AUR you generally don't have `-Werror` because it would break too many times.
Ooh, I see. Makes sense. Or a CMake option to enable it (which the CI would do)? Just thinking about reducing the round trips between my compiler and the CI :D.

This was done to prevent the vehicle from doing anything stupid on arming. For instance if it is in mission mode and you arm, it might not just spin the propellers but takeoff straightaway. This can be a safety hazard and the goal was to make arming and takeoff to explicit commands.

It **will** take off straight away on a copter or VTOL in almost all circumstances: https://docs.px4.io/en/flight_modes/mission.html

title: REQUEST_MESSAGE vs custom getters like REQUEST_CAMERA_INFORMATION
author: JonasVautherin
body:
It's currently part of the [list for MAVSDK v2](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/issues/2002), and though I don't think I can contribute an implementation, I think I can contribute a (relatively informed) opinion.

TL;DR: I don't think this can go in MAVSDK v2 :see_no_evil:.

#### We cannot detect what the receiver supports

There is no way to detect if the receiver supports `REQUEST_MESSAGE`, because the requested message could have been requested by someone else, or it could be transmitted spontaneously by the receiver. So making statistics to try to guess stuff like "was this `CAMERA_INFORMATION` message an answer to my request, or is it a coincidence?" is probably not worth it by far.

Also each message is independent. So even if we managed to detect that `REQUEST_MESSAGE` is supported for `CAMERA_INFORMATION`, it would not say anything about e.g. `REQUEST_PROTOCOL_VERSION`.

#### What we can do

* Push the receivers to support both messages (i.e. the drone should support both `REQUEST_MESSAGE(<camera_information>)` and `REQUEST_CAMERA_INFORMATION`.
* Keep the old way in MAVSDK until we feel like we can completely drop it.

In other words, the implementation work is not on the MAVSDK side, but on the receiver side (e.g. make sure that PX4/Ardupilot support the newer messages, make sure that cameras do, push proprietary players to do it).

Some day, maybe we will feel comfortable in dropping the old way and telling people "well if your drone does not support the new way, that's your problem".

answer_comments.body:
> But I see many problems there

Yes, there are many problems. But at some point switching and saying we don't support the old way also doesn't work and also has problems. So my idea is to try hard and do a best effort solution that - while having corner cases - generally works.

> For instance, it is legal to broadcast the command and expect multiple systems/components to broadcast their message.

Yes, it gets indeed tricky with multiple systems and components, so let's only use these commands to specific sysid/compid pairs and not use broadcast.

> Should we somehow keep a state in MAVSDK that says "I am pretty sure that this drone supports the new message because I got an answer once"?

I think you're missing something here. A success is not if we receive the message that we asked for but we receive the ack *AND* the message. That's a definite confirmation that it worked.

> A success is not if we receive the message that we asked for but we receive the ack

Oh, that's a good point! It is a command, so it will be acked in case of success, and therefore you can detect a success (but not all failures: a timeout is indistinguishable from an unsupported command).

So I think you're right: you can probably try both until one (or both) is acked, and when it is, keep it (or keep the new one if both are supported). Or of course if it is UNSUPPORTED then fallback to the other.

> So what about switching to the new REQUEST_MESSAGE command and if it gets UNSUPPORTED, FAILED or a timeout, then we fall back to the old one?

I don't think that is entirely correct. If you have a timeout, you cannot conclude anything, so you should not fall back. I think it's better to try both messages until an answer (SUCCESS/UNSUPPORTED/FAILED) is received, rather than trying the new one for an arbitrary number of seconds and blocking everything during that time in case only the old one is supported.

> A success is [when] we receive the ack AND the message

Hmm I think the ack is enough to detect that the message is supported, no need to deal with the message (which again will be a mess because the message is unreliable and can be sent for many other reasons).

IMO the code in MAVSDK should always handle those messages as "unreliable, spontaneous messages", but MAVSDK can request them separately if it wants to encourage the drone to send it. I.e. don't write logic that says "send the REQUEST, do something with the response, and in the same logic do something with the message and wrap that whole thing to look like a reliable request/response". If that makes sense?
In v3 I want to remove the [MAV_CMD_REQUEST_AUTOPILOT_CAPABILITIES](https://mavlink.io/en/messages/common.html#MAV_CMD_REQUEST_AUTOPILOT_CAPABILITIES).

comments.body:
Thanks for bringing this up. Let's talk through it and make a decision.

My question is: Wouldn't a receiver that doesn't support `REQUEST_MESSAGE` nack it and therefore tell you that it doesn't support it?

> Wouldn't a receiver that doesn't support REQUEST_MESSAGE nack it

I don't think so :thinking:. One problem with MAVLink is that the specs do not require to  nack unsupported messages. I am pretty sure I have seen implementations that just ignore unsupported messages (resulting in a timeout, indistinguishable from an actual timeout in a sane way IMO).

So same thing there: one would have to make it a requirement to nack unsupported messages, ask implementations to change to that, and in a few years when we are fairly sure that all the implementations we care about do it, we could rely on nacks :innocent:.

So actually UNSUPPORTED is for a command that is not supported but not necessarily for a command param that is not supported. So, in that case, it should probably be failed. I would argue a decent camera implementation would do that, rather than timing out.

So what about switching to the new REQUEST_MESSAGE command and if it gets UNSUPPORTED, FAILED or a timeout, then we fall back to the old one?
This means that old implementations would still work, just slower, while new ones will work nicely, and quickly. What am I missing?

I wish it worked, and maybe I'm being too pessimistic. But I see many problems there :see_no_evil:.

> I would argue a decent camera implementation would do that

My understanding of the specs is that it is legal to timeout. For instance, it is legal to broadcast the command and expect multiple systems/components to broadcast their message. I suppose it would be rational to not have all the components return UNSUPPORTED in that case. The specs clearly mention the broadcast possibility : "Request the target **system(s)** emit a single instance of a specified message".

> What am I missing?

Say the drone only supports the new message, and does not time out for unsupported commands. Say the request happens to timeout. What do we do? If we fallback to the old message, it will always time out. Should we then fallback again to the new message? Should we somehow keep a state in MAVSDK that says "I am pretty sure that this drone supports the new message because I got an answer once"? title: Move protoc generation out of cmake and version generated files
author: JonasVautherin
body:
@julianoes, @thomasetter: I'd like to have your opinion on that :blush:.

We use protobuf + gRPC in `mavsdk_server`, and therefore generate code with the proto compiler (`protoc`), at build time. I believe this should change, mainly for the following reasons:

* We will soon want to autogenerate more code, using our own protoc plugin. It will make the autogeneration a bit more complex (will require to build a python module, etc), and therefore I don't feel like keeping that in our CMakeLists. We already have separate scripts for that [in Swift](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK-Swift/blob/master/tools/generate_from_protos.bash) and [in Python](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK-Python/blob/master/other/tools/run_protoc.sh).
* We will autogenerate the C++ header files, and it would make sense to version them, so that we can link to the github files in discussions. We already do that [in Swift](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK-Swift/tree/master/Sources/MAVSDK-Swift/Generated) and [in Python](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK-Python/tree/master/mavsdk/generated).
* When cross-compiling, we currently need to build for the host first, so that we get `protoc`, and then we can cross-compile. It takes time (e.g. on the CI), and sometimes it doesn't work. For instance when using dockcross on my machine, my host-built `protoc` relies on a version of glibc that is not available in the dockcross container, and therefore `protoc` doesn't run there.

For those reasons, I believe it makes sense to generate the files separately, and version them.

The new workflow would look a bit like this:

1. If you don't need to generate the files (typically when cross-compiling), you just run `cmake` (configure) and  `cmake --build` (build), and rely on the versioned generated files.
2. If you need to generate the files, you:

    a. run `cmake` (configure) so that you get `protoc`
    b. run `generate_protos.sh`
    c. run `cmake --build` (build)

@thomas.etter: Note that this would break the changes you did for automatically re-generating when the proto files change.

comments.body:
I have also come to think that checking in the generated files is the way to go.

> @thomas.etter: Note that this would break the changes you did for automatically re-generating when the proto files change.

If we create a CI check which runs the proto-file compilation and makes sure that there are no diffs, we can run it in parallel, get up-to-date generated files, and keep good build latency.

We can do this for arbitrarily many code-generation pipelines without significantly increasing the total check latency.
