title: MAVSDK failed to initiate UDP connection
author: cjffly
body:
I have strange issue when I try to use MAVSDK C++ application to start a connection using UDP:
I got a "pixhawk - raspberry pi(as a bridge) - wifi router - ubuntu machine" setup. While I am trying to run some MAVSDK application, such as take_off_land example like `./take_off_land udp://:14540`, it will tell me `No system found, exiting.`

When I open QGC on the ubuntu machine, it still won't automatically find any system. However, when I manually add udp connection throught QGC, specify the IP, like `192.168.0.101:14540`, QGC will find the system and connect to my pixhawk. 

Even strangely, I close QGC at this moment, and run the MAVSDK application `./take_off_land udp://:14540` on the same ubuntu machine, it recognize the system and let the drone take off.

Can someone tell me is this a bug in MAVSDK? or the QGC manual UDP connection is different than udp connection used by MAVSDK?

answer_comments.body:
I think it's a networking issue. When you run `./take_off_land udp://:14540`, what MAVSDK does is that it waits until it receives HEARTBEAT messages from the drone over UDP. QGC does the same. Apparently, the network broadcasts coming from your drone don't reach the Ubuntu machine. That's not unsurprising, many network topology behave the same.

By specifying the RPi's IP (`192.168.0.101`) to QGC, my guess is that QGC started sending heartbeats to it, which "opened" the connection. And then the RPi started talking to your Ubuntu machine instead of broadcasting, which is why MAVSDK got the messages. MAVSDK does not initiate the connection.

Can you modify the RPi side so that it sends MAVLink directly to your Ubuntu IP address, to verify that?

The mavftp server example does it: https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/develop/examples/ftp_server/ftp_server.cpp#L43

I wonder if you could do that [here](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/develop/examples/takeoff_land/takeoff_and_land.cpp#L47):

```c++
connection_result = mavsdk.setup_udp_remote(...);
```

instead of 

```c++
connection_result = dc.add_any_connection(...);
```

If you try it, let me know what happens :slightly_smiling_face:

> The system seems only find the last argument, not all systems.

Hmm, it could be that it only has one udp remote, at the moment. Not sure how it could be edited to add multiple ones. Feel free to have a look and open a PR if you find a solution :blush:.

I'm closing this in the meantime, let's open a new issue if you want to discuss the multiple `setup_udp_remote`.

title: Get mavlink messages through the SDK
author: douglaswsilva
body:
We'd like to be able to read mavlink messages in the Swift SDK, similar to what QGC has. For instance, we were having problems with starting mission and didn't know what the problem was until we look at the debug logs in our console to see this message: 
```
[12:57:31|Debug] MAVLink: critical: Maximum distance from home exceeded by 18.1 m (system_impl.cpp:292)
```

We'd like to get this message as part of telemetry or something else, so we could display it to user.
resolution_evidence: maintainer points at the fix: 'Done in: https://github.com/Dronecode/DronecodeSDK/pull/'

answer_comments.body: @julianoes: Would it make sense to add that to `Telemetry`, or another plugin?

Ok it's good that you're describing the actual problem which is that you need to know when and why things don't work. @bkueng is actually working on a proposal and implementation to address exactly this problem. This means we should get much more status information like this in the not so distant future :).

Now until then, we might want to just add the statustext messages to telemetry as @JonasVautherin suggested. it's just a `char[50]`, so nothing fancy.
The next step for adding the statustext to the telemetry is to make a PR on the [API definition](https://github.com/Dronecode/DronecodeSDK-Proto/blob/master/protos/telemetry/telemetry.proto) :-).

title: Provide Autopilot/Server functionality for MAVLink services
author: bazfp
body:
It would be exceptionally useful to have MAVSDK provide server functionality for MAVLink microservices. 

There is currently a gap missing in MAVLink, the raw data types are provided by the MAVLink headers but the implementation of the microservices (Command, Mission, Heartbeat, Parameters etc) is still up to the user to implement. This can easily lead to fragmentation of the standard with the services. It also makes MAVLink integration into existing systems difficult.

MAVSDK does a good job of tackling this from a GCS/Companion side, but API is not currently suitable for the autopilot side as it was built on the assumption we're communicating with a MAVLink autopilot that implements the services we require. MAVSDK connects as a client.

There is a real case for server implementation in MAVSDK along these lines and MAVSDK could be used as a basis for a MAVLink autopilot. While obviously not for embedded platforms, there are certainly use-cases for this on non-PX4/Ardupilot autopilot systems but also in testing frameworks. In addition MAVSDK could bridge existing autopilot systems with MAVLink.

I propose MAVSDK implement the following plugins:

- Mission server (`MISSION_REQUEST_INT` workflow from autopilot side)
- Command server (subscribe to commands, ack, etc)
- Parameter server
- Message server (`MAV_CMD_REQUEST_MESSAGE`? `MAV_CMD_SET_MESSAGE_INTERVAL` support?)

I've recently documented what MAVLink messages + parameters MAVSDK requires in order to function, I can list these as it would probably be a useful starting point for these services.

title: Add Functionality to Broadcast to Interface without Explicit Vehicle Connection
author: AlexKlimaj
body:
I am working on recreating the QGC RTK Base station functionality in a C++ application on a raspberry pi. I have the PX4 GPS driver running and now I am trying to figure out how to get mavsdk to broadcast the RTK corrections to all vehicles on two different interfaces. One serial and the other is UDP. 

It does not appear that mavsdk can do a broadcast to all connected vehicles. My approach is to discover all connected vehicles on the serial and UDP connections, then iterate through all of them doing a mavlink passthrough message to send the RTK corrections to each vehicle independently.

answer_comments.body: MAVSDK does not allow to broadcast messages right now. So right now it would just do the same loop as you do :+1:. I am not sure if broadcasting is in the scope of MAVSDK right now, because many things are not expecting to be broadcasted, right? Like all the commands, or basically any targeted message. Or is that incorrect?

I understand that broadcasting some messages may make sense (typically a GNSS base station wants to do just that). But at the MAVSDK level, the user does something like `drone.action.takeoff()`, where `drone` represents a MAVLink system (i.e. a pair of <sysid, compid>). Should MAVSDK allow for broadcasting the `takeoff` command? Because a command is a reliable message, MAVSDK expects to receive an ACK, otherwise it will resend the message. How do you broadcast a reliable message? How many ACKs do you expect, and from which <sysid, compid>? What do you do if one of them times out? Do you consider that your `takeoff` command failed? Or do you tell the user that it "partially succeeded"? Do you give a list of <sysid, compid>, with the result code for each of them?

I don't think it is trivial, but of course we are open to PRs if somebody figures out an nice API doing that in MAVSDK :blush:.
Maybe this is a hint that the MavlinkPassthrough plugin should not be a plugin but a direct API of the Mavsdk class. We could then add some sort of flag to signal the broadcast option.

You can now use the added [RawBytesConnection](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/2460e15689052b8cc3ce7fa4052bf584be0e7c83/src/mavsdk/core/include/mavsdk/mavsdk.h#L493-L528) and implement whatever sending/receiving protocol you want.

Personally, I'm not a fan of broadcast, so I'm not in favor of including it.

title: Organize & Cleanup Receiver System & Component ID Handling
author: coderkalyan
body:
Hello, I was looking into the source code and I found quite a few FIXME's in `mavsdk_impl.cpp` regarding how different system and component IDs are handled. I created this issue so we can try to fix these issues, and to offer my thoughts on how they should be implemented as well as hear other people's ideas.

1. [L256](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/master/src/core/mavsdk_impl.cpp#L256): Agreed, there are a couple things wrong here. First of all, we should not be setting the SID to a known CID, that's bad usage of the definitions. However, I don't think we should simply hard code in another value. See point 3 for my thoughts on a better approach.
2. [L258](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/master/src/core/mavsdk_impl.cpp#L258): Again, this time at least we are setting the CID to a value designated for a Component ID (but incrementing it by 1? :thinking: ). This is still a fairly arbitrary value, and furthermore is hardcoded.
3. Personally, I think the `Configuration` structure is rather limiting. It forces the user to use a specific SID and CID (which is automatically decided for them) which further has the implication of only being able to successfully run 1 instance of MAVSDK at a time (well, maybe 1 per `Configuration` but you get the idea). Furthermore, the hardcoded values are set to some weird values! :thinking: 

My suggestion is: as far as API goes, start with a `void set_mavlink_id(uint8_t sid, uint8_t cid)` or similar which allows for manual user setting of the SID and CID. The current `Configuration` idea can still remain as a feature but should be refactored to something like `set_auto_mavlink_id(MavType type)` which makes more sense to me - it allows the user to have MAVSDK automatically choose an *appropriate* SID and CID based on the type of system the user is implementing with the SDK. Also, I personally feel that setting either the SID and CID or the `MavType` should be mandatory at the constructor level, but I'm not sure how others feel about this?

Now for what those auto values should be:
* For `MavType GCS`: Quoted from MAVSDK source: "Usually QGC identifies itself with sysid 255" - we should just pick a standard ID that we want to be the default MAVSDK SID, and stick to it. According to the MAVLink documentation, it is good practice to count GCS SIDs down from 255. So I'm throwing the value `245` out there, as its reasonably close to the top but leaves some room for multiple QGC/other GCS instances to be run. In reality any SID would work, and we should probably do at least some basic searching before deciding on one, to minimize conflicts (at least with existing open source GCS). The CID should be set to `MAV_COMP_ID_MISSIONPLANNER` as this is most likely what the user needs (stated in docs as "Component that can generate/supply a mission flight plan (e.g. GCS or developer API).", which is most likely the usage of MAVSDK in the context of a GCS.)
* For `MavType CompanionComputer`: This is a bit more difficult, As the FIXME says it should be autodetected. The best way to do this would probably be to read incoming `MAV_HEARTBEAT` messages until one with the CID `MAV_COMP_ID_AUTOPILOT1` is discovered, and set our SID to the source SID of that message. As for CID, `MAV_COMP_ID_PATHPLANNER` would probably be the most idiomatic, considering the companion computer is usually involved in path planning, obstacle avoidance, etc.
* For `MavType Autopilot`: As far as default values go, the existing is fine - 1 as SID and and `MAV_COMP_ID_AUTOPILOT` as CID.

4. [L263](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/master/src/core/mavsdk_impl.cpp#L263): See point 3.
5. [L78](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/master/src/core/mavsdk_impl.cpp#L78): This is a tough one. Could someone explain to me why we are blanket ignoring all QGC messages? Is this a QGC specific thing, or do we just not want to handle messages from other GCS? If that's the case, we should again use heartbeat to get a list of GCS based on `MAV_COMP_ID_MISSIONPLANNER` or similar, and ignore anything in that list. This seems restrictive, however, as you can't communicate with other GCS... i.e if 2 MAVSDK instances were communicating with each other. Either way, checking a specific SID is a bad idea - I for one run multiple QGC instances with different SIDs, so this wouldn't work off the bat. Would something bad happen if we didn't ignore GCS messages? Instead of "blacklisting", maybe we could "whitelist" by deciding on a per-message basis if we are capable of handling it?

These are just my thoughts - please feel free to comment and share ideas. Once we have a good idea of what we want to do, I can open a PR and implement the changes!

title: Add option to build without curl
author: julianoes
body: For slow compilation (e.g. on embedded boards) it would be nice to be able to build without curl.

answer_comments.body: Sometimes you're in a debugging situation where you just need to rebuild on the device.

Right. But I don't think that adding options in CMakeLists and ifdefs in the code is the right solution for debugging on the device.

If you are debugging curl on the device, then you need to compile it. If you are debugging MAVSDK, then you don't have to recompile curl. Yes, that implies that you may need to not use our superbuild and to learn how to do that (e.g. cross-compile the dependencies separately, copy that on your device and build mavsdk on the device without SUPERBUILD=ON). But that's "basic" dependency management in cmake. I'm happy to write a superbuild to make that easier for most use-cases, but for specific use-cases, I believe that developers should learn how to deal with that.

To me it would be the same as saying "we should make it such that cmake checks if the submodules are correctly synced, because we don't want our developers to have to know about git submodules", and then "cmake should show a warning when people push to their fork without having an 'upstream' branch, because not everyone knows how to work with a fork".

We can do all that, but it results in more code that we need to maintain, and it forces devs to learn about our custom wrappers instead of learning to use the actual tools.

Am I too much of a purist? :laughing:
I agree with your examples but this is more a request that the MAVSDK should be able to build and run with minimal dependencies if required.

For the record: it still requires curl but you can now also use libcurl from the system instead of getting it via git and building it. The way to do so is to use the configure option `cmake -DSUPERBUILD=OFF` for the configure step. Note this is supported as of Ubuntu 18.04 but not 16.04.

mavlink协议 是通过 ID 进行区分
一个无人机，在系统中是一个 system，通过system id进行区分
同一个无人的多个功能模块例如照相、gps，通过component id进行区分，不管有多少个connection，都将给更新同一个system。
这些id都在无人机固件中配置的

Translation:
The MAVLink protocol distinguishes a single drone by ID. In the system, a drone is considered one "system," identified by a system ID. Multiple functional modules within the same drone — such as the camera and GPS — are distinguished by component ID. Regardless of how many connections there are, they all update the same system. These IDs are all configured in the drone's firmware.

title: Migration to MAVLink organisation
author: JonasVautherin
body:
Copying @hamishwillee's message on the PX4 Slack, to keep a record of the discussion.

The MAVLink dev team accepted the "MAVLink RFC Proposal" so we'll be taking the Dronecode SDK into the MAVLink organisation and renaming it to the "MAVSDK": https://github.com/mavlink/rfcs/blob/master/text/0011-mavlink-sdk.md

### Code


* [x] Agree on new names for SDK repos
 => Will be `MAVSDK`, `MAVSDK-Proto`, `MAVSDK-Swift`, `MAVSDK-Python`, etc.
* [x] Move all SDK repos into github mavlink org
* [x] Agree new names for namespaces and other code items
 => The documentation and official name is `MAVSDK`, but the code doesn't have to follow that. We will generally prefer lowercase (i.e. namespace: `mavsdk::`), and we may capitalize if necessary (e.g. `class MavSdk`).
* [x] Update code in line with new names
* [ ] Update READMEs with appropriate new links to repos and docs
* [x] Make an official first release. Would this be 1.0?
 => The release will not be 1.0, but just the continuation of current releases, each repo going at its own speed. The Python SDK will be released as `0.1.0` on pip ASAP.
* [x] Make sure all old repositories redirect correctly

### Docs


* [x] Design of new logo & tagline
 => Taken care of in #750.
* [x] Confirm name of docs repo in mavlink org [I think `sdk_docs` to `mavsdk_docs`]
* [x] Move docs repo into mavlink org
* [x] Update head revision docs API reference
* [x] Update docs guide materials
* [ ] Review/update docs on marketing/positioning. Ie where it is hosted and the goals.
* [x] Decide what to do about previous releases/docs. These all will refer to the Dronecode SDK.
* [x] Propose that we delete all the old ones and start from scratch with a master release and initial release
* [x] Re-sync via gitbook
* [x] Get new domain/URL. 
 Current: `https://sdk.dronecode.org/en/`. Proposed: `https://mavsdk.mavlink.io/en/`. This is probably easier than try to do `mavlink.io/mavlink`, `mavlink.io/mavsdk` etc.

- SDK repos: I propose `mavsdk-proto`, `mavsdk`, `mavsdk-swift`, `mavsdk-python`, `mavsdk-java`, `mavsdk-js`.
- Namespaces, code items: I would use "mavsdk" (lowercase) as much as possible.

I would move to 1.0 once all the API is autogenerated (C++ is the next and last one coming for that). However, we should release packages when possible (I'm thinking about CocoaPods and python-pip here).

- SDK repos. I'm ambivalent. I slightly lean towards MAVSDK  _in text_ when referring to the project and product. However I don't extend that desire to package or repo names. Ie. We could use mavsdk-proto for the repo URL and still refer to it in the readme as MAVSDK-Proto. 
- Namespaces, code items - whatever works for the core maintainers - you
- First release ... - Agree. However would like to have "a" release as soon as possible.

title: Race condition in assigning callbacklist handle
author: devbharat
body:
There could be a race condition in assigning handle [here](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/3131cc9b34b04d6d7affb09d3ad2fdbf81c677af/src/mavsdk/core/callback_list_impl.h#L23) can do something like _last_id.fetch_add(1, std::memory_order_relaxed);

Another thing i noticed is nested subscriptions wouldn't work from callbacks. Maybe we should add a comment for it, or better do deferred subscriptions as well like removals.

answer_comments.body: I like the deferred subscription and removal! It would be great if you can make a pull request for it.

linked_prs.title: Add conditional callback, use atomic handle_id and add some tests

comments.body:
Hmm. What if we extend the mutex around that part?

Would nested subscriptions work using `std::recursive_mutex` and would that be safe?

I didn't wanna use a recursive mutex (hard to debug), and extending the mutex to cover the handle got a bit complicated(with deferred subs), so I went with atomic which works, and seems to be the kind of thing it is designed for. I also added deferred subscriptions, you can see it [here](https://gist.github.com/devbharat/ce952fc9f32a9771c7be1c2a62fc31a0).

I also created something similar to the MavlinkMessageHandler class that uses a map of msgid to callbacklists, but crucially it allows adding subscriptions from within callbacks (if you get this mavlink message, send this message and are now interested in this mavlink message kind of workflow), which meant (in addiiton to deferred subs in cblist) the execution of the callbacklist from MavlinkMessageHandler needed to be outside the lock (comparison [here](https://gist.github.com/devbharat/17a11229bd7df818f9a7fd65828f4ddd)). Not sure if it is generally interesting for everyone.
I like the deferred subscription and removal! It would be great if you can make a pull request for it.
will make the PR
@devbharat I think this would still be great :)
ah damn i forgot
That was quick, thanks!
Fixed in #2307, thanks @devbharat!

title: GTest is a submodule dependency, but unless all other dependencies is not automatically downloaded
author: LorenzMeier
body:
This leads to unexpected build failures on clean checkouts:

```
CMake Error at src/CMakeLists.txt:73 (add_subdirectory):
  The source directory

    /Users/lorenzmeier/src/MAVSDK/src/third_party/gtest

  does not contain a CMakeLists.txt file.
```

Running `git submodule init && git submodule update` fixes it. Having some dependencies auto-download and others not is very confusing.

comments.body:
That's an interesting point. I would believe that this is one consequence of using submodules: you can never really know if you must fetch the submodules or if they are optional, can you?

The reasoning is the following:
* For some reasons we could discuss, I am not into using submodules for dependencies.
* When I moved the dependencies into a superbuild, I did not change gtest. Because we need submodules for `proto/` and `mavlink/`, that would not have removed the need for a `--recursive` checkout. I am not sure if moving gtest into our superbuild would make sense or not. I guess it could, because the [Google note](https://github.com/google/googletest/blob/36066cfecf79267bdf46ff82ca6c3b052f8f633c/googletest/docs/faq.md#why-is-it-not-recommended-to-install-a-pre-compiled-copy-of-google-test-for-example-into-usrlocal) advising against installing gtest may apply to other dependencies, and therefore one should probably not install dependencies coming from our superbuild.

TL;DR: we could move gtest into the superbuild, but that would not remove the need for the `--recursive` checkout.

What do you think? @julianoes do you have an opinion on that?

What I'm asking for is consistency: Either the super build handles all the dependencies, or it handles none and they are documented. I think removing the automation you already have would however be a mistake. It makes it convenient. If you simply add the git submodules update to the super build you're already done.

I wouldn't spend too much energy on trying to find the perfect solution. Do it one way, make it consistent and make sure the documentation is clear.

Right now my main criticism of the documentation is that it is trying to explain too much from the start (it is a reference, not a Quickstart). I don't want to read all of it. I just need to know if a) MAVSDK is for me (why should I use it) and b) give me the shell commands to get going in 3 minutes and c) give me a simple example.

That should be in the Quickstart and maybe even in the README. Look at what Homebrew does:
https://brew.sh

While I perfectly agree with you about the documentation, I don't think I would want the superbuild to update the submodules. Sometimes I want to test with different states of the submodules (`mavlink/` and/or `proto/`).

We could add logic similar to PX4, which shows a message to the user ("your submodules are not in the state we expect. If you're not an expert, type 'key', ..."). But this brings its own kind of complexity and confusion (which may be necessary for PX4, but which I believe is not for MAVSDK).

I would vote for merging that with #949 and I'll work on improving the documentation, if that's okay for you.
Cool.
Closing in favor of #949.

```

answer_comments.body:

title: Support cameras without camera definition file

body:
Currently, MAVSDK requires that cameras have a camera definition file, otherwise the camera plugin fails:

```
[08:23:45|Info ] Downloading camera definition from:  (camera_impl.cpp:1074)
[08:23:45|Error] Error while downloading text, curl error code: URL using bad/illegal format or missing URL (curl_wrapper.cpp:38)

However, the [spec](https://mavlink.io/en/messages/common.html#CAMERA_INFORMATION) says:

> Camera definition URI (if any, otherwise only basic functions will be available).

So it seems like this should be a supported case.

answer_comments.body:
MAVSDK will try to download the camera definition file 3 times and then it will give up. Does that give you issues (like does it crash), or is it just that you don't want to see those error messages?

Would you mind trying it and opening a PR if that solves your problem? :blush:

title: TCP connection from MAVSDK breaks app after 16 minutes of idle time due to reconnection
author: fibonacci-matrix
body:
I'm developing an app that uses MAVSDK to connect to a device via the built-in MAVSDK TCP connection. MAVSDK has an excellent TCP reconnection mechanism that fits my requirements well, namely the possibility of temporary disconnection. In this case timer is started, which checks every second whether the connection has been restored. But after 16 minutes, this mechanism breaks my app with the message **"socket errorToo many open files"**. 

I did some basic research and the problem is that the MAVSDK in a loop reopens the sockets, but does not close them with the `close` function in case of unsuccessful execution of the `connect` function. 

```
// from tcp_connection.cpp

_socket_fd = socket(AF_INET, SOCK_STREAM, 0);
```

I have tested basic fix on Linux, but I don't know if it will work on other operating systems

title: Maintain a connection instance per component in case of UDP
author: shakthi-prashanth-m
body:
Right now we've maintain one connection per System (one or more components).
This creates problem if there are more than one component in a system.

Consider below scenario:

- After we receive heartbeat from a component A of a system on udp port (say, 14540), we fill source ip/port details as part of connection instance. When we receive heartbeat from another component B of the same system, **_Core assumes System IP may be changed due to Wifi disconnection._**
- While we're sending commands/messages, we need to make sure we send to IP/Port of the corresponding component whom it is meant to be.

I think, to support multi-component in core, we shall have one connection per component. We should map each component with its connection to make this happen.

Please provide better suggestions, if any.
It is linked to #304 . And hopefully the fix should be part of #310 .

answer_comments.body:
Thanks @shakthi-prashanth-m. This is indeed something to think about. We're getting into the mavlink networking territory which is anything but trivial and not properly specced.

We can also have cases where there are two connections, one UDP (wifi) and one serial (a long range radio) to the same system possibly including more than one component.

The other question is if we should ever send commands to a specific component or if we can always send it on all connections and hope it will arrive in some way.

What cmake version is this?

In theory it should compile because it does so in CI. So if you replicate the steps and environment from GitHub Actions it "should just work".

By the way, you can just put ``` around code blocks.
Oh, I see, you're trying to build with MingW64. That's not officially supported. I'm sorry you're on your own. The recommendation is to use MSVC.

I remember battling these. It's frustrating and I don't understand this stuff. Maybe that's why I don't develop for Windows.

Given the errors are with gtest, you can try building without testing:
```
-DBUILD_TESTING=OFF
```

Sure! Good idea! :blush:

I would just like to add a +1 requesting this feature. Especially for UTM applications, which are taking positions in WGS84 coordinates, it'll be very useful to set the own vehicles's position using the same reference frame. Incoming coordinates are not only other vehicle's positions (see [UTM_GLOBAL_POSITION](https://mavlink.io/en/messages/common.html#UTM_GLOBAL_POSITION)), but might also be temporary and stationary geofences (for obstacles, but also dynamically closed sections of the airspace).

Using the follow-me mode or goto location might be a short-term workaround, but not a good solution, because follow-me is intended for something else (and might interfere with the mobile QGC app setting the target position) and goto has no connection loss failsafe like offboard control. Also the pilot should always have the opportunity to disable control of the companion, which would not be possible using goto. (If I understood the message's documentation correctly, receiving the message once will switch to hold mode with a custom position. Such a mode change might not always be a reasonable choice.)
Hi, I added it in this [PR](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/pull/1620)

author: JonasVautherin
body:
Instead of sharing one gRPC server between all the plugins, each plugin should have a companion library implementing its own gRPC server.

title: Add support for NED missions
author: hamishwillee
body:
Generally when writing "reusable" drone applications and examples it is much better to be able to specify positions in NED co-ordinates rather than absolute positioning - because then you can specify a pattern of movement and re-use it as needed.

NED missions are supported by MAVLink, but not PX4. The proposal is to add a sensible API in DroneCore with a backend that can be replaced by PX4 support when that comes available.

linked_issues.title: Example Fly mission uses hard-coding of mission points

comments.body: The PX4 side might not be that far off. https://github.com/PX4/Firmware/pull/7432

@shakthi-prashanth-m So caveat here, is that I don't know anything much about "NED" missions in mavlink other than that apparently they exist. We'd have to start by looking at what MAVLink expects to supply and work out our API from there. 

That said, I am *assuming* NED waypoints would be just like NED goto commands - relative to the home position OR to the current vehicle position rather than a GPS position. The API would look something like:
```
add_waypoint(north_m, east_m, down_m)
```
I suspect that the mission would define the frame globally (ie relative to home or current vehicle body), though depending on what PX4/MAVLink supports, it might be possible to supply a different frame for each mission item.
@hamishwillee I hope you didn't mean Offboard position control. Did you ?
@shakthi-prashanth-m No. Though I'd expect the sort of things you could do would be the same - ie specify a position relative to your current position.

title: Server plugin should not receive commands that are addressed to other components.
author: slovak194
body:
Hi!

I'm working on multiple cameras using [mavlink camera protocol](https://mavlink.io/en/services/camera.html) as it is [not supported so far](https://mavsdk.mavlink.io/main/en/cpp/api_reference/classmavsdk_1_1_camera.html).

While browsing the source code I've noticed, that it seems the **component_id** field is missing in MAVLinkCommandIntHandlerTableEntry and MAVLinkCommandLongHandlerTableEntry which may be used to filter out commands sent to another component in a system (in a similar way as it is implemented for mavlink_message_handler)

As for now every camera server will process and react to all commands regardless if the component ID matches its own_component_id. For example, if I select camera and subscribe to video_stream_info - all cameras will send ack and video_stream_info message, which seems wrong to me.
This may be simply fixed as it is done [here](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/30825da62876b8437a9c06f11fe6ad77d79c8136/src/mavsdk/plugins/tracking_server/tracking_server_impl.cpp#L316):
But I'm not sure if this is the right place/level where it has to be done.

Many thanks!

Best regards,
Alex

answer_comments.body:
Thanks for the issue. I think I understand the issue but disagree on the implementation change that you suggest.

The issue is that a server plugin is tied to a component in the first place, so it should not receive commands that are addressed to other components.

The filtering is supposed to happen somewhere in [mavsdk_impl.cpp](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/30825da62876b8437a9c06f11fe6ad77d79c8136/src/mavsdk/core/mavsdk_impl.cpp#L414) but it's not. I think you're right that components receive all messages, even if they are targeted at other components only.

It looks like that the message handler has the appropriate interface:

https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/973c663f9776130cce9f3cc7b05cb432c4f16254/src/mavsdk/core/mavlink_message_handler.cpp#L26

but it's not used. We need to find a way to use it from server components.
Turns out this component ID filter is to filter for source, for multiple camera plugins (not camera server plugins).

Having looked at this a bit more it looks like your suggestion was pretty close. We don't actually have to add the component ID into the handler table because we can get it from the parent server component.

Can you check if https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/pull/2270 fixes your problem?

title: pthread library perhaps should be linked to libdronelink.a
author: shakthi-prashanth-m
body:
Hi Julian, as we see that DroneLink is built as a [static library](https://github.com/PX4/DroneLink/blob/master/CMakeLists.txt#L52); why so ? Is it not meant to be used by multiple applications ?

And, `libdronelink.a` itself [uses threads](https://github.com/PX4/DroneLink/blob/master/core/udp_connection.h#L7); but it is not linked to pthread lib. The [example takeoff_and_land](https://github.com/PX4/DroneLink/blob/master/example/takeoff_and_land.cpp#L8) itself is using threads so linking thread make sense.
But if an application doesn't intend to use threads don't link it as part of their build; then app build would fail again for the same reason! 

Ideally, `libdronelink.a ` should be linked to pthread library. And, I think its not possible if its static library.
Please share your thoughts about this and correct me if I am wrong.

Thanks.
Shakthi

answer_comments.body:
> Hi Julian, as we see that DroneLink is built as a static library; why so ?

The current build as a static library easily allows to build it for iOS and Android. I'm not sure if and how that is possible with a dynamic library.

> And, libdronelink.a itself uses threads; but it is not linked to pthread lib

It is linked to a thread library, check: https://github.com/PX4/DroneLink/blob/master/CMakeLists.txt#L12, however pthread does not get included into a static lib because [pthread seems to be part of glibc](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/10390584/force-gcc-to-static-link-e-g-pthreads-and-not-dynamic-link#answer-10390911).

I'm open for suggestions and changes but I need to understand what exacly the problem is. In my opinion, linking to pthread is possible.

Looking at [MissionItem](https://mavsdk.mavlink.io/develop/en/api_reference/classmavsdk_1_1_mission_item.html) it seems you are correct - it has gimbal yaw, but not vehicle yaw (which may differ).
@julianoes any reason not to support setting ROI too?

----

That said, this should not be "somewhat random". The way this works in MAVLink is that the [waypoint-like-items](https://mavlink.io/en/messages/common.html#MAV_CMD_NAV_WAYPOINT) have a yaw field. If the yaw is explicitly specified then that will be used. If the yaw is a NaN the vehicle will point towards whatever the system setting is (that is set using parameters, and default to "the next waypoint". 
The yaw can also be affected by the gimbal and ROI. 

If you were working in raw mavlink then I'd suggest calling the command to set an ROI. Not sure what to do now, but Julian probably will be!

title: Odemetry Telemetry message subscription does not persist after reboot
author: BestITUserEUW
body:
Hey,
  i'm currently trying to integrate mavsdk::Telemetry::Odometry into my application. I'm using the following to subscribe to Odometry telemetry:

Subscription:

> telemetry->set_rate_odometry(1);
telemetry->subscribe_odometry(
    [&](mavsdk::Telemetry::Odometry odometry)
    {
        ....
    });

Reboot Command:

> mavsdk::MavlinkPassthrough::CommandLong{
            sysId,
            compId,
            static_cast<uint16_t>(MAV_CMD::MAV_CMD_PREFLIGHT_REBOOT_SHUTDOWN),
            1.0F,
            0.0F,
            0.0F,
            0.0F,
            0.0F,
            0.0F,
            0.0F};

When rebooting PX4 Autopilot i stop getting messages  from Odometry subscription. When restarting the application i receive Odometry again. Do i have to set message rates again after each reboot ?

PX4 Version: 1.13.3
Mavsdk Version: v1.4.6
System: Quadcopter

answer_comments.body:
> Do i have to set message rates again after each reboot ?

I don't know exactly how this is implemented on the PX4 side, but it could well be. MAVSDK [sends the MAV_CMD_SET_MESSAGE_INTERVAL command](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/main/src/mavsdk/core/system_impl.cpp#L1211C23-L1211C51), which is specified [here](https://mavlink.io/en/messages/common.html#MAV_CMD_SET_MESSAGE_INTERVAL).

I don't see anything in the specs that say that it should or should not be persistent, it only mentions a default value:

> 0: request default rate (which may be zero).

I would personally just request it every time, to be sure. An alternative would be to check how the default value is set on the PX4 side (maybe it's a param?), and you could set it yourself for your drone.

Yes, you have to set it each time.

If you want to have messages sent out at all times, make sure to use the correct telemetry mode on the PX4 side (see param: https://docs.px4.io/v1.14/en/advanced_config/parameter_reference.html#MAV_0_MODE).

Or set up a `mavlink stream ...` command in the PX4 startup, either by modifying the startup scripts directly, or from SD card: https://docs.px4.io/main/en/concept/system_startup.html#starting-additional-applications-extras-txt

get_entries()

get_entries()

If that works, it would show that there is a significant delay on that link.

Also, does MAVSDK work other than get_entries? E.g. can you take a photo, receive telemetry, stuff like that? Just to know if mavlink messages can go from your MAVSDK code to PX4 and back.
This has been improved with v2 and fixed up recently. I'll close this for now.

title: Enable serial and TCP connections for backend
author: julianoes
body:
The backend currently only supports UDP and the port is hardcoded for the backend_bin.

We should use `add_any_connection`, so that we can pass any connection URI.

answer_comments.body: @shrit: Would you have examples illustrating what you mean (instead of the connection URI)?
We already support shortening where applicable, e.g. `udp://` will use the default port on localhost.

I would argue that's too rare of a use case. I would then just have the cli be a list, e.g.: `foo udp://:14540 udp://:14541` and then loop through it.

And note that you can have several vehicles connecting on the same UDP port at the same time, so you don't need a port per vehicle.

title: `set_root_directory()` does not set the root directory (FTP)
author: thomasteisberg
body:
The [`set_root_directory`](http://mavsdk-python-docs.s3-website.eu-central-1.amazonaws.com/plugins/ftp.html#mavsdk.ftp.Ftp.set_root_directory) function is supposed to update the local root directory for the FTP service by updating `_root_dir` in `MavlinkFtp`.

I added `LogWarn() << "_root_dir: " << _root_dir;` to the `_work_list()` function and it still prints the default value of `_root_dir` (which is `.`) even after calling `set_root_directory`.

**To reproduce:** The easiest thing is to run the FTP server example (https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/main/examples/ftp_server/ftp_server.cpp) and try passing in different root directories. No matter what you pass in, the root directory will always be set to the current working directory (i.e. `.`, the default value of `_root_dir`).

Big thanks for @julianoes for helping me work through this and some other FTP issues.

I'm guessing this is going to be a simple fix, but I can't see the issue and Julian hasn't had time, so I'm making this issue in the hopes that someone else might see what's going wrong.

title: Rename to MAVLink SDK
author: JonasVautherin
body:
There are some concerns with the "Dronecode" branding of the project, such as:

* Confusion between the Dronecode Foundation and the SDK
* Confusion on slack (#sdk vs #dronecode)
* Makes it sound like it is limited to PX4 and may be offensive to other communities (even though there is some work regarding adding support for APM in #728)

The proposition here is to rename it to "MAVLink SDK", as it is a MAVLink implementation and a high-level API in different languages. As a consequence, the project would move to the MAVLink organization.

And RFC has been open on the [MAVLink repo](https://github.com/mavlink/rfcs/pull/15) to see if that would be acceptable from the MAVLink side.

Please feel free to share your opinion and discuss it here :blush:!

answer_comments.body:
> I'd like to add that as a MAVLink SDK it will need MAVLink command passthrough functions to provide complete MAVLink functionality.

That's not the intent and not easily possible. The intent is to provide an SDK with certain functionality which uses MAVLink under the hood for the communcation to the drone. However, it does not necessarily expose the MAVLink API. If the raw MAVLink API is required, an implementation of MAVLink in a specific programming language should be used instead.

For the C++ library it is possible to export the C API as a passthrough / backdoor. However, if this API would be passed on to the language bindings, either all of the MAVLink messages would need to be added to the protobuf messaging or everything would need to be assembled at runtime which would require the SDK to parse the whole xml MAVLink definitions.

Thanks @laurenwinter for the comment!

I agree with Julian, though, and I would like to add that IMO, the passthrough is not a very nice way to provide "complete MAVLink functionality" (as in: not super elegant, not community-friendly, and soon not faster). Let's compare what it (currently) takes to add a feature to the SDK and what it takes to use the passthrough (again, that's my opinion and maybe I am missing something there):

### SDK

1. Define the API as a proto definition
2. Implement the mavlink logic in a C++ plugin
3. Implement the gRPC server boilerplate to bring that to the language bindings (Swift, Python, Java, ...)
4. Auto-generate the language bindings

### Passthrough

A. Define the interface for the new features (not necessary, but any readable piece of code would likely do it: that is about putting one feature in one function)
B. Implement the mavlink logic through the passthrough

Note that:

* 1 is trivial and corresponds to A.
* 2 corresponds to B.
* 3 is currently "boilerplate" to write, but we are working on having that auto-generated (that's one of the top priorities). Once finished, it will be merged with 4.
* 4 comes almost for free ("just run the auto-generation script").

As a conclusion, I understand that the passthrough may seem faster to implement now (because of 3), but we are putting a lot of effort into removing the costs related to 3.
Also, what is implemented into the SDK is "contributed" to the community in all the supported languages, whereas whatever is written with the passthrough will never come back upstream, and is technically limited to C++. And in that sense, using the passthrough goes "against" the community.

Not sure if that makes sense, but under those conditions, I don't see a use-case that actually wants the mavlink passthrough. What I believe you want is the full auto-generation, and we are working hard on that! :blush:.
Back to the topic of this issue, it seems to have more activity on the [MAVLink RFC](https://github.com/mavlink/rfcs/pull/15), so let's close this one in favor of the RFC.

title: How to use the `set_always_send_heartbeats` of Configuration
author: flaviol-souza
body:
I'm building on a sample Proxy Mavlink with MAVSDK between QGC and PX4 (SITL).
I would like to know how to use the ``set_always_send_heartbeats`` of Configuration for Autopilot even if it is defined as false. 
`Mavsdk::Configuration custom_config(1, 1, false);
 custom_config.set_always_send_heartbeats(false);
 Mavsdk mavsdk_px4{custom_config}; `

This attribute is reset to true in MavsdkImpl::add_udp_connection when the ``add_any_connection`` is called (which seems to me to be a bug).

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8ea31776-d969-48c6-b85a-a384d7fca119)

answer_comments.body:
The configuration option is set internally depending on the connection you add. If you are sending UDP messages to another IP (instead of listening on a local port) you need to send something to initiate the connection and allow the counterpart to send anything back. Otherwise, the communication can't really start.

What are you trying to do exactly? What sort of connections are you adding?

I see, thanks for the context. That's quite involved.

I can see how this automatic option does not work for you, but I also don't want to break the behavior for existing users.

One workaround I can think of is to intercept the outgoing messages and drop the heartbeats manually, using:
https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/v2.12/src/mavsdk/core/include/mavsdk/mavsdk.h#L422-L434

Would that work?

comments.body:
The configuration option is set internally depending on the connection you add. If you are sending UDP messages to another IP (instead of listening on a local port) you need to send something to initiate the connection and allow the counterpart to send anything back. Otherwise, the communication can't really start.

What are you trying to do exactly? What sort of connections are you adding?

@julianoes 
I am creating a "MAVLink Proxy" using MAVSDK. The primary purpose of the Proxy is to act as a MAVLIN message broker between QGroundControl (QGC) and PX4 SITL. This proxy intercepts all MAVLink messages sent between the two components (QGC and PX4) via ``subscribe_message`` of MavlinkPassthrough. Later, when the other component connects, the message is forwarded to the destination.

The basic flow is:

1. QGC connects to the Proxy, but believes it is connected directly to PX4 (`Mavsdk::Configuration mavsdk_px4{Mavsdk::Configuration{Mavsdk::ComponentType::Autopilot}};`).
2. The PX4 connects to the Proxy, but believes it is connected directly to the QGC (`Mavsdk mavsdk_qgc{Mavsdk::Configuration{Mavsdk::ComponentType::GroundStation}};`).
3. The Proxy transparently forwards MAVLink messages between the two.

**Challenges Found**

1. **Automatic HEARTBEAT Messages from the Proxy (MAVSDK)**:
- When I configure MAVSDK for `ComponentType::Autopilot`, it sends automatic `HEARTBEAT` messages to initiate communication with the QGC.
- These `HEARTBEAT` messages generated by the Proxy (with default values, such as `type == 0`) are mixed with the real messages from the PX4, causing problems in the QGC behavior. For example, the QGC constantly switches between the "PreFlight" and "Custom" states. That's why the QGC doesn't understand that the PX4 is ready for flight, releasing the Take Off commands, for example.

2. **Internal Behavior of `set_always_send_heartbeats`**:
- I explicitly configured `set_always_send_heartbeats(false)` in `Mavsdk::Configuration`. However, when the `add_any_connection` function is called, the attribute is reset to `true` in the `add_udp_connection` method due to the internal logic of MAVSDK.
I understand the justification for sending `HEARTBEAT` when adding an outgoing UDP connection, but in this case, the Proxy should act as a passive (reactive) intermediary. In other words, it should not send `HEARTBEAT` messages automatically; it should just redirect the real messages from the PX4 to the QGC and vice versa.

My goal is to completely disable the sending of `HEARTBEAT` messages automatically generated by MAVSDK in the Proxy. I would like:
- The Proxy is to send MAVLink messages to the QGC only when it receives a message from the PX4, and vice versa.
- No `HEARTBEAT` messages are generated or sent by the Proxy in normal situations.

I see, thanks for the context. That's quite involved.

I can see how this automatic option does not work for you, but I also don't want to break the behavior for existing users.

One workaround I can think of is to intercept the outgoing messages and drop the heartbeats manually, using:
https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/v2.12/src/mavsdk/core/include/mavsdk/mavsdk.h#L422-L434

Would that work?

Thank you for the suggestion! 

I tested the approach of intercepting outgoing messages and manually dropping the heartbeats using the `intercept_outgoing_messages_async()` method, and it worked perfectly for my use case. I implemented an MAVLink proxy that forwards messages between PX4 and QGroundControl while filtering specific messages as needed.

To help others with similar requirements, I have created an example and submitted it as a pull request: [#2467](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/pull/2467). This example demonstrates how to set up an MAVLink proxy using `MavlinkPassthrough` and includes message interception and forwarding logic.

Thank you again for pointing me in the right direction!

title: What's the difference between telemetry.unix_epoch_time() and telemetry.subscribe_unix_epoch_time() ?
author: AlexisAlexisM
body:
What's the difference between telemetry.unix_epoch_time() and telemetry.subscribe_unix_epoch_time() ?

With the first method it seems that the time does not change, while it changes with the second

Ty

answer_comments.body:
> What's the difference between telemetry.unix_epoch_time() and telemetry.subscribe_unix_epoch_time() ?

- [subscribe_unix_epoch_time](https://mavsdk.mavlink.io/main/en/cpp/api_reference/classmavsdk_1_1_telemetry.html#classmavsdk_1_1_telemetry_1a172eb7793c61744a8195e38c0612ec1f) gives you a subscription, so your callback will be called each time a message with that information arrives in MAVSDK. This is an async API.
- [unix_epoch_time](https://mavsdk.mavlink.io/main/en/cpp/api_reference/classmavsdk_1_1_telemetry.html#classmavsdk_1_1_telemetry_1ab5ea5f6bb35b5670e34d5697d8c880f4) just gives you the latest value at the time when you query it. This is a polling based API that you call every time you want to know the value.

> Should I use set_rate_unix_epoch_time when I subscribe ?

It depends whether you want or require a certain rate. If your autopilot already sends it at an acceptable rate, you don't have to. If it doesn't send it at all, then yes, you have to request it.

> Should I use a mutex inside of subscribe callback?

If you are writing or reading shared data from different threads (which the subscription callback is), then likely, yes, you want to add a mutex around the data, or use a `std::atomic` if it's just one value you set.

title: Timesync adjusting outgoing message timestamps
author: jkflying
body:
The usual method for timesync with mavlink is that outgoing messages are sent with the sender's clock source, and the receiver should translate it into their own time frame. However, we've seen now with MAVSDK that after an initial timesync exchange it adjusts the clock source for _outgoing_ messages. This causes massive confusion on the flight controller side, since it was trying to adjust timestamps on incoming messages to what the clock source on MAVSDK was _before_ it did the timesync. This might be the root cause of #960 ? It can also cause instability in both timesync algorithms since they try to estimate each other when the offset is constantly changing, instead of estimating a single offset which should be mostly constant.

To fix this, outgoing messages should be timestamped with a consistent clock source (preferably CLOCK_MONOTONIC_RAW, ie something that isn't affected by time jumps or temporary clock slewing on the host system), and only incoming messages should be adjusted via the timesync message.

FYI @irsdkv , @JonasVautherin suggested I tag you since you contributed this. Do you see any problems here? Would you have time to fix this?

Thanks @DanielePettenuzzo for the investigation.

I can be wrong, but in my mind current MAVSDK tymesync mechanism (https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/pull/890) shouldn't cause these problems. Similar behavior [implemented in ROS](https://github.com/mavlink/mavros/blob/master/mavros/src/plugins/sys_time.cpp).

UPD. 
Unfortunately now I haven't much time to figure it out so I can just try to help, sorry.

Reading through your PR I don't see a problem there, everything looks good. However it looks like it has been changed since then: https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/8afd4640cebf4fae242a9ff9650d354cebab2f48/src/core/timesync.cpp#L42
It now responds with the offset from autopilot time, not system time, which is exactly the problem we now see on flight control side.

> it has been changed since then:

Yes it is related to https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/pull/934

More about this solution:

1. Source:
https://github.com/mavlink/mavros/blob/master/mavros/src/plugins/sys_time.cpp#L310

2. I think it can be a bad solution if `ros::Time::now()` is a host-machine time, not local adjusted clocks.

So I can understand that it might be a problem if we want to have MAVSDK at the same time as MAVROS running, because each of these is only designed to sync with a single external source.

What #934 does breaks the assumption of the timesync module in the Firmware, that the MAVSDK clock has constant offset, since Firmware sends at 10Hz, so gets responses and estimates the MAVSDK time offset before the MAVSDK has the firmware offset and shifts the clock in the first big step.

Perhaps one way (it feels a bit hacky) is to not respond to external timesync messages until the first timesync has completed with the autopilot. So [this line ](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/8afd4640cebf4fae242a9ff9650d354cebab2f48/src/core/timesync.cpp#L45) needs to have something like `&& timesync_set` which is set true when the autopilot time is actually updated.

The 'proper' solution, a lot more work, is to fix the MAVSDK/Firmware/MAVROS to have multiple timesync offsets, based on component ID.

title: Subscribing to multiple vehicles from a single udp port
author: Jaeyoung-Lim
body:
I am trying to use other vehicle's position / velocity information to de-conflict paths when operating multiple vehicles. However, mavsdk seems to enforce the constraint that there can be only one system on a single udp port.

https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/e7f80158d7fc4f9526d3641eb595440777005dc6/src/core/mavsdk_impl.cpp#L291-L312

This means that in order to subscribe to other vehicles (vehicles with different sysIDs) we need to have prior knowledge of what ports the vehicle will be located to. However, such circumstance is unrealistic and I believe most realistic scenarios it would be even hard to know how many vehicles would be in the network. 

Would there be a way to subscribe mavlnk information of multiple vehicles from a single udp port? or if we this need to be added, how could it be done?

answer_comments.body: That should be perfectly possible - mavlink differentiates vehicles my SysId/component id, not UDP address. Whether or not it handles the case is another matter.

You are quoting `get_system()`, but I think you are interested in [`get_system(const uint64_t uuid)`](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/e7f80158d7fc4f9526d3641eb595440777005dc6/src/core/mavsdk_impl.cpp#L314-L324), which allows you to get the system that corresponds to a UUID. 

And you get a list of discovered systems with [`register_on_discover`](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/e7f80158d7fc4f9526d3641eb595440777005dc6/src/core/mavsdk.h#L230).

Does that help?
The API to access multiple vehicles has been changed. I think this issue has been resolved, otherwise please re-open @Jaeyoung-Lim.

Alternatively, you can make a pull request to https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK-Proto/blob/master/protos/telemetry/telemetry.proto to extend the Telemetry plugin to include an API for Raw GPS.

For `GLOBAL_POSITION_INT` there are these https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/6e2607de8b84c16fe65c37a9dd7f7696265d4f0b/src/plugins/telemetry/include/plugins/telemetry/telemetry.h#L810-L820.
This has been added, see https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/pull/1333.

title: Race condition bug
author: JoC2000
body:
### Issue:
Specific race condition between [send_capture_status](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/3e26666176bad4a1df51575808fc05ec494abea9/cpp/src/mavsdk/plugins/camera_server/camera_server_impl.cpp#L1370)  and [send_tracking_status_with_interval](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/3e26666176bad4a1df51575808fc05ec494abea9/cpp/src/mavsdk/plugins/camera_server/camera_server_impl.cpp#L2140).

`send_capture_status` locks `_mutex`, before calling `queue_message` and locking `_mavlink_packet_mutex`, `send_tracking_status_with_interval` calls `queue_message`, blocking `_mavlink_packet_mutex`.
`send_capture_status` gets stuck waiting for `_mavlink_packet_mutex` and `send_tracking_status_with_interval` gets stuck for `_mutex`

```

```


I think the error of this issue is unrelated to the build type though.

comments.body:
Hi!
I think I can get on with implementing this.

Just to clarify. This error message reporting will go in the Manual Control plugin and is used if some means of control i.e. a joystick is not available?

From what I am understanding (and can confirm by testing), manual control needs a setpoint before entering the mode. This is an example for offboard `offboard->set_velocity_body({0, 0, 0, 0}); `
So, in code it looks like this:
`auto offboard = std::make_shared<Offboard>(*system);`
` offboard->set_velocity_body({0, 0, 0, 0}); /* Needed */`
`Offboard::Result offboard_result = offboard->start();`

Without the `offboard->set_velocity_body({0, 0, 0, 0}); ` then we get the Result shown in Julian's comment above (Offboard::Result::NoSetpointSet;). 

**Manual Control**
Manual Control needs to be started in a very similar fashion

`manual_control->set_manual_control_input(0.f, 0.f, 0.f, 0.f); /*Needed*/`
 `auto manual_control_result = manual_control->start_position_control();`

However, if the `manual_control->set_manual_control_input(0.f, 0.f, 0.f, 0.f);` is NOT there, manual control will not be achieved. This should be an error. However, the code returns ManualControl::Result::Success instead of a result that would indicate that manual control is not going to work. (For example: ManualControl::Result::NoSetpointSet)

**TODO**
Implement something like ManualControl::Result::NoSetpointSet that will tell the developer they need to insert `manual_control->set_manual_control_input(0.f, 0.f, 0.f, 0.f); ` into their code

@julianoes is that a fair analysis?

title: Local validation of PX4 parameter values
author: shakthi-prashanth-m
body:
When a plugin perform `set_param_float_async()`, we send mavlink command to set param values. We can save time by locally validating values if we maintain (Min, Max, Default) range for each parameter may be in an XML file (similar to QGroundControl).
```
    <parameter default="8.0" name="NAV_MIN_FT_HT" type="FLOAT">
      <short_desc>Minimum follow target altitude</short_desc>
      <long_desc>The minimum height in meters relative to home for following a target</long_desc>
      <min>8.0</min>
      <unit>meters</unit>
      <scope>modules/navigator</scope>
    </parameter>
```

title: Issue of Mission Execution and Manual Input Priority
author: liu12344321
body:
When the "manual_control.set_manual_control_input"s value keeps changing, I want to execute a mission or other automode. In such a case, the value needs to remain consistent before and after the mission is triggered; otherwise, the mission will be interrupted. However, I’ve noticed that even if I set the manual value right before executing the mission, and then immediately trigger the task, it still gets interrupted. It turns out that I have to wait several hundred milliseconds after setting the value before executing the mission. It seems that the mission has a higher priority, even if the command is input later, the flight controller receives and processes it first.

Then I looked into the source code and found that these two types of commands follow different paths，one goes through a queue, while the other is sent directly as a command. So now I’m wondering: how can I make the information in the queue be delivered faster, so that I don’t have to wait for several hundred milliseconds?

Im current using v3.3.0
Thanks.

comments.body: I'm not following. What are you trying to do and what is the problem exactly? And is this with PX4 or ArduPilot?

@julianoes Im using PX4.
I want to implement the following use case: the drone is originally flying in mission mode, and my onboard vision computer monitors the environment. When an obstacle is detected, it will intervene and interrupt the mission. Once the obstacle is cleared and it's safe to proceed, I want to resume the mission.

The problem lies in resuming the mission. For example, initially I send set_manual_control_input(0, 0, 1, 0) to take control. Then, when I want to hand control back to the mission, I set set_manual_control_input(0, 0, 0.5, 0) and immediately call mission.start_mission(). After that, I continuously send set_manual_control_input(0, 0, 0.5, 0).

However, the resumed mission gets interrupted again right away. I believe this is because the earlier manual control input set_manual_control_input(0, 0, 1, 0) is still considered active by the flight controller. To avoid this, I have to wait a few hundred milliseconds after sending the first set_manual_control_input(0, 0, 0.5, 0) before calling mission.start_mission().

It seems like mission.start_mission() is being sent after but received before the manual control command by the flight controller.

Ok, I think manual_control is not the right interface to do this. Instead, I would pause the mission using `mission_pause` which will go into hold.

Or, alternatively if you want to do some control to avoid the obstacle, I would do that in offboard mode, e.g. using velocity commands.

Manual control is really meant for "manual" as in human control, and not automated control like that.

Also, PX4 implements an interface for obstacle avoidance that we probably should use instead, however, it's not implemented by MAVSDK yet, and I also don't know what the state of it is in PX4, but I do know that it would be the right thing to do, at least long term.

title: Add support for MAVLink communication faking/mocking
author: hamishwillee
body: In order to allow sensible unit tests to be written.

answer_comments.body:
Unit tests are supposed to test just the functionality of a particular component. As each plugin is a MAVLink processor - sending and/or receiving MAVLink messages to unit test our code we would need to  create some  mock system that can sensibly act as a source/sink of MAVLink and respond to messages from our plugins as "required".

This would allow us  to unit test our code in isolation from other plugins and with completely repeatable behaviour, on any platform.

For our integration tests we use SITL as a sync/source but that is no good for unit tests, because SITL requires all sort of setup, and does not respond repeatably on different systems, or even the same system on a different load. 

I have no idea what "exactly" this would look like, but I'd start by considering the QGroundControl mocklink.

Yes it could be something like a `FakeConnection` that whenever you send it a command it that is correct it would respond with ack. Additionally you could also check the failure cases such as timeouts, or responding with denied if a param doesn't make sense.

We use system tests now for that sort of thing, to test "client" vs. "server" MAVLink protocol functionality. This uses the UDP connection but it could in theory use the RawBytes direction connection instead. In any case I consider this done.

title: Return vectors by value in C++11
author: shakthi-prashanth-m
body:
In below piece of code:
https://github.com/dronecore/DroneCore/blob/a2b9db92f83e53bcce75c611f6e9b473f4341562/core/dronecore_impl.cpp#L210-L211
although we clear vector in every invocation, we made it as `static`; this is because we want to return a reference to it:
https://github.com/dronecore/DroneCore/blob/a2b9db92f83e53bcce75c611f6e9b473f4341562/core/dronecore_impl.cpp#L207


_We can return a vector **by value** in C++11, because it has move semantics, which will simply move local vector into callers' vector (hence no copying). Thus we gain advantage of time complexity._


**References:**
- http://en.cppreference.com/w/cpp/container/vector/operator%3D
- See Bjarne Stroustrup's answer in https://isocpp.org/blog/2013/01/quick-q-is-it-still-bad-practice-to-return-a-vector-from-a-function

However, this doesn't actually set up triggering on PX4. To use triggering, you have to set up the trigger pin in the Actuator setting, and then use MissionRaw and use the command [MAV_CMD_DO_SET_CAM_TRIGG_DIST](https://mavlink.io/en/messages/common.html#MAV_CMD_DO_SET_CAM_TRIGG_DIST), or [MAV_CMD_DO_SET_CAM_TRIGG_INTERVAL](https://mavlink.io/en/messages/common.html#MAV_CMD_DO_SET_CAM_TRIGG_INTERVAL)

However, this doesn't actually set up triggering on PX4. To use triggering, you have to set up the trigger pin in the Actuator setting, and then use MissionRaw and use the command [MAV_CMD_DO_SET_CAM_TRIGG_DIST](https://mavlink.io/en/messages/common.html#MAV_CMD_DO_SET_CAM_TRIGG_DIST), or [MAV_CMD_DO_SET_CAM_TRIGG_INTERVAL](https://mavlink.io/en/messages/common.html#MAV_CMD_DO_SET_CAM_TRIGG_INTERVAL)
@JonasVautherin @julianoes This is probably a PX4 question too, but there is no "Actuators" menu in my QGC, is that because I selected the wrong or an incompatible airframe?
I don't know. This seems to come up again and again and I just don't seem to get a straight answer.

> @JonasVautherin @julianoes This is probably a PX4 question too, but there is no "Actuators" menu in my QGC, is that because I selected the wrong or an incompatible airframe?

I could solve this just going to the airframe file in /init.d/airframes, disable the mixer and enabling the SYS_CTRL_ALLOC, and then setting all the necessary PWM functions up. In my case, i set `param set-default PWM_AUX_FUNC5 2000  # Camera trigger` for the pwm trigger.

After this i could see the Actuators menu in QGC.

Then, to trigger, make sure you set up the parameters for TRIG_PWM_NEUTRAL and TRIG_PWM_SHOOT. also you could set the TRIG_INTERFACE to generic pwm and TRIG_MODE to 1 for example.

To activate the trigger just send a pymavlink command long [MAV_CMD_DO_SET_CAM_TRIGG_DIST](https://mavlink.io/en/messages/common.html#MAV_CMD_DO_SET_CAM_TRIGG_DIST) and wait for ACK
Awesome, thanks for documenting this. So we can close this? I assume it will get a bit more straightforward once v1.14 is out and the actuator config in QGC shows up by default.

title: Disconnection Issue with Ardupilot Flight Controller on serial port
author: yangqunfeng
body: The C++ mavsdk-based onboard computer program connects to the Ardupilot flight controller through Telem2. After establishing the connection, the flight controller will automatically disconnect after a random duration. Later, through the serial port debugging tool, I found that the flight controller’s Telem2 port had no MAVLink data stream output. However, after restarting the flight controller software using Mission Planner (MP), data returned and the connection was re-established correctly (I ruled out hardware issues through this). Once the serial port detects that the flight controller has disconnected, even if I restart my control program, it still cannot reconnect. I later tried using a TCP/UDP connection to the flight controller, but the disconnection issue persisted. However, sometimes after about half an hour, the flight controller reconnects on its own. This issue has been bothering me for months. I want to know why the flight controller serial port behaves this way. From the Ardupilot wiki, I learned that there may be conflicts caused by telemetry link sharing, but I am not sure if this is the cause of the problem, since I also use Telem1 to connect to QGC. I would greatly appreciate it if anyone could help me analyze the possible causes.

[6011.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/18268933/6011.zip)

First, I use the **subscribe_on_new_system** function, which is used to callback when the flight controller connects and disconnects. Then, I create a telemetry service, but also connect to the drone through passthrough, and I set the message intervals for the following messages using MAV_CMD_SET_MESSAGE_INTERVAL. The key is the message ID, and the value is the message interval.
`const std::vector<std::pair<uint32_t, float>> message_intervals = {
        {MAVLINK_MSG_ID_GPS_RAW_INT, 500000.0f},
        {MAVLINK_MSG_ID_GLOBAL_POSITION_INT, 500000.0f},

`
I have created the corresponding callback functions to receive messages such as **Global Position** and **Raw Position**, and I check whether the position information is being returned at the specified frequency. By the way (a side note), when I previously used MAVSDK version 2.0.1, when I detected that the drone hadn't sent the subscribed messages for a while, I would again use MAV_CMD_SET_MESSAGE_INTERVAL to resubscribe to the messages. Although the drone would occasionally disconnect, it didn't happen as frequently as it does now.
I am sure the issue might be with my program, mainly because the QGC (Ground Control Station) doesn't show the drone disconnecting, but my program does.
I also want to ask if the message intervals I’ve set are feasible, particularly {MAVLINK_MSG_ID_GPS_RAW_INT, 500000.0f} and {MAVLINK_MSG_ID_GLOBAL_POSITION_INT, 500000.0f}. title: [Discussion] How to set a parameter and reboot the vehicle for PX4 MAVSDK SITL Test
author: junwoo091400
body:
## What I want to do
I wanted to have the following feature on [MAVSDK Test](https://github.com/PX4/PX4-Autopilot/tree/main/test/mavsdk_tests) in PX4 SITL:
1. Set the parameter in PX4 (to set it to a non-default value)
2. Reboot the vehicle (Or start the vehicle directly with the modified parameter from the beginning)
3. Perform a SITL MAVSDK test with the vehicle that had the modified parameter when it booted up

The reason for this was for the [Payload delivery SITL test PR](https://github.com/PX4/PX4-Autopilot/pull/20230), I needed a way to set the parameter and reboot the vehicle, in order to have the startup script recognize the non-default parameter to enable the `payload_deliverer` module, and start the module, which is necessary for payload delivery feature.

## Problem
Currently it seems like we can't arbitrarily set the parameter before booting up, neither can we reboot the vehicle in the SITL test function.

### Proposed Solutions
1. Have a way to reboot the vehicle after setting the parameter in the mavsdk sitl test pipeline
2. Have a way to load an arbitrary / modified parameter through MAVSDK interface for the drone

## Discussion 
If we want to support such feature, what would be the best way to implement it? Are there any other solutions? Would this be possible without modifying MAVSDK?

comments.body:
So the goal of the test is to check that the parameter is set correctly after reboot, but SITL resets the params when it boots, right?

I don't really see how this is related to MAVSDK, though :thinking:. It feels like you need SITL to persist the params (instead of resetting after reboot), and that's not how SITL does it, right?

1. From what I know there is not yet a way to reboot/restart PX4 from within PX4 in SITL but only externally via helper scripts. So for the PX4 mavsdk_tests you would have to script it there.
2. You can always load/get an arbitrary param from PX4. I think that part is not a problem.

Regarding your question: to me it sounds like a test script issue around PX4, and not a MAVSDK issue as such.

But then if it requires custom code to make it work in SITL, is it really a test? It feels like params persistence after reboot is just not a SITL feature. We can simulate it with external scripts, and then we can test that those external scripts simulate it correctly, but at the end of the day it's not testing the actual feature :sweat_smile:

I think I found the solution :thinking:, which is using a custom model with the airframe file specifying the parameters that needs to be changed on startup. It is of course not scalable, but for a SITL test for a specific feature, I think this can be tolerated.

Hi, good question. You can actually just use `set_rate_gps_info` as the underlying mavlink message is the same.

@JonasVautherin should we add it nevertheless or add a comment to clarify this?

I first was thinking about adding it, and handling the case where somebody does `set_rate_gps_info()` AND `set_rate_raw_gps` like this:

* If both `subscribe_gps_info` and `subscribe_raw_gps` are active, use the max of both rate values
* If only one is active, take its rate

The problem is for the polling interface: what if I want to poll gps_info very fast, but subscribed to raw_gps at a slow rate? Or maybe something like:

* If both `subscribe_gps_info` and `subscribe_raw_gps` are active, use the max of both rate values
* If only one is active, take its rate
* If `set_rate_` has been called (even if the subscription is inactive), use that rate in the max computation

Which then means that if you do `set_rate_gps_info` and then only poll `raw_gps`, you see the effect of the new rate (if that rate was faster than the default). Not sure if that's a problem, though... And we should document the behavior, and maybe add a log line when `set_rate_` is being set to the lower value and is therefore ignored.

Not perfect, but that's the best I can think of to have a rather natural way of using both rates :sweat_smile:

title: Deprecate embedded camera definition files
author: JonasVautherin

answer_comments.body:
> I remember correctly, this was implemented as a temporary workaround more than a year ago, but the original intent was always to download this file from the camera.

To be very pedantic, the intent was to download _and cache_ the file from the camera using the revision number.

There is a bit of a discussion around the caching [here](https://github.com/mavlink/mavlink/issues/1198), which I haven't read/followed up yet.

Anyway, personally I wouldn't remove those files, but I would start checking the revision number and work out what you're going to do if there is a mismatch.

The thing is that right now we don't cache those files, we hardcode them. A cache should be transparent, meaning that disabling the cache should not break the functionality.

We should first have the implementation without cache, and then we could add the cache to improve performance. 

This means I agree with you, @hamishwillee. But what we have now is not a cache, it is prone to errors and it makes our build system more complex (by adding `cpp_rsc`), and that makes cross-compiling harder. So I don't think we want to build on top of that...

@JonasVautherin I'm just being pedantic on where we need to go ... eventually. Up to you what we do now.

FWIW though, it is hard to say whether removing the files completely is OK without knowing what you will do if the files cannot be downloaded or take some time to download.

title: Determine exact time fly
author: dangviethieu-hntv
body: Hi all, I have mission with take photo action each waypoints. How I can determine exact time when drone fly from waypoint to waypoint and time drone do action at waypoint?

answer_comments.body: @dangviethieu-hntv this would depend on the mission speed that you set. Given the distance you could then calculate the approximate time required to fly it.

> How about determine time drone do action at waypoint, sir? (take photo, control gimbal)

That would depend on the gimbal and camera you are using. 

Does it matter? You're never going to be able to get a perfect estimate - and omitting these is likely to be a relatively small fraction of your error.

I think the best you can do is monitor MISSION_ITEM_REACHED, which the autopilot must send whenever it gets to a new item. This is not timestamped, but it would give you a good approximation. 

It isn't as far as I know possible to get more detailed information about start and end "generically" of mission information from MAVLink. Depending on what you are doing you might be able to get a bit more of a guess for *some operations*. For example if you already know that the mission takes 4 photos at a particular place, then you could look at the messages which are broadcast and get their timestamps. However this is not something reliable, or that you would do in this kind of SDK.
This should probably happen on the autopilot side and not the MAVSDK side.

answer_comments.body: If you use C++ you can use MavlinkPassthrough to access these messages. Otherwise, you'd have to make a pull request for the telemetry module to add the data that you require.

In the MAVSDK superbuild, when building mavlink, there is a [`-DMAVLINK_DIALECT`](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/main/third_party/mavlink/CMakeLists.txt#L9) which is [set by the superbuild](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/main/CMakeLists.txt#L8).

So it should work if you make a clean build of MAVSDK, and in the configure step (the first one, which has something like `-Bbuild/default` in it), add `-DMAVLINK_DIALECT=ardupilotmega`.

You can now use https://mavsdk.mavlink.io/main/en/cpp/api_reference/classmavsdk_1_1_mavlink_direct.html.

Also see:
https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/tree/main/examples/mavlink_direct
