title: Different connections to the same system
author: eastman-bechamo
body:
I have a MAVLink-enabled autopilot that I'm connecting to from a PC using MAVSDK. I'd like to communicate with the AP using two different connections, one USB and one UART. I can connect to the AP using either one, but it doesn't seem that I'm able to connect to both at the same time.

Specifically, my approach is to call `add_any_connection` twice and get two different `System` pointers. From those pointers, I want to create two `MavlinkPassthrough`s so that I can send custom MAVLink messages directly to the device.

Is this possible? If it is, what kind of approach should I take?

Thank you!

comments.body:
Hmm, that's not how the MAVSDK architecture works. A system is a representation for a MAVLink system. You only have one system, and two connections to it.

Why do you want to have two MavlinkPassthrough instances? Do you want outgoing messages to be sent on both connections (which it ought to do unless something is broken), or do you want to send specific messages on either one or the other connection?
Hi @julianoes , thanks for replying. If it's possible, I'd like to send some messages over one connection, and some over a different connection exclusively.

That's not really possible then. The only way to make that work would be to add an intercept_mavlink_messages() function per connection rather than per mavsdk instance. The problem with that would be that there is currently no public facing connection object, so it's not obvious how we would do it.

Maybe to take take a step back, what sort of filtering would you want to do? What's the idea behind it? Maybe we can add connection configuration based on something higher level, like the notion of a low bandwidth fallback link (e.g. satellite)?
Are you trying to achieve some kind of multihoming? Like having redundancy between two different links (e.g. both a radio link and an Internet link), such that messages go through the "best" path?

@JonasVautherin @julianoes I appreciate the questions, but unfortunately that's as much detail as I can give right now :(

I'll admit that I'm not extremely familiar with the architecture of MAVSDK, but how hard would it be for a system to maintain and choose between two connections?

What does a `System` require of a connection after initialization? Is there any reason that initialization couldn't happen twice for the same `System` object?

Thank you :-)

> Is there any reason that initialization couldn't happen twice for the same System object?

Conceptually, IMO because it doesn't make sense at the MAVSDK level. In terms of implementation, MAVSDK does some stuff for you in the background, so if you split the same connection between two systems, then all of that will be doubled, and will most likely conflict (`systemA` sends a command, `systemB` receives the ACK that looks like it was for itself, but is confused because it never sent a command in the first place, ...).

> unfortunately that's as much detail as I can give right now :(

Pretty hard to help then :laughing:. If I was to do multihoming, I would do it "in front" of MAVSDK, as a different component. MAVSDK would never know about it, it would just happen.
@JonasVautherin I know the lack of information is hard, my apologies. What do you mean by "in front of MAVSDK"?
Some kind of proxy like mavlink-router, running between the drone and the mavsdk instance. If that makes sense?
If you can't share why you would need a feature, that's unfortunately not quite enough incentive for me to implement/change anything to solve your challenge in your top secret project. :smirk:

title: Inconsistent documentation in Action class.
author: jwidauer
body:
In the `Action` class the function `goto_location()`s documentation specifies:  
`Send command to reposition the vehicle to a specific WGS84 global position.`

But then underneath it it states:  
`float altitude_amsl_m - Altitude AMSL in meters`

Does this mean the `altitude_amsl_m` will be converted to WGS84 internally or is this a mistake in the documentation?

answer_comments.body:
Good point, thanks for raising this.

I think this is the same that @mzahana found in Dronecode/DronecodeSDK#485 and lead me to create this issue:
https://github.com/PX4/Firmware/issues/10246

Given that, we should make sure that's documented correctly (for now) here.

~I guess the global position would refer to latitude/longitude but is excluding the  altitude.~

I'm confused, I need to check what's exactly going on and then document it.

Almost certainly it is WGS84 position, and AMSL altitude, because that is the underlying definition of the MAVLink frames: https://mavlink.io/en/messages/common.html#MAV_FRAME

This is complicated further by the fact that the actual frame might not quite match even that, depending on the positioning hardware (anecdotally, came up in a MAVLink call).

title: Support for multi-part statustext messages
author: julianoes
body:
We should add support for multipart statustext messages as specified in https://github.com/mavlink/mavlink/pull/1295.

Here https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/138ee4acebfbfa5875425048423014cb454ebee4/src/core/system_impl.cpp#L216-L258

answer_comments.body:
Good questions. I don't think we try very hard to deal with out-of-order in MAVLink in general, unless for things that are implemented to be guaranteed such as commands or a mission upload.

While a debug output is important the message is just a stream and you can potentially miss it all, that's just currently the state until we have the [events interface](https://docs.google.com/document/d/18qdDgfML97lItom09MJhngYnFzAm1zFdmlCKG7TaBpg) which deals with that using an events counter, if I remember it correctly.

Anyway, I would suggest to parse and display whatever arrives (in order) and just omit whatever does not. I think that will already bring value for most cases.

> Should we change those too?

Yes that would make sense. And there an implementation that waits for chunks if the id is set until it prints them out. and a timeout in case the final chunk does not arrive.

author: Zipdox2
body: Currently you can make install but there's no make uninstall.

answer_comments.body: If you install locally, then it's easy to delete. If you install globally on your system, I would suggest you rely on a package manager instead of doing something like `sudo make install` :+1:.

We are just using cmake. If we wanted to implement this, here is how: https://gitlab.kitware.com/cmake/community/-/wikis/FAQ#can-i-do-make-uninstall-with-cmake

I personally wouldn't bother but if you want to contribute it and maintain it going forward, feel free to make a PR.

I would honestly vote against. I am always nervous about scripts that do any kind of `rm -rf $some_variable`, and I wouldn't want to be held responsible for removing random files on a user's system.

Also installing random stuff on your system with `sudo make install` is a bad idea. That is literally the job of the package manager, it should not be done with cryptic scripts in CMake (can you honestly assure me that `"@CMAKE_COMMAND@" ARGS "-E remove \"$ENV{DESTDIR}${file}\""` will never, ever remove stuff you did not expect?).
Right agreed. Let's stick with the default cmake setup that we have now.

title: Camera plugin uses deprecated messages
author: dlech
body:
The camera plugin currently uses deprecated messages like [MAV_CMD_REQUEST_CAMERA_INFORMATION](https://mavlink.io/en/messages/common.html#MAV_CMD_REQUEST_CAMERA_INFORMATION) instead of [MAV_CMD_REQUEST_MESSAGE](https://mavlink.io/en/messages/common.html#MAV_CMD_REQUEST_MESSAGE).

This would make it unusable with a camera that only supports the "new" request message.

answer_comments.body:
I see your point, but here is my personal opinion: MAVLink "servers" should implement both in the foreseeable future, because MAVLink does not provide a way to detect which command is supported and which is not (well, there is a `MAV_CMD_ACK_ERR_NOT_SUPPORTED`, but I don't think it is mandatory nor generally implemented, and it's not enough for `MAV_CMD_REQUEST_MESSAGE` which represents subcommands).

More specifically, if we move MAVSDK to using only `MAV_CMD_REQUEST_MESSAGE`, we will break all legacy systems that don't support the new way. "Deprecated" means that it may be removed in the future, not that it is not supported anymore. MAVLink still supports them, so MAVSDK should still support them (until MAVLink removes them entirely).

Now, we may be tempted to wish for a transition: after all, why not letting new servers implement only the new messages, and have MAVSDK detect which message it should use? The problem with that is that MAVLink cannot make a difference between an unsupported command and a command that timed out. It is very common for systems that don't support a command to just ignore it, and it is sometimes designed like this: only one component of the system is meant to know that command and answer to it, and the others just ignore it.

So how do you make MAVSDK detect if the new message is supported? If you send a "dummy" `MAV_CMD_REQUEST_MESSAGE` and get an ACK, then you know that the drone supports this message, but what happens if it times out? Should you assume that the drone does not support it, or should you assume it was an actual time out? How many times should you try again before you can be "reasonably sure" that it is actually not supported? And when you do that for one specific `MAV_CMD_REQUEST_MESSAGE`, it does not say anything about another one, does it?

### Conclusion

In my personal opinion, the only way to move towards the new message is to remove the old one and break all the systems that still use it. This is not a MAVSDK decision but a MAVLink decision. Until then, MAVSDK should use the old way and drones should support both.

I agree with @JonasVautherin and this was my stance about one year ago. I think by now we can start to try using the new MAV_CMD_REQUEST_MESSAGE and fallback to the previous one if it doesn't work. This might lead to suboptimal behavior for systems that don't support it yet but that might be ok in my opinion. The cameras that I'm aware off, except the ones with Yuneec H520, should support the new way.

title: Build in docker as user
author: julianoes
body:
Currently when we build in docker it uses root and therefore leaves build artefacts with root as the owner. This requires `sudo make distclean` to clean up afterwards outside of docker which is inconvenient.

As @hamishwillee suggests we should build something similar to:
https://dev.px4.io/en/test_and_ci/docker.html
https://github.com/PX4/containers/blob/master/docker/px4-dev/Dockerfile_base#L64

answer_comments.body:
Docker ENTRYPOINT with this script seems to work well.
https://github.com/PX4/containers/blob/master/docker/px4-dev/scripts/entrypoint.sh

Dockerfile

    # create and start as LOCAL_USER_ID
    COPY scripts/entrypoint.sh /usr/local/bin/entrypoint.sh
    ENTRYPOINT ["/usr/local/bin/entrypoint.sh"]

When running the container you need to pass - eLOCAL_USER_ID=$UID and it creates an internal user matching your UID. Otherwise it uses UID 9001, which is still better than root.

I am not familiar with UWP apps. Does it have access to the serial port, or is there some kind of permission system?
If it works in a bare CLI app and not with UWP, I would look into that permission system more closely :innocent:

There is a permission system, but I made sure to add serial communication as a capability. It is defined this way:

```
  <Capabilities>
    <Capability Name="internetClient" />

    <DeviceCapability Name="serialcommunication">
      <Device Id="any">
        <Function Type="name:serialPort" />
      </Device>
    </DeviceCapability>
  </Capabilities>
```
If it works in a bare CLI app and not with UWP, I would look into that permission system more closely :innocent:

title: set_acceleration_ned problem along down direction
author: PeymanAmirii
body: When we use set_acceleration_ned(AccelerationNed(0, 0, 0)), the drones descend so fast and do not stay at a point. If we use set_acceleration_ned(AccelerationNed(0, 0, -0.1)), the droens relatively stay at a point. What is the problem?

answer_comments.body:
> now, we want to use the command set_acceleration_ned

Ok, why? What are you trying to solve or improve?

If you command set_velocity_ned(VelocityNed(0, 0, 0)) I expect it to drift in position over time, unless you are closing the loop with a position P controller around it.

In the same way if you command set_acceleration_ned(AccelerationNed(0, 0, 0)) I expect it to drift in velocity over time, unless you are closing the loop with a velocity (and eventually position) controller around it.

I assume it works much better with velocity inputs because you only integrate drift once, so the drift is slow an manageable. If you control acceleration however, you are integrating twice, so acceleration -> velocity -> position, so your drift accumulates much quicker.
It's estimated using the ekf2 estimator. So it contains IMU, GPS, whatever is available.

comments.body:
First of all, trying to understand, what are you trying to do? What is the context?

I would assume that when you control acceleration, you need to "close the loop" outside, so you need to have a controller that controls acceleration based on a velocity or position setpoint that you are trying to reach.

However, this is not trivial, so the question is why you are trying to use the acceleration interface in the first place.

Thanks for your answer. We have used the command set_velocity_ned(VelocityNed(V_north, V_east, V_down)) to send the target velocity obtained based on P controller to get the quadcopter to a set point. After successful experiments, now, we want to use the command set_acceleration_ned(AccelerationNed(A_north, A_east, A_down)) to send the target acceleration obtained based on P controller to get the quadcopter to a set point. 
When we use the command set_velocity_ned(VelocityNed(0, 0, 0)), the quadcopter stays at a point but when we use the cammnd set_acceleration_ned(AccelerationNed(0, 0, 0)), the quadcopter descends. If we use the command set_acceleration_ned(AccelerationNed(0, 0, -0.1)), the quacopter relatively stays at a point.

> now, we want to use the command set_acceleration_ned

Ok, why? What are you trying to solve or improve?

Thanks for your answer. We want to see if a P controller with acceleration command can be more accurate than a P controller with velocity command or not. Is it possible to find out why when we use the command set_acceleration_ned(AccelerationNed(0, 0, 0)), the drones descent (however, they should stay at a point), but when we use the command set_velocity_ned(VelocityNed(0, 0, 0)), they stay at a point?

(We have developed a framework named Helix.io to control mutiple drones using MAVSDK library. The link to framework is:
https://github.com/CUEDOS/helixio)
Thanks.

If you command set_velocity_ned(VelocityNed(0, 0, 0)) I expect it to drift in position over time, unless you are closing the loop with a position P controller around it.

In the same way if you command set_acceleration_ned(AccelerationNed(0, 0, 0)) I expect it to drift in velocity over time, unless you are closing the loop with a velocity (and eventually position) controller around it.

I assume it works much better with velocity inputs because you only integrate drift once, so the drift is slow an manageable. If you control acceleration however, you are integrating twice, so acceleration -> velocity -> position, so your drift accumulates much quicker.

Thanks fo your detailed answer. As the last question, how acceleration is measured in this case? By derivating the position obtained using GPS, twice or using accelerometers of IMU or a fusion of these two methods?
It's estimated using the ekf2 estimator. So it contains IMU, GPS, whatever is available.
I suppose I can close this.

title: Detecting button pressing in real radio command with MAVSDK
author: jonazti07
body:
I'm a new user of MAVLINK and I'm looking for a particular functionality that I'm not sure if it's implemented in MAVSDK (i.e, I haven't seen it in the source code).

I'm trying to detect the actual pressing of a button in the real radio command of my drone.

Is this possible with MAVSDK?

answer_comments.body: Ok, can you give some more context? So, where is MAVSDK used: on the ground or on a companion? In other words, do you want to detect the button pressed on the drone based on what a ground station (or RC) sends? Or do you want a button command to be sent from the ground using MAVSDK?

Ok, and what message is used to send that button? Presumably it's [MANUAL_CONTROL](https://mavlink.io/en/messages/common.html#MANUAL_CONTROL)?

In that case, I wonder if PX4 emits something to signal that a button has been pressed, presumably not, and you have to "intercept" this message in MAVSDK.

Are you using MAVSDK in C++? In that case you can intercept messages manually:
https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/v2.12/src/mavsdk/core/include/mavsdk/mavsdk.h#L408-L420

So what you're saying is that you're not sending MAVLink RC to PX4, so there is no way for MAVSDK to intercept that message. In that case you have to make sure PX4 sends out [RC_CHANNELS](https://mavlink.io/en/messages/common.html#RC_CHANNELS) and than subscribe to this one in MavlinkPassthrough.

title: Mavsdk::remove_connection does not remove system
author: jperez-droneup
body:
I believe there are still some subscriptions on the MAVSDK side for the removed connection. When removing and re-adding a connection, I get multiple printouts of messages (see heartbeat, MAVLink: info:, and Received ack messages in attached log).

It looks like the connection is removed, but the system itself is not. So when we reconnect we get duplicate messages.

At this point, I am not subscribed to anything but `subscribe_is_connected` (which is unsubscribed when a disconnect happens) and `subscribe_on_new_system` (which is unsubscribed when the connection is made). Unsubscribing everything on my end does not fix the multiple messages. For example, the only time I see `_heartbeat_timeout_cookie` ("heartbeats timed out" message) unsubscribed is when the `SystemImpl` is destructed, but `_systems` in `MavskImpl` is only cleared on destruction and I don't see any way to remove the system after removing the connection.

I found that the system id of my first system is changed to 1 in [this line](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/ed7ac0777f97a84531c1790cbbc2b0de0438225b/src/mavsdk/core/mavsdk_impl.cpp#L356). However, subsequent connections (after disconnect of initial one and removal of connection) create systems with ID zero and are not changed to 1 because the systems list is not empty. Seems like we need to properly remove the systems - and all internal subscriptions to them - in order for it to properly remove and add a new remote system and have it work correctly.

answer_comments.body: @jperez-droneup would you mind testing https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/pull/2081? It should avoid creating yet another null system whenever you add a connection using setup_udp_remote.

title: Disable automatically re-sending setpoints in offboard
author: hugh-cover-ms
body:
Is there a way to disable the MAVSDK offboard class from automatically re-sending setpoints?

It seems that this is done to bypass the fact that Px4 needs off-board setpoints to be minimally sent at 2Hz, however there is a good reason Px4 does that. 
The current behaviour of MAVSDK can leave the drone mindlessly following the last setpoint if there is an unexpected fault on the companion computer. This is particularly a problem with velocity setpoints.

I guess I could modify the value of SEND_INTERVAL_S, but that seems like a less than optimal solution.

title: Log file download resume after a partial download?
author: flybratten04
body:
Julian/Gents:
 I don't know if the community is interested in such a capability as it is sort of a unique situation. Our drones have an associated Raspberry Pi, so when powered but not armed, we download the log files from Ardupilot to the Pi over a serial port (implied relatively slow). Our log files can grow to 200MB or so, hence it is quite possible for an operator to power down while a download is in progress, hence leaving a partial file.
 I modified (hopefully not a hack) the logfile plugin to support a resume of downloading from where the partial download ended. From the initial tests the code appears robust, but this is only against a simulator and not field tests.
 If there is interest I would certainly share the approach and the code with the community where it could reviewed potentially improved. 

Cheers,

answer_comments.body:
I'd be ok merging this if it doesn't introduce too much complexity or other problems.

That being said, I think we should probably move to the MAVLink FTP protocol instead of using the clunky log files messages, because that one features CRC checks and partial downloads out of the box. We could even implement MAVSDK to support resuming downloading a file with FTP.

Not sure why it would be slow with FTP. It shouldn't be in general, and even supports burst mode to speed it up.

It would be worth investigating that.
I'm closing this issue but I would say let's try with FTP as we're likely moving to that, not just with MAVSDK. For a broader discussion, see: https://github.com/mavlink/mavlink-devguide/pull/668

title: operator<< for MavlinkPassthrough::Result missing MAVSDK_PUBLIC
author: dunnman
body:
Title pretty much says it. Hit a linker error trying to stream a MavlinkPassthrough::Result to std::cout. Looks like the operator<< overload in the passthrough header is missing the MAVSDK_PUBLIC specifier that the equivalent MavlinkDirect one has, so the symbol doesn’t get exported.

In mavlink_passthrough.hpp (line 94):
`friend std::ostream& operator<<(std::ostream& str, MavlinkPassthrough::Result const& result);`

In mavlink_direct.hpp (line 126):
`friend MAVSDK_PUBLIC std::ostream& operator<<(std::ostream& str, MavlinkDirect::Result const& result);`

Adding MAVSDK_PUBLIC to the passthrough declaration should fix it I would think.
Building latest main on Rocky 8 using g++ 8.5.0

linked_prs.title: fix(mavlink_passthrough): export operator<< for Result with MAVSDK_PUBLIC

comments.body: good catch — just a missing visibility macro, opened #2881 mirroring how MavlinkDirect declares the same operator

In fact, if you say you don't support Mojave, then that's less work for me :)
Ok! Let's "drop" support for Mojave, then! Thanks a lot for reporting!

As it turns out, all that was needed was to build MAVSDK with a newer toolchain than the one provided by the system. (Though I guess that shouldn't be surprising.)

Just thought to let you know in case it's useful elsewhere (or for whomever else stumbles upon this issue).

title: How to change PWM output signal?
author: maitham
body: I'm trying to change the PWM output using dronecode sdk. I don't need to run a mission or anything, I want to do a static test where I can simply change values. I seem to be running out of options in terms of simply changing pwm outputs within a script in a reliable manner (NSH pwm test works but only for main out). Is there anyway of currently doing this?

answer_comments.body:
I don't think this is possible with the SDK because there is AFAIK no API to support it AND this won't necessarily be supported by default in PX4. 

Without having tried this  (i.e. maybe not correct) .... to make it work in PX4 you'd have to look at adding a mixer file to map control inputs to outputs - http://dev.px4.io/en/concept/mixing.html
To drive it you would need to send the appropriate MAVLink message (or have an onboard app that does the work for you).

PS The people who might help with this are possibly at Interdrone. 

@bkueng Can you comment about PX4 support? As I understand it the mixer is what defines what comes out of the MAIN/AUX outputs - for certain inputs (control group UORB topics?). Does the mapping between MAVLink and those UORB topics exist - ie if you create a mixer and send the appropriate MAVLink message will this work?

@maitham1 this will need some work for the SDK.

In the meantime, if `pwm test` works, you should try to make `pwm test` work for the aux output as well. Note that there is a `-d` argument which should enable you to choose the device, e.g. `/dev/pwm_output0` or `/dev/pwm_output1`.

https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/68c8041bc911e31f99c8575a042d6b3919583b39/src/mavsdk/plugins/action/include/plugins/action/action.h#L447-L456

title: FTP Server file descriptor leak
author: Zhumos
body:
**Version**: 1.4.16 as well as main

The FTP Server currently leaks a file descriptor every time MavlinkFtp::_work_list is called as it does not call closedir() on the descriptor used.

If there is a system limit for file descriptors, the server will eventually start failing to open any further descriptors. This was confirmed by watching "/proc/<pid>/fd" and observing errors when 1024 descriptors was reached.

This issue causes failures such as when requesting a directory listing, the client reports "Ftp::Result::ProtocolError" with the server reporting "OPC:CMD_OPEN_FILE_RO" followed by "FTP: Open failed"

Line where descriptor is allocated:
https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/fadfe22e7c053945107201e2638be9a7f8b8ee5c/src/mavsdk/core/mavlink_ftp.cpp#L989

comments.body: Fixed, thanks @Zhumos!

title: Including the sdk via FetchContent to the project errors on build
author: tlapik123
body:
When I try to include the library to my project using FetchContent it errors when building.

The error: 
```
[build] <path>/build/_deps/mavsdk-build/src/mavsdk/core/include/mavsdk/mavlink_include.h:3:10:  fatal error: mavlink/v2.0/common/mavlink.h: No such file or directory
[build]     3 | #include "mavlink/v2.0/common/mavlink.h"
[build]       |          ^~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
[build] compilation terminated.
```
I looked into the code and it seems that only that the install target would work correctly, but I don't want to install I just want to build it and use it :sweat_smile:  

Is there something that I'm doing wrong? Is there some option to set?
Thank you for your time.

answer_comments.body:
This will soon change actually: https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/pull/2028

title: Support MissionItems for LAND, TAKEOFF
author: hamishwillee
body:
We need [MissionItem](https://docs.dronecore.io/v/develop/en/api_reference/classdronecore_1_1_mission_item.html) functionality for takeoff and landing. These items should attempt to properly support common options for MC, Plane and VTOL (where they differ). Specifically I would hope that we could have a single land and single takeoff item to support all of these:
https://mavlink.io/en/messages/common.html#MAV_CMD_NAV_LAND
https://mavlink.io/en/messages/common.html#MAV_CMD_NAV_TAKEOFF
https://mavlink.io/en/messages/common.html#MAV_CMD_NAV_LAND_LOCAL
https://mavlink.io/en/messages/common.html#MAV_CMD_NAV_TAKEOFF_LOCAL
https://mavlink.io/en/messages/common.html#MAV_CMD_NAV_VTOL_LAND
https://mavlink.io/en/messages/common.html#MAV_CMD_NAV_VTOL_TAKEOFF

Once these exist they also need to be supported in the mission import and download from vehicle and added to tests.

There was some discussion originally that these are not needed because 
* MC automatically takes off if no takeoff is present
* Action API supports these functions.

They are needed because:
* MC automatic takeoff does not allow you to specify any takeoff behaviour
* Plane and VTOL do not automatically takeoff if no takeoff item is present
* QC plan import and download from vehicle can end up being different in round trip.

To me this just makes sense.

title: Improving logging
author: shakthi-prashanth-m
body:
Right now, we're logging DroneCore logs on console. Generally its a practice to dump all the debug logs to a file. We could save them onto say, `build/default/logs/dronecore.log`.

Then, a user may simply run on a terminal:
```tail -f build/default/logs/dronecore.log```

So, we can add **more debug/info logs** in the code (as it won't collide with application console logs) which are really helpful to analyze issues. For ex: say, arming/takeoff fails. We can easy look into logs to see whether **all the necessary things went well** or not.

PS: _As discussed in Slack, we're planning to add this in future (not right now)._

title: Name change proposal for "Device" class to "Drone" or "Vehicle"
author: shakthi-prashanth-m
body:
This is regarding name change proposal of the class `Device`, `DeviceImpl`, etc.
We've named the library & API after **drone**, as in **DroneCore**, it makes sense to name its core service class to be `class Drone`, or at least `class Vehicle` (in QGroundControl) rather than `class Device`.

Cons of having `Device` name is that it is likely to be used for Ground Control Station, Mobile device also.
In other words, GCS is a device as well;
When we say `Vehicle`, there is no room of confusion whether it is Drone or Ground Control Station.

If DroneCore is also intended for general Robotics application, then probably `Device` might sound good.
Kindly share your thoughts, opinions.

Thanks.

answer_comments.body:
Looking at your logs above, one time you run it with `./start-mavsdk-server.sh`, which apparently runs something like `./mavsdk_server udp://:14551`. The other time, you run something like `./mavsdk_server`, which is equivalent to `./mavsdk_server udp://:14540`.

Therefore the second instance does not discover your drone because apparently your drone sends mavlink on udp 14551.

Run this instead:

```
./mavsdk_server_linux-arm64-musl udp://:14551
```

title: Difference between CompanionComputer and  GroundStation
author: ZhongmouLi
body:
Hi guys,

I am using mavsdk v3. Could you please help me understand the difference between `Mavsdk mavsdk{Mavsdk::Configuration{ComponentType::GroundStation}};` and `Mavsdk::Configuration{ComponentType::CompanionComputer};`?

In the examples given, I found `CompanionComputer` is only used by `mavlink_direct` while `GroundStation` is used by the other examples. But I cannot tell their differences between using them.

answer_comments.body:
It will be recognised differently by the autopilot (e.g. your program will have a different MAVLink system_id and component_id).

Say your drone is configured to refuse to takeoff if no ground station is connected and your MAVSDK program enumerates as a companion computer, then the drone will refuse to takeoff. If MAVSDK says it is a ground station, then the drone will takeoff.

You probably don't want to enumerate as a ground station if you actually run onboard the drone, because then the failsafe won't work properly. Same if you run your MAVSDK code on the ground, you probably want to enumerate as a ground station so that the drone knows that it is connected to "something in the outside".

Does that help?

title: Expose io_context for external event loop integration
author: bansiesta
body:
## Problem

Currently MAVSDK always owns its `asio::io_context` and runs it on an internal `_io_thread`. There is no way for an application that already runs its own Asio event loop (e.g. a drone autopilot written with Asio, or a ROS2 node using its own executor) to share the io_context with MAVSDK.

## Proposed solution

Add a `Mavsdk` constructor overload that accepts an `asio::io_context&`:

\`\`\`cpp
Mavsdk(Configuration configuration, asio::io_context& external_io_context);
\`\`\`

When constructed this way:
- MAVSDK does not start `_io_thread`
- The caller is responsible for calling `io_context.run()` (or integrating it into their event loop via `poll()` / `run_one()` etc.)
- All other behaviour is identical

## Design considerations

- Exposing `asio::io_context` in `mavsdk.h` means Asio becomes part of the public API. We may need a forward-declared wrapper or an `any_io_executor` variant to keep the public header clean.
- An alternative: expose a `run_once()` / `poll()` method that lets callers drive the event loop without exposing the type directly — but this is less idiomatic for Asio users.
- Related: `set_callback_executor()` already lets users redirect _callbacks_ to their own thread. This issue is about integrating the _I/O loop_ itself.

## Context

This came up after #2810 which migrated all internal I/O to a single Asio io_context. That PR is a prerequisite for this feature.

answer_comments.body: @bansiesta Does `set_callback_executor` still work with the new Asio rework? If so, there is no issue.

Yes, `set_callback_executor` works exactly as before after #2810. The Asio rework didn't touch the callback dispatch path at all — all user-facing callbacks still go through `_user_callback_queue` / `_callback_executor`, fully independent of the io_context thread.

So for the common integration case — "I have my own event loop and want MAVSDK callbacks delivered there" — `set_callback_executor` is still the right tool and it works.

The original issue is about a more advanced case: sharing the actual `io_context` so that MAVSDK's I/O participates in an existing Asio application without spawning an extra thread. That's a valid future enhancement but it's not needed for basic event loop integration. Closing this for now; can reopen if the shared io_context use-case becomes a concrete requirement.

title: attitude_euler_angle() returns "NaN" for Pixhawk 2.1 Cube
author: loganriggs
body:
### Using Raspberry Pi 3 B+

- If running with the Pixhawk 2.1 cube (with motors, gps, lidar, flow, etc powered) , attitude_euler_angle().yaw_deg returns "NaN". (Also returns "NaN" for roll, pitch, and quaternion values)
- If running the sitl simulation, attitude_euler_angle().yaw_deg returns the correct attitude

### Using Linux Ubuntu 16.04.3
- If running with the Pixhawk 2.1 cube (Just connected straight to the Cube, no peripherals are powered), attitude_euler_angle() also returns the correct attitude.
- If running the simulation, attitude_euler_angle() returns the correct attitude.

### Possible Leads
1. I have a video of receiving the correct attitude from mid-May. The major difference there is the v1.8.0 Firmware update released June 19th. At the time of the video, it was (most likely) running v1.7.3 released Jan. 6th. I was having trouble reverting back to that firmware to check, so I haven't tested that yet.
2. Telemetry().longitude/latitude/velocity also are null on the Pixhawk 2.1 cube if the gps isn't locked (flashing green). This makes sense, so there might be a different hardware component that affects attitude like the gps affects the above values.

title: Plugins should not try resending on disconnected devices
author: hamishwillee
body:
For example, if you disconnect the device but then try landing, the plugin will still try to send the message, and to resend it. 
```A
Altitude: 2.679 m
Disconnected device with UUID: 4294967298
Landing...
sending again, retries to do: 3  (21).
sending again, retries to do: 2  (21).
sending again, retries to do: 1  (21).
Retrying failed (21)
Land failed:Timeout
```
I am not sure what the correct behaviour should be, but certainly it is not a resend. Ideally the user should be notified of this when they try to make the method call - typically there is a device disconnected "Results".

title: CPU load too high when downloading logs
author: Katawann
body:
Hello !

**Description**
I download automatically the missing logs from the PX4 to my companion computer (RPi) thanks to the [LogFiles](https://mavsdk.mavlink.io/main/en/cpp/api_reference/classmavsdk_1_1_log_files.html) plugin.

**Issue**
When I'm downloading a log and I try to arm, I get the error below. You can see this behavior on [this flight review](https://logs.px4.io/plot_app?log=8180f6b3-fbfb-4a3d-9173-5101d76bfe73).
`Warning: [PreFlightCheck] Fail: CPU load too high: 98.1%`

**Context**
Pixhawk 4 with San Disk U3 32GB (same behavior with Pixhawk 5x)
Raspberry Pi 3B+ (connected with USB to the pixhawk)
PX4 v1.12.3
MAVSDK v0.48.0

**Question**
Is it possible to interrupt the [download_log_file_async](https://mavsdk.mavlink.io/main/en/cpp/api_reference/classmavsdk_1_1_log_files.html#classmavsdk_1_1_log_files_1a48712c031e204b23e00cfa28a0b1bc01) function ? Otherwise is it possible to set a parameters to reduce the ressources used by the download to avoid this kind of situation ?


Thank you in advance for your suggestion !

answer_comments.body:
I think that this is somewhat likely or expected. You could try to use Mavlink FTP as an alternative but it might have the same issue.

The logfile download implementation on PX4 is made in order to maximize the rate and serve the file as fast as possible, usually using the USB 1 interface. You could try to debug that by running `top` in the PX4 console and check just how much CPU is used by mavlink. From the log it looks like your base CPU usage is already at 80%, so then logfile download pushes it do 100%.

![bokeh_plot](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1419688/143534984-11e8f3ae-fbb8-4655-b207-6d84c0ed01d1.png)

I don't have a good suggestion except not downloading logfiles while trying to fly, or dive in the PX4 code (or MAVSDK code?) to artificially slow it down.

comments.body: Can you give some context of what you're trying to do overall without the implementation specifics?

Well, I want to implement a server that is awaiting the connections of drones, an unknown number of drones. This server is listening on one port. The main function of the server is to give orders like go to the point (x, y) or follow a predefined route and meanwhile, the drones will transfer images or videos to another server that will process all the data. This second server's IP address and Port information is passed to the drone when it connects to the first server. 

To sum up, there will be two servers, one that only gives orders and missions to the drones and check their states. And another that will process the photos.

2. Once a drone is connected, you would reconfigure it to another port using some sort of mechanism that you have to implement

It would basically be some sort of discovery mechanism on UDP.

The backend currently implements a subset of all the actions as defined [here](https://github.com/dronecore/DroneCore-Proto/blob/master/action/action.proto). Note that this issue can be split in multiple, smaller PRs. Using "Connects to #315." on the description of the PR will connect it to this issue on the [kanban board](https://waffle.io/dronecore/DroneCore) without closing this issue.

The following actions need to be implemented:

- [ ] Disarm

- [ ] Kill

I got a request to expose the `serial_number` of [SMART_BATTERY_INFO](https://mavlink.io/en/messages/common.html#SMART_BATTERY_INFO).

From the specs, I read:

> Smart Battery information (static/infrequent update). Use for updates from: smart battery to flight stack, flight stack to GCS. Use [BATTERY_STATUS](https://mavlink.io/en/messages/common.html#BATTERY_STATUS) for smart battery frequent updates.

Should I try to integrate that to the normal `Battery` updates of MAVSDK (I guess setting `serial_number=""` for non-smart batteries), or should it go in a specific `SmartBattery` type that comes with another subscription?

@hamishwillee @julianoes I wanted to ask for your opinion on that :slightly_smiling_face:.

Related to https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK-Proto/pull/290

title: We should be able to track connection status of Device objects other than by callback
author: hamishwillee
body: The suggestion is that it should be possible to detect whether Device is connected from the object itself. This would allow a client to iterate the vector of devices and only handle those that are connected - without having to separately manage tracking connection/and disconnection.

answer_comments.body:
OK, though for completeness ... this was not quite what was delivered. We now have a top level DroneCore mechanism that can check if a particular UUID is connected. What this originally asked for is a mechanism for a device to check itself for a connected state. 

The semantics are slightly different but I am not sure if what has been done is better or not. Really depends on whether you'd write code where you have a device and check its connection status before "doing stuff" or you would instead manage all connection/disconnection at a single top level location. My object orientation head makes me think that we might well want device-centric behaviour, but not sure how realistic that is.

author: hamishwillee
body: For arming, landing, flight mode etc it is likely that you will only want to get callbacks notified when the values change. The suggestion is to allow clients of the API to specify whether notification should happen on every message, or just when the value changes.
resolution_evidence: closed by maintainer, no clear resolution marker

comments.body: I feel like leaving this to the user would complicate the API quite a bit. Also no one has asked for this in 8 years, so I'm closing.

title: Need to be able to set the System ID of Dronecore itself

title: Support multiple batteries
author: JonasVautherin
body: As discussed [in this thread](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK-Swift/issues/189#issuecomment-802221631), I think that `telemetry.battery()` should expose a list of batteries (instead of only one). In the usual case with one battery, that would be a list of length one. Also, MAVSDK should use BATTERY_STATUS if it is advertised, but fallback to SYS_STATUS if it is not.

title: Support ArduPilot REMOTE_LOG_DATA protocol
author: julianoes
body: MAVSDK currently only supports log streaming from PX4 using [LOGGING_DATA](https://mavlink.io/en/messages/common.html#LOGGING_DATA). However, ArduPilot uses different messages called [REMOTE_LOG_DATA_BLOCK](https://mavlink.io/en/messages/ardupilotmega.html#REMOTE_LOG_DATA_BLOCK) (in the ardupilotmega.xml dialect).

title: Position mode takeoff goes into altitude hold on ArduPilot
author: julianoes
body:
There seems to be an issue where taking off in ArduPilot doesn't use position hold but instead only altitude control.

In general, we should revisit how to do a safe take off with ArduPilot. Some flight modes require throttle to be held down (altitude and position hold), while arming in loiter isn't possible like in PX4.

Also, presumably auto mode automatically arms with ArduPilot? Worth checking.
